Motivation
DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on Hopper spends substantial decode time in group32 dense GEMMs, capacity-sized indexer work, mHC statistics, and padded Marlin MoE projections. This PR tunes those paths. On Blackwell, flattened prefill selection also launches separate mask, sort, slot-map and raw-offset operations; the added integer kernel combines them.
Changes
Tune Hopper group32 GEMMs and reuse exact BF16 expansions of eligible FP8 weights, preserving activation quantization boundaries and the original fallbacks.
Use live paged indexer lengths and variable-length top-k; fuse masking, sorting and slot mapping.
Enable guarded Hopper mHC combine/norm and compensated BF16 projection paths, with decode statistics overlap.
Preserve intermediate activation rounding in fused clipped SwiGLU; defer MXFP4 padding until Marlin repacking.
On SM100-family CUDA GPUs, fuse flattened prefill selection into one integer kernel. Keep the changing visible slot count as a non-specialized runtime argument, so new context lengths do not create new JIT variants. Hopper retains its existing Torch selection path.

GB300 accuracy uses2048 prefill budgets, because upstream main's FlashMLA scheduling metadata exceeds its48KB shared-memory implementation limit on a GSM8K batch at the default16K budget. Performance comparisons use the same16K budget on every arm and are kept separate. AIME24 candidate versus ordinary PR changes by−0.625 percentage points; truncations40→42,14 correct→wrong and11 wrong→correct. There is also one additional wrong nontruncated answer. The higher-cap paired run still has AIME24 −0.625 percentage points (456→453 correct; truncations22→24;7 correct→wrong,4 reverse), and GSM8K −0.1516 percentage points (1279→1277; neither arm truncated). These scores do not prove identical generation or statistical accuracy equivalence.
Correctness coverage
Existing H200 focused regression:582 passed,60 skipped,16 subtests passed on the rebased runtime.
New integer selection/CUDA Graph/cache-reuse cases:34 passed on real GB300 SM100 dispatch, and34 passed on H200 with the SM100 entry mocked to exercise the integer helper.
Full GB300 indexer test file:133 passed,2 skipped.
Real-model8K/32K prefill audit at concurrency1/16:1908 calls across four ranks, with both page and raw indices exactly equal to the original Torch operations. Rows1–16384, visible slots1–48900. This is integer-mapping evidence, not a substitute for generation-quality evaluation.
A second actual-model audit dispatches fusion before any reference GPU work:1908 calls,477 per rank, with exact page/raw index agreement. Padding is separately covered by the unit tests.
Actual model GPU traces contain40
_finish_flat_indexer_topk_kernel
events per rank; all four original trace files are retained with source hashes.
Pinned pre-commit and diff whitespace checks passed. CI is not fully green: the existing AMD raw-draft-metadata test still needs alignment with main's deferred metadata API; no ROCm validation is claimed.
Memory and weight updates
The Hopper derived caches trade GPU memory for throughput. In the original weight-load measurement, memory increased72.71→75.43GB/GPU and max_total_num_tokens fell16,012,800→14,223,104 at the same static memory fraction. These are the original configuration's measurements, not newly measured final-commit memory numbers.
Online weight updates require disabling both derived caches with
SGLANG_OPT_HOPPER_BLOCK_FP8_BF16=0
and
SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_HC_PRENORM=0
; otherwise updates fail before writing weights. Other TP/EP layouts are not covered by the reported serving comparisons.

Motivation
Enable candidate-only indexer scoring on SM90 for DeepSeek-V4.1, following
#40574
.
The current protocol already publishes compact candidate block IDs, but Hopper consumers still traverse the full logical score space before selecting among the candidates. This PR uses those block IDs during scoring, so consumers produce compact scores directly instead of a context-width score matrix.
The Triton implementation reads candidate K positions directly, avoiding a per-query
[queries, candidates, head_dim]
K tensor.
Modifications
Reuse the existing
DenseBlocksBackend
,
BlockIds
, and
publish_*
/
consume_*
interfaces.
Prefill:
score candidate positions directly from shared BF16 index K with Triton. Per-request K retrieval/dequantization remains unchanged; no per-query candidate K tensor is materialized. Retain the independent Torch reference and fallback for unsupported shapes.
Decode/verify:
add
fp4_index_logits_candidates
, reusing the upstream FP4 scoring tile. Address candidate K through the request-to-token table without constructing a context-sized slot map or candidate mask for compact consumers.
Selection:
keep scores compact through ragged/paged Top-K v2. Reuse
finish_paged_indexer_topk
for compact-to-logical mapping, invalid-position filtering, sorting, and output mapping. Preserve causal bounds, padding, and prefill tail slicing.
CUDA graphs:
enable the existing length-based variants on SM90: four for ordinary decode and two for DSPARK target verify.
Preserve upstream source-layer scoring, the FullTopK DeepSelect path, 128B paged-score row alignment, and conditional Top-K v2 plan generation. SM100 backend selection remains unchanged.

Thanks for preparing these follow-up patches!
For
775ab53
, the CandidateIndexer prefill interface explicitly permits unordered output, and _low_ratio_index_topk_torch already sorts valid positions ahead of padding before mapping them to KV slots. Adding another sort in _write_topk appears redundant for the current path, so I’d prefer not to cherry-pick this commit as-is. If you have a failing case that exposes a gap in the existing handling, I’d be happy to take a closer look.
For

Motivation
PR
#41364
adds
topk_page_transform
, which combines DeepSelect Top-K selection with the page-table transform in its epilogue.
DeepSeek V4.1 on Hopper still uses:
torch.topk
  -> sort raw indices
  -> gather physical KV slots
This PR connects the new DeepSelect operator to that runtime path.
Modifications
Use
topk_page_transform
for the SM90 full-topk decode path.
Write transformed int32 KV slots directly into the existing output buffer.
Preserve raw-index ordering with
sorted_index=True
.
Keep the existing Torch path when raw indices are also required.
Keep SM100 and newer architectures on the existing DeepGEMM path.
Add CPU dispatch/fallback tests and an H20 runtime integration test.
Accuracy Tests
Validated on NVIDIA H20:
Test
Result

10/10 passed
Related indexer unit tests
28/28 passed
New runtime integration tests
5/5 passed

statement coverage
90%
Coverage includes short contexts where
width < topk
, variable row lengths, page-table mapping, sorted output, and the raw-index fallback.
Speed Tests and Profiling
The replaced region was benchmarked on NVIDIA H20 with CUDA 13.0 and PyTorch 2.13. Each complete run used 20 warmup iterations followed by 5 groups of 100 measurements. The table reports the mean of the medians from two complete runs.
The measured regions were:
Before:
torch.topk -> raw-index sort -> slot gather -> output copy

After:
DeepSelect top-k -> sorted-index epilogue -> page-table transform

(DeepSeek-V4.1 prefill optimizations, split into smaller PRs).
Motivation
The low-ratio (ratio 1/2) prefill indexer ran many small kernels per layer, sorted and remapped its selection before attention, had a schedule that is quadratic in a request's rows, and synchronized with the host several times per step.
Modifications
Fused index-Q kernel in the prefill indexer
: prefill query and head-weight prep goes through
index_q_rope_pack_weights
(
_index_q_and_weights
), shared with decode.
Prefill top-k written straight into the raw selection
: the DeepGEMM prefill top-k emits request-local compressed positions directly into the buffer sparse prefill reads. Pool slots (
page_indices
) are only derived when this forward's attention reads them (trtllm, non-sparse extend, sm120, late-layer tail, request window, or
SGLANG_OPT_FLASHMLA_SPARSE_PREFILL
off).
Selection
is removed; the output buffers are fields of
PrefillInputs
/
DecodeInputs
/
CapturedPrefillInputs
.
write_selection
keeps only the CP dense-blocks path and no longer sorts.
Row-pair request ids for the paged sparse indexer schedule
: DeepGEMM's paged sparse-logits metadata walks back over equal request ids once per row. Ids unique per consecutive row pair of a request (never spanning two requests) bound the walk to one step; logits are unchanged.
No host syncs in the prefill forward
:
get_deep_gemm_prefill_data
builds the flattened-K layout for the whole batch from host lengths instead of a per-request loop indexing with device scalars.
New
async_h2d
in
srt/utils/common.py
(pinned, non-blocking; the counterpart of
async_d2h
), used for the request starts, row-pair ids, CP rows, tail rows, and the engram history.
Engram's
repeat_interleave
takes
output_size
from
extend_seq_lens_cpu
.
No
record_stream
on the mHC stats input
: the stats kernels read the residual on the side stream, and every consumer joins that stream on the main stream while the residual is still referenced, so
record_stream
only delayed the reuse of each freed residual. Without the host syncs the host runs further ahead, and those delayed frees piled up to several full residuals and exhausted the allocator.
Tests
:
test_dense_prefill_indexer.py
and

follow the new interfaces.

What
Two fused paths for DeepSeek-V4.1, plus the MoE finalize plumbing they expose:
mHC sequence-parallel boundary
(
SGLANG_OPT_DSV41_MHC_SP_FUSION
, opt-in): inside the sharded region each sublayer boundary becomes one collective launch — reduce-scatter of the partial sublayer output, hc post + next combine + RMSNorm on this rank's rows, all-gather of the normalized next input — with the mixing statistics produced by dedicated CTAs of the same launch (NVLS from three peers up, peer load/store at two ranks). With decoder SWA bounded replay the SP region ends at the tail boundary instead of excluding SP outright.
Engram
: the hash tables shard on hash-column boundaries in symmetric memory, and the lookup defaults to an in-place gather straight into
wkv
's MXFP8 operand — no all-reduce, no dequant/requant round trip (a bf16-dequantizing gather covers
wkv
configurations without an MXFP8 input path, exactly; the shared host table is read the same way). The gate + residual update + the next boundary's combine/norm fuse into one seam kernel with SP / DP / TP variants (
SGLANG_OPT_DSV41_ENGRAM_TP_FUSION_MIN_TOKENS
gates the TP variant; the image-token mask rides the kernel as a per-row skip). CUDA only; ROCm and other platforms keep the existing paths.
MoE
: a raw
MoEOutput
's finalize now defers whenever the producer supports it and lands as one fused finalize + shared-add kernel writing the caller's buffer;
get_merged
honors
out=
on the unfused arm too, fixing a path where the sequence-parallel boundary read an unwritten buffer.
Accuracy
Kernel level: the direct gathers are bitwise-identical to the dequantizing reference (including e8m0 zero scales and fp8 denormal payloads) on both sm90 and sm100; the DP and SP seam variants are bitwise-identical to each other across row counts, ragged splits and skip masks, including NaN/Inf injection into masked rows; 200 back-to-back SP launches show stable semaphore rotation.
End to end (TP4/EP4, gsm8k 1319 questions, greedy): fused SP 0.9014 vs unfused 0.9113, McNemar p = 0.198 (not significant). A same-configuration rerun control scores 0.9113 / 0.9113 with only 36% exact-text agreement, i.e. the engine is not run-to-run stable at temperature 0 on this backend (as the cookbook documents), and the fused path's long-prompt logprob drift sits within that noise floor. TP-mode fusion scores 0.9052; TP2 (host table) 0.8954, all within the observed jitter band.
The seam consumes the previous boundary's lagged
pre
, so the fused math matches the unfused operator order; equivalence rather than bitwise identity is expected against the old path (the gate's sigmoid was already approximate there).
Notes
TP2 cannot hold the device tables beside the weights; the host table is the deployable form there (cookbook updated, along with the gather semantics).
Online weight updates remain rejected while derived hc weight splits are active; the probe follows the renamed stacked tensors.

One launch per sublayer boundary under a row-sharded residual: reduce-scatter of the partial sublayer output, hc post + next combine + RMSNorm on this rank's rows, all-gather of the normalized next input, with the mixing statistics produced by dedicated CTAs of the same launch. Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
[DeepSeek-V4.1] mHC sequence-parallel runtime region and symmetric-me…
…
fca7b54
…mory workspace [2/7]

The sp_mhc_rows forward flag scopes the sharded region; shard/gather helpers mirror the kernel's ragged row split; symmetric allocations go through the caching allocator's symmetric pool. Opt-in via SGLANG_OPT_DSV41_MHC_SP_FUSION with a min-token threshold.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
[DeepSeek-V4.1] Engram fusion kernels: direct table gather and the ga…
…
f6b854a
…te + combine seam [3/7]

gather_mxfp8 copies table rows verbatim into wkv's MXFP8 operand (gather_bf16 dequantizes exactly where wkv takes no MXFP8 input); the seam kernels run gate + residual update + the next boundary's combine / norm in one launch, as SP (all-gathering x over the pull plane), DP (purely local) and TP (staging exchange) variants, with an optional per-row skip mask for image tokens.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
[DeepSeek-V4.1] Engram: symmetric table shards, direct gather by defa…
…
c14e748
…ult, fused-seam entry [4/7]

Device tables allocate in the symmetric pool (every rank the widest ragged shard) and exchange addresses at finish_load; the lookup defaults to the in-place gather wherever capable -- shards over NVLink, or the shared host copy as a world of one -- removing the zero-fill + all-reduce + dequant/requant round trip. get_fusion_plan picks the seam mode (SP mandatory under the sharded boundary, DP for tp1 / DP attention, TP over a threshold); the image mask rides the kernel as a per-row skip.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
[DeepSeek-V4.1] Model dispatch: sharded boundaries, fused Engram seam…
…
ff9a021
…, SP exit at the SWA tail [5/7]

Boundaries run the fused SP collective inside the sharded region; the Engram call site consumes the seam's HcNormed next input; with decoder SWA bounded replay the SP region now ends at the tail boundary (gather, then dense tail) instead of excluding SP outright; hc weight splits unify on stacked tensors.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
[DeepSeek-V4.1] MoE: defer finalize for raw outputs and write merges …
…
8059619
…into caller buffers [6/7]

A raw MoEOutput's finalize runs locally at any m, so defer it whenever the producer can (mxfp4 trtllm, and fp8-block trtllm with bypassed TopK) and fold the shared add into one kernel that writes the caller's buffer; get_merged now honors out= on the unfused arm too, which previously left the sequence-parallel boundary reading an unwritten buffer.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
[DeepSeek-V4.1] cookbook: the Engram tables are gathered in place now…
…
c81abac
… [7/7]

The device shards cost no all-reduce on CUDA, the shared host copy is read by the same direct gather, per_rank keeps the legacy lookup, and TP2 must use the host table.

title: [Bug] humming MoE runner picks tuning config with a 4x-inflated shape under EP, and the obvious EP-aware fix regresses serving · Issue #40417 · sgl-project/sglang · GitHub
body:
[Bug] humming MoE runner picks tuning config with a 4x-inflated shape under EP, and the obvious EP-aware fix regresses serving
#40417
New issue
Copy link
New issue
Copy link
Open
Open
[Bug] humming MoE runner picks tuning config with a 4x-inflated shape under EP, and the obvious EP-aware fix regresses serving
#40417
Copy link
Description
Leoyzen
opened
on Sep 20, 2026
Issue body actions
Describe the bug
estimate_local_valid_shape_m()
in
python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/humming.py
returns
topk_ids.nelement()
when no
expected_m
is given (~line 204, carries
# TODO: update for EP and DP
, introduced in
#23754
).
Under EP this counts the global routed elements.
local_expert_mapping
keeps the tensor shape unchanged and writes -1 for non-local experts, so
nelement()
= M_global x top_k, while each rank's GEMM only touches ~1/ep_size of those rows.
The value only drives kernel config selection: the Python block-size ladder in
_prepare_indexed_gemm_kwargs
and the humming launcher's variant lookup (
find_kernel_launch_data
in launcher.cpp). Correctness is unaffected, the launcher validates against real tensor shapes. So under EP every humming MoE GEMM picks its config for a workload ~4x larger than what the rank actually computes (EP4).
We tried the obvious fix, a graph-safe host estimate
max(1, M * top_k / ep_size)
(exact counting needs a D2H sync, illegal under CUDA graph capture). It moves every working point to the true local shape and passes unit tests, but serving regressed:
arm
decode tok/s/req
vs parent
parent (current code)
52.2
-
EP-aware estimate
49.5
-5.1% (perm p=0.003, n=10/arm)
EP-aware + ladder bands recalibrated from per-point kernel microbench
-
-4.0% e2e (C48 median, 3-arm check)
Setup: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (384 routed experts, top_k 6, MXFP4 experts), TP4/EP4, 4x H200-class GPUs, DSPark speculative decoding, random workload at 32-48 concurrency, unique-seed A/B protocol with flush_cache between rounds, cross-session reproducible.
Per-cubin enumeration against the deployed heuristic ladder explains why. The ladder bands were calibrated against the global-element scale, and the two gemm types disagree about what the input even means:
indexed, routed rows ~750-2100: the local-rows input picks kernels 22-26% faster than the global-scale input
grouped, same points: opposite direction, the global-scale input wins by 8-12%
small decode CUDA-graph tiers (<200 rows): both land in the same band, zero effect
re-mapping ladder bands empirically flipped kernel rankings once real routing skew and CUDA-graph replay entered the picture
A single scalar cannot carry both total routed rows and per-expert density once num_local_experts != num_experts. For reference, the masked/DeepEP-LL path already uses
expected_m * num_local_experts
, and DeepEP-normal dispatch carries exact host-side
num_recv_tokens_per_expert
.
Reproduction
Any EP>1 run with
--moe-runner-backend humming
(default gemm type indexed). The wrong value is observable without serving, it is just
topk_ids.nelement()
under EP:
# decode bs=48, top_k=6, EP4: topk_ids (48, 6).nelement() = 288 passed as
# valid_shape_m while the rank's GEMM only handles ~72 rows.
# See estimate_local_valid_shape_m in
# python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/humming.py
Serving A/B protocol:
python3 -m sglang.benchmark.serving --dataset-name random --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 256 --random-range-ratio 1 --num-prompts 384 --max-concurrency 48
, unique seed per round, /flush_cache between rounds, drop first warmup round, median of 4.
Environment
Python: 3.12.3, PyTorch: 2.13.0+cu130, CUDA: 13.0 (driver 580.105.08)
GPU 0-3: NVIDIA L20X (SM90)
sglang: 0.0.0.dev1+g20518d851, sglang-kernel: 0.4.7
flashinfer: 0.6.18, triton: 3.7.1, transformers: 5.12.1
Possible fixes (for discussion)
(a) Document
valid_shape_m
as a hint defined on the global routed-element scale and leave the estimator as-is (what we reverted to; zero risk).
(b) Make ladder generation convention-aware per gemm_type and re-tune per device.
(c) Extend the launcher/config-selection API to take (rows, local expert count) or tokens-per-expert as a second key.
Happy to share the full A/B matrix and per-cubin timing data, attaching below.

Issue body actions
Checklist
I searched related issues but found no solution.
The bug persists in the latest version.
Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at

. Otherwise, it will be closed.
Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.
Describe the bug
Serving
deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash
with
--speculative-algorithm DSPARK
on
2 nodes × 4 H200 (TP8 + EP8, LeaderWorkerSet, one 4-GPU pod per node over RoCE)
deterministically deadlocks during startup, right after the DSpark draft weights finish loading. Three consecutive attempts across two different images all hang at the same point with the same split stack; removing the DSPARK flags (identical everything else) starts cleanly in ~10 minutes.
The split we capture on every occurrence (py-spy dump, all 8 scheduler processes):
Node 0 schedulers (leader, TP0-3) — parked after
Load weight end ... type=DeepseekV4ForCausalLMDSpark
:
monitored_barrier (torch/distributed/distributed_c10d.py:5435)
dist_barrier_after_load (model_runner_components/load_model_utils.py:380)   # also seen :344 on dev-cu13
load_model (model_runner.py:1307)
initialize (model_runner.py:653)
Node 1 schedulers (worker, TP4-7) — parked earlier, inside the KV-pool memory probe:
all_reduce (torch/distributed/distributed_c10d.py:3252)
wrapper (torch/distributed/c10d_logger.py:83)
get_available_gpu_memory (utils/common.py:550)
_profile_available_bytes (kv_cache_configurator.py:2214)
The worker-side ranks have posted the memory-probe all-reduce and wait for the leader-side ranks, while the leader-side ranks wait at a different synchronization point (post-load barrier). The two node halves sit at mismatched collective sites permanently — GPU utilization 0%, GPU memory and logs frozen from that point on. No watchdog fires (the stall happens before the scheduler loop starts).
This looks like the same unsynchronized-decision family as
#39886
(DSpark CUDA-graph memory check not synchronized across ranks → ranks disagree on collective participation) and the runtime variant in
#33289
(multi-node TP + DSpark → per-rank divergence → unmatched collectives). Our case adds a multi-node TP8/EP8 startup reproduction with full per-node py-spy stacks.
Reproduction rate:
3/3 with DSPARK on 2 nodes (2×
dev-cu13
, 1×
dev-cu13-dsv41
); 0 failures without DSPARK — the identical non-DSPARK cell starts cleanly in ~10 min and served a full benchmark suite.

title: [Performance] MXFP4 x MXFP8 W4A8 with group-32 activation scales is slow on H100 · Issue #38 · vllm-project/humming · GitHub
body:
[Performance] MXFP4 x MXFP8 W4A8 with group-32 activation scales is slow on H100
#38
New issue
Copy link
New issue
Copy link
Closed as not planned
Closed as not planned
[Performance] MXFP4 x MXFP8 W4A8 with group-32 activation scales is slow on H100
#38
Copy link
Description
hit-zhengbao
opened
on Jul 13, 2026
Issue body actions
We are evaluating an MXFP4 x MXFP8 W4A8 GEMM on NVIDIA H100.
The fused-E8M0 Humming kernel is numerically correct, but with group-32
MXFP8 activation scales it is significantly slower than both:
Humming's generic group-scale path
A QDQ baseline that dequantizes both operands and then runs a BF16 GEMM
We would like to ask whether group-32 MXFP8 input scaling is an intended
performance target and whether there are plans to optimize this case on Hopper.
Quantization format
The operands use the following format:
Activation payload: FP8 E4M3
Activation scale: per-token, per-K-group power-of-two scale
Activation group size: 32
Weight payload: MXFP4 E2M1
Weight scale: E8M0
Weight group size: 32
Output dtype: BF16

Core Kernels
1. _gluon_w4a8_mxfp8_accs_kernel
Processes one 32-element K group at a time:
WGMMA(A_fp8, W_fp8) -> FP32 partial
partial *= input_e8m0_scale
master += partial
This is the key to preserving numerical accuracy: the activation scale is applied to the FP32 partial accumulator, avoiding an additional rounding step from dequantizing and casting the activation back to FP8.
2. _gluon_w4a8_mxfp8_accs_batched_kernel
Loads multiple 32-element K groups in each TMA stage, typically using LOAD_K=128 or LOAD_K=256. This reduces TMA transactions, barrier overhead, and main-loop scheduling costs. It is the default high-performance path for large M.
3. _gluon_w4a8_mxfp8_splitk_kernel
Used for small M. It increases parallelism by distributing the K dimension across multiple CTAs. Each CTA accumulates into an FP32 temporary output using atomic additions, after which the result is converted to the requested output dtype.
4. _gluon_w4a8_mxfp8_prmt_kernel
A fallback path used when the WPREQ exactness guard fails. It uses prmt.b32 to fuse the decoding of packed MXFP4 weights with their weight scales into FP8 values. This path requires an offline T2 weight repacking step.
5. _gluon_w4a8_mxfp8_kernel
The most general but slower fallback path. It explicitly performs MXFP4 decoding, E8M0 scale application, and FP8 conversion inside the main loop.

Summary
This PR pipelines direct NVLink dispatch using three shared-memory TMA buffers per dispatch warp.
Previously, a dispatch warp prepared tokens sequentially around remote S2G stores. With this change, the next token's hidden data, scale factors, metadata, and routing information are prefetched while previous remote stores remain in flight.
At steady state, the three buffers are used for:
A previous token whose remote S2G store may still be in flight.
The current token being sent to remote ranks.
The next token being prefetched from global memory.
Before recycling the oldest buffer,
tma_store_wait<1>()
reduces the number of outstanding store groups to one. This keeps buffer reuse safe without fully draining all remote stores between tokens.
The shared-memory calculation now accounts for all three staging buffers, and direct NVLink dispatch is limited to at most 14 dispatch warps. The non-NVLink path remains single-buffered.

Tested on 8 x NVIDIA H100 GPUs with direct NVLink dispatch.

v6
The multi-buffer TMA scheduling and matching shared-memory sizing appear consistent across NVLink and non-NVLink paths, with outstanding stores flushed before buffer reuse.
v4
The dispatch kernel switches from single per-warp staging (drained fully per token) to three round-robin staging TMA buffers per dispatch warp. While the current token's remote S2G/NVLink/RDMA store stays in flight, the next token's hidden/SF/metadata/routing is prefetched into the buffer whose previous use is the oldest outstanding store group (deterministically token_iter - 2 of 3, or none on a warm-up iteration); tma_store_wait<1>() retires that group before the buffer is overwritten, and the final barrier drains the last in-flight store. The host sizes per-warp smem by 3x (RDMA: 1x) and caps NVLink dispatch warps at 14, with the RDMA path remaining single-buffered and full-drained (unchanged behavior). Edge cases (first iteration, last token skipped, warps with no tokens, per-token global slot/counter writes) are all safe and unchanged. Measured on 8xH100 dispatch goes 250->280 GB/s, combine unchanged. Overall the change correctly and faithfully implements the PR as a pure pipelining/perf optimization on the previously single-buffered path.
v3
This PR pipelines direct NVLink dispatch by switching from double- to triple-buffered TMA staging (kNumDirectNVLinkTmaBuffers 2->3, kNumTmaBuffers 2->3 for the NVLink path), and refactoring the per-token body into a
prepare_token
lambda so the next token's hidden/SF/metadata/routing can be prefetched while the current token's remote S2G stores are in flight. The phase tracking was generalized from two scalars (phase_0/phase_1) to a
phases[kNumTmaBuffers]
array, and buffer indexing changed from bitmask (
& (kNumTmaBuffers-1)
) to modulo (
% kNumTmaBuffers
) to support 3 (non-power-of-two) buffers. The host-side shared-memory computation already multiplies by num_tma_buffers and caps direct NVLink dispatch at 14 warps.
Correctness analysis (all verified sound):
Buffer-reuse safety: In steady state, entering iteration N up to 2 store groups (iters N-2, N-1) are outstanding.
tma_store_wait<1>()
retires iter N-2's store (which read buffer (N-2)%3 == (N+1)%3) before prepare_token(N+1) writes into that same buffer. This correctly matches the recycled buffer to the just-retired store group, so triple buffering is safe.
Per-buffer mbarrier phases persist across reuse (buffer b used at iters b, b+3, ...), and
phases[]
is zero-initialized; flip semantics are preserved.
The buffer indexing change to
% kNumTmaBuffers
is applied consistently in both prepare_token and the main loop and is required because 3 is not a power of two.
The NVLink prefetch (prepare_token for the next token) is issued before awaiting the current buffer's load arrival, correctly overlapping the next token's G2S load with the current token's remote S2G store; it targets a distinct buffer with an independent mbarrier so there is no cross-buffer hazard.
Non-NVLink path stays single-buffered (kNumTmaBuffers=1) and keeps a full
tma_store_wait()
drain before recycling; behavior is unchanged. Startup/drain edges (num_tokens <= 1, first iteration with no outstanding stores) are handled by the
next_token_idx < num_tokens
guards.
Host/device consistency: the smem divisor in dispatch.hpp accounts for num_tma_buffers=3 and matches the device-side kNumTmaBuffers.
Overall the change is internally consistent and the pipelining logic is sound. The two comments below are minor maintainability suggestions, not correctness issues.

MXFP4 weight + FP8 activation path:
MXFP4xBF16: optimize the existing MXFP4 weight + BF16 activation path.
INT4xFP8: optimize the existing INT4 weight + FP8 activation path.
MXFP4xFP8: add MXFP4 weight + FP8 activation with pre-MMA E8M0 scale fusion and runtime
per-token FP8 activation quantization.
The MXFP4xFP8 path follows the high-level weight preprocessing and
dequantization idea used by
Humming
:
the MXFP4 weight scale is transformed into a bounded E8M0 exponent offset and
folded into the FP8 operand before MMA. FlashInfer keeps this flow integrated
with its fused MoE runtime, autotune, and CUTLASS extension backend.
The implementation keeps the changes inside FlashInfer's CUTLASS extension
layer rather than modifying vendored CUTLASS. The main changes are:
Enable Hopper FP4 kernels without requiring CUDA native FP4 headers on SM90
by using CUTLASS subbyte FP4 types.
Add optimized mixed-input mainloops for post-MMA scaling and pre-MMA E8M0
scale fusion.
Precompute grouped GEMM work scheduling and TMA descriptor state before the
main GEMM kernel.
Use folded weight-scale storage so the weight-scale layout is independent of
the profiled
TileK
.
Add precomputed scheduler kernels for ping-pong and cooperative grouped GEMM
schedulers.
Add runtime activation expansion and per-token FP8 quantization support for
the pre-MMA E8M0 scale-fusion path.
Add per-token scale epilogue callbacks for the FP8 activation + MXFP4 weight
path.
Extend autotune and tactic validation so Hopper mixed-input tactics are
checked for correctness before being selected.
Add and update tests for Hopper MXFP4xBF16, INT4xFP8, and MXFP4xFP8 pre-MMA scale
paths.

Implementation Notes
The Hopper FP4 compatibility path uses CUTLASS FP4 storage on SM90 and keeps
CUDA native FP4 as a toolkit-dependent feature instead of a Hopper
requirement.
The mixed-input grouped GEMM scheduler now supports a precomputed work map.
This avoids doing grouped tile lookup and descriptor updates in the main GEMM
hot path.
The folded weight-scale layout decouples model preprocessing from the
selected
TileK
, which lets autotune choose among multiple
TileK
values
without requiring multiple prepacked weight-scale layouts.
The pre-MMA E8M0 scale path fuses the weight scale into FP8 operands before
WGMMA and applies the activation token scale in the epilogue.
The MXFP4xFP8 pre-MMA scale path is inspired by Humming's weight
preprocessing/dequantization flow:
https://github.com/inclusionAI/humming
The runtime FP8 activation quantization path computes per-token activation
scales while expanding routed MoE rows.
The autotune validation path now rejects tactics that fail correctness before
timing and selection.

Purpose
With
--moe-backend humming
and expert parallelism, Humming runs DeepSeek-V4.1's MXFP4 experts on its grouped GEMM. On Hopper the indexed GEMM is much faster for this model. This PR makes
get_humming_moe_gemm_type()
return
indexed
when all of these hold:
the experts are MXFP4 with DeepSeek V4 routing;
model_type
is
deepseek_v41
or
deepseek_v41_text
;
the device is CUDA SM90;
there are no all2all kernels, or the backend is
allgather_reducescatter
.
Without EP, Humming already picks indexed, so nothing changes there.
VLLM_HUMMING_MOE_GEMM_TYPE
still overrides the choice. Since
#56997
, Humming is the default MXFP4 MoE backend on SM90, so V4.1 with EP on Hopper otherwise runs the grouped GEMM by default; this PR moves that default path to indexed too. The rule applies with BF16 activations and with per-token FP8 activations (
--quantization-config.moe.activation fp8_per_token
).
The MXFP4 MoE method (DeepSeek V4/V4.1, Kimi-K3, plain mxfp4) now runs
quantization_config.moe.activation
:
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash -tp 8 --enable-expert-parallel \
    --moe-backend humming --quantization-config.moe.activation fp8_per_token
Humming takes the named format as a fixed input schema, with its input-schema fallback off.
Other explicit backends must run the named format, and
auto
keeps only the backends that do. Before, these models ignored the name on every backend. Now a backend that does not run it stops vLLM, on every platform (CUDA, ROCm, XPU, CPU). The DeepSeek V4 MegaMoE backends (
deep_gemm_mega_moe
,
aiter_mega_moe
) build their own experts and do not read the name. On ROCm, the Kimi-K3 AITER path, which skips the backend selector, now refuses a named activation instead of ignoring it. For example,
fp8_per_token
with
flashinfer_trtllm
now stops vLLM instead of running MXFP8. A draft model with its own
speculative_config.moe_backend
inherits the target's
quantization_config
, so the same rule applies to it.
The startup log prints the format Humming runs:
Humming MoE activations: fp8_per_token (group size 0, scale dtype float32)
. The line appears for every Humming MoE model, gpt-oss included.
On SM90 Humming,
mxfp8
and
fp8_per_block_dynamic
stop vLLM at startup, before the weights load. Humming has no e8m0 input scales on WGMMA, and humming 0.1.16 rejects fp32 group scales with MXFP4 weights (
[Bug][Humming] MXFP4 weight + block-FP8 activation is listed as supported on Hopper, but humming-kernels 0.1.16 rejects it
#60600
). Group-wise scales are also 1.2x to 24x slower than per-token in the SM90 Humming GEMM at M >= 256 (numbers in the review reply).
VLLM_HUMMING_INPUT_QUANT_CONFIG
still works as on main, with no early check: a format Humming cannot run fails while the weights convert, as before. With
--moe-backend humming
, setting it together with
moe.activation
is an error.
gpt-oss is unchanged. With no name, nothing changes.
Test Plan
pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_moe.py -k
"
named_activation or activation_on_sm90 or humming or indexed
"
pytest tests/quantization/test_quantization_config_args.py \
    tests/quantization/test_humming_mxfp4_block_fp8.py tests/kernels/moe/test_b12x.py \
    tests/kernels/moe/test_topk_softplus_sqrt.py tests/quantization/test_gfx950_moe.py
pytest tests/models/kimi_k3/test_gfx942_int4.py
pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_ocp_mx_moe.py -k unsupported_reasons
test_humming_deepseek_v41_hopper_uses_indexed_gemm_with_ep
calls
get_humming_moe_gemm_type
and checks that V4.1 with EP gets indexed, with and without
allgather_reducescatter
, and that DeepEP, SM100 and DeepSeek V4 keep the grouped GEMM. It does not need the humming package.
test_deepseek_v4_mxfp4_backend_must_run_named_activation
checks on any GPU that
auto
and
flashinfer_trtllm
refuse
fp8_per_token
, and that
humming
refuses the env JSON plus a name ("not both").
test_humming_deepseek_v4_activation_on_sm90
checks that SM90 Humming accepts
fp8_per_token
and refuses
mxfp8
. It skips on other GPUs, so in CI it runs only in the optional H100 FP8 MoE kernels job;
kernels-moe-test
runs on L4. The Kimi-K3 AITER refusal has no unit test: it is a short guard, and a test would have to mock the whole K3 path.
user_moe_activation_override()
(was
_user_moe_activation_override()
) is now public because
quantization/mxfp4.py
imports it; the existing monkeypatches in
test_b12x.py
,
test_ocp_mx_moe.py
and
test_gfx950_moe.py
use the new name.
Startup check:
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash -tp 8 --enable-expert-parallel --moe-backend humming
on 8x H200, with these additions:
A:
--quantization-config.moe.activation fp8_per_token
and DSpark speculative decoding (
--speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":1}'
; V4.1 has no classic MTP draft), then one completion request.
B:
--quantization-config.moe.activation mxfp8
.
C:
--quantization-config.moe.activation fp8_per_block_dynamic
.
D:
--quantization-config.moe.activation fp8_per_token
with
VLLM_HUMMING_INPUT_QUANT_CONFIG='{"dtype":"float8e4m3"}'
.
E: only
VLLM_HUMMING_INPUT_QUANT_CONFIG='{"dtype":"float8e4m3"}'
, then one completion request.
auto
: no
--moe-backend
and no activation name, then one completion request.
Throughput: offline
LLM
runs of DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on 8x H200, TP8+EP,
--moe-backend humming
, 2 repeats. Prefill is 16 random 8192-token prompts with 1 output token. Decode is 64 random 512-token prompts with 256 output tokens. The GEMM type was set with
VLLM_HUMMING_MOE_GEMM_TYPE
.
Test Result
Unit tests on one H200: the
test_moe.py
selection above, 41 passed (the SM90 test runs there, not skipped). The other selector and config tests: 1741 passed, 17 skipped.
test_gfx942_int4.py
: 7 passed. The
test_ocp_mx_moe.py
test that patches the renamed function: 1 passed. pre-commit is clean.
Startup check on 8x H200. B, A and the
auto
run are on this PR's head (one commit on
e2414ec
). C, D and E ran on an earlier head (
194da61
), before the error messages were shortened:
B (
mxfp8
): stops in model init, before any weights load:
ValueError: Humming MoE cannot run activation=mxfp8: SM90 WGMMA needs float32 input scales
A (
fp8_per_token
, DSpark): ready after 341 s, completion
" Paris. The Eiffel Tower is in Paris."
. The log shows:
[fused_humming_moe.py:146] Using indexed gemm for humming moe
[mxfp4.py:529] Using 'HUMMING' Mxfp4 MoE backend.
[moe.py:633] Humming MoE activations: fp8_per_token (group size 0, scale dtype float32)
[mxfp4.py:2142] Using HummingIndexedExperts
The DSpark draft builds its own MoE (16/128 experts per rank) through the same method and prints no different backend or format line.
auto
(no
--moe-backend
, no activation name): ready after 221 s, completion
" Paris."
. The log shows:
[fused_humming_moe.py:146] Using indexed gemm for humming moe
[mxfp4.py:808] Using 'HUMMING' Mxfp4 MoE backend.
[moe.py:633] Humming MoE activations: bf16 (group size 0, scale dtype None)
[mxfp4.py:2142] Using HummingIndexedExperts
C (
fp8_per_block_dynamic
): stops at model init. On this head the check is the same; the message is now:
ValueError: Humming MoE cannot run activation=fp8_per_block_dynamic: No compatible Humming input schema for HummingInputSchema(... input_scale_group_size=128, input_scale_dtype=float32 ...) with weight schema HummingWeightSchema(b_dtype=float4e2m1, bs_dtype=float8e8m0, weight_scale_group_size=32 ...) on SM90 (allow_fallback=False)
D (env JSON plus name): stops at model init. On this head the message is now:
ValueError: Set quantization_config.moe.activation or VLLM_HUMMING_INPUT_QUANT_CONFIG, not both.
E (env JSON only): ready after 430 s, completion
" Paris."
, and the log shows
Humming MoE activations: fp8_per_token (group size 0, scale dtype float32)
. On this head the env JSON gets no startup check, as on main.
Indexed vs grouped throughput:
Activations
Prefill
Decode
BF16
+47%
+63%
per-token FP8 (reference)
+24%
+36%
For reference, with FP8 at decode, grouped is 16% slower than Marlin (2,222 vs 2,648 output tok/s) and indexed is 14% faster.
An end-to-end run on TP4+EP logged
Using indexed gemm for humming moe
and
HummingIndexedExperts
.

I think it is interesting to support this, but I am a bit skeptical about how safe it is to make it the default, i.e., assume per-token FP8 quantization has no accuracy impact over BF16/grouped-FP8.
Notably, on Blackwell where FP8 activations are already the default, we use MXFP8 (group-32 e8m0 scales), or block-FP8 (group-128); both much finer-grained than one scale per token row. I suspect per-token FP8 is too coarse, and GSM8K is simply not a rigorous enough eval to study real accuracy impact.
I would either make the per-token FP8 path opt-in for now, or evaluate this more exhaustively before making it default, e.g. on agentic evals.

Thanks, agreed. The latest push makes the activation format an explicit, named choice. It uses the existing typed field instead of a new env string, because those names are documented, validated at parse time, and shared with gpt-oss:
--moe-backend humming --quantization-config.moe.activation fp8_per_token
The names come from
QUANT_KEY_NAMES
(
fp8_per_token
,
fp8_per_block_dynamic
,
mxfp8
). Each name is one scale layout on every arch. A named format turns Humming's input-schema fallback off, so it runs as named or vLLM stops.
It applies to the MXFP4 MoE method: DeepSeek V4/V4.1, Kimi-K3 and plain mxfp4 checkpoints. A backend that cannot run the name stops vLLM at startup, also on SM100f. For example,
fp8_per_token
with
flashinfer_trtllm
or
auto
no longer runs MXFP8 silently.
On SM90 Humming,
mxfp8
and
fp8_per_block_dynamic
stop vLLM at startup, before the weights load.
mxfp8
needs e8m0 input scales, which Humming's WGMMA path does not have. humming 0.1.16 rejects
fp8_per_block_dynamic
(fp32 group-128 scales) with MXFP4 weights, although vLLM's supported-pairs table lists it for Hopper. I opened
[Bug][Humming] MXFP4 weight + block-FP8 activation is listed as supported on Hopper, but humming-kernels 0.1.16 rejects it
#60600
for that mismatch.
The startup log prints the resolved format, for example
Humming MoE activations: fp8_per_token (group size 0, scale dtype float32)
. It also does so for the old
VLLM_HUMMING_INPUT_QUANT_CONFIG
path, which still works. Setting both the env JSON and the name is an error.
With no name nothing changes: Marlin with BF16 stays the default for V4.1 on Hopper.
gpt-oss is unchanged: its selector still drops Humming when an activation is named.

Humming indexed GEMM with EP on Hopper: for DeepSeek V4.1 (model_type
deepseek_v41 / deepseek_v41_text) MXFP4 experts on SM90, Humming now
picks the indexed GEMM also under expert parallelism, when there is no
all2all or the all2all is allgather_reducescatter. Other EP setups still
use grouped_contiguous. Humming is already the default MXFP4 MoE
backend on SM90 (
vllm-project#56997
), so this also changes the default path. On
TP8+EP, indexed is 47% faster at prefill and 63% faster at decode with
BF16 activations, and 24% and 36% faster with per-token FP8.
VLLM_HUMMING_MOE_GEMM_TYPE still overrides the choice.

Named MoE activation format: the DeepSeek V4 MXFP4 MoE selector now
honors --quantization-config.moe.activation, so per-token FP8 on Humming
is an explicit choice:

  --moe-backend humming --quantization-config.moe.activation fp8_per_token

- With --moe-backend humming, the format is checked before the weights
  load and then passed to the Humming conversion with schema fallback
  off. On SM90, mxfp8 is refused because WGMMA has no e8m0 input scales.
  Setting VLLM_HUMMING_INPUT_QUANT_CONFIG as well is an error. The env
  JSON alone works as on main.
- Another explicit backend that does not run the format fails, and auto
  keeps only the backends that run it. For example, fp8_per_token with
  flashinfer_trtllm no longer runs MXFP8 without saying so.
- The Kimi-K3 SiTU AITER path skips the selector and runs BF16 only, so
  it refuses a named format.
- The Humming MoE conversion logs the activation format it runs.
- user_moe_activation_override() is public and returns None when no
  vLLM config is set.

Without moe.activation, backend and activation selection are unchanged.

def _get_priority_backends() -> list[Mxfp4MoeBackend]:
    """Get available backends in priority order. SM100+ prefers DeepGEMM FP4 /
    TRTLLM MXFP8; SM90 falls through to Triton_unfused or Marlin (the

        ]
    if current_platform.is_xpu():

        return [Mxfp4MoeBackend.CPU]
    _AVAILABLE_BACKENDS = [
        Mxfp4MoeBackend.FLASHINFER_TRTLLM_MXFP4_MXFP8,

def get_humming_moe_gemm_type(moe_config: FusedMoEConfig | None = None) -> str:
    env_gemm_type: str | None = envs.VLLM_HUMMING_MOE_GEMM_TYPE
    if env_gemm_type is not None and env_gemm_type.lower() != "auto":
        env_gemm_type = env_gemm_type.lower()

FILE vllm/model_executor/kernels/mhc/tilelang_kernels.py:58-98; SHA256 61a384a091344d8207a04b2b7c74d30a81626eec4c068cf1dd034699cbfc34b5
# every (tile_n, n_thr) pair is one more kernel to compile. Tuned on GB300
# (hc_mult 4, hidden_size 5120 and 7168) against the separate post + split-k
# GEMM it replaces; the bands are coarse because the loss against a per-shape
# optimum is ~1-2%, while one fixed config gives up to 18% at the top of the
# range.
_FUSED_POST_PRE_N_THR = 128
_FUSED_POST_PRE_MAX_TOKENS = 32


def mhc_fused_post_pre_split_config(
    num_tokens: int, hidden_size: int, hc_mult: int
) -> tuple[int, int, int] | None:
    """Pick ``(tile_n, n_splits, n_thr)`` for the fused post + pre-norm GEMM.

    Returns None when a separate post kernel followed by a split-k GEMM is the
    better choice, or when the hidden size does not divide evenly across the
    fused kernel's block. One source of truth for the dispatch decision, the
    compile key and the launch, which must agree.
    """
    if num_tokens > _FUSED_POST_PRE_MAX_TOKENS:
        return None
    n_thr = _FUSED_POST_PRE_N_THR
    if hidden_size % n_thr:
        return None
    # The projection tiles supply the parallelism a small token count cannot,
    # so the tile grows with the batch: 1.3x at one token and 1.03x at 32
    # against a split-k GEMM given the split its own estimator computes.
    if num_tokens < 16:
        tile_n, n_splits = 2, 8
    else:
        tile_n, n_splits = 6, 8
    # The kernel drops projection tiles and k-slices it cannot fill evenly.
    mix_size = hc_mult * (hc_mult + 2)
    while tile_n > 1 and mix_size % tile_n:
        tile_n -= 1
    while n_splits > 1 and hidden_size % (n_splits * n_thr):
        n_splits //= 2
    return tile_n, n_splits, n_thr


def require_fused_post_pre_config(

FILE vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/ops/mhc.py:30-72; SHA256 c8233a70004719017ff6a5826ca538c92ea6319a9c7c0090dc8fc2e603db25e7
    from vllm.distributed.device_communicators.cuda_communicator import CudaCommunicator

    from .cute_dsl import AllReduceMHC

logger = init_logger(__name__)

# GB200 TP4/FlashInfer improves through 16 tokens; larger screens tie or regress.
MHC_OVERLAP_MAX_TOKENS = 16

# The fused all-reduce + mHC kernel of the overlap path, built once by
# init_mhc_all_reduce.
_all_reduce_mhc: "AllReduceMHC | None" = None


def supports_mhc_overlap(vllm_config: VllmConfig) -> bool:
    """Check kernel requirements and safety of sharing the coefficient stream."""
    config = vllm_config.model_config.hf_config
    # DeepGEMM's prenorm kernel requires K % 64 == 0, N % 8 == 0, and N <= 32.
    mix_size = config.hc_mult * (config.hc_mult + 2)
    return (
        current_platform.is_device_capability_family(100)
        and is_deep_gemm_supported()
        and config.hidden_size % 64 == 0
        and 0 < mix_size <= 32
        and mix_size % 8 == 0
        and not vllm_config.parallel_config.use_ubatching
    )


def supports_mhc_all_reduce(vllm_config: VllmConfig) -> bool:
    parallel = vllm_config.parallel_config
    config = vllm_config.model_config.hf_config
    if (
        parallel.tensor_parallel_size != 4
        or parallel.enable_expert_parallel
        or config.hidden_size != 5120
        or config.hc_mult != 4
    ):
        return False
    # The custom all-reduce's MNNVL buffers succeed exactly when NVLink
    # multicast does, which the fused kernel's own mailbox needs too.
    comm = cast("CudaCommunicator", get_tp_group().device_communicator).ca_comm
    return comm is not None and bool(comm.mnnvl_lamport_ag_multicast_ptr)

title: [DNM][Experimental] Add MI355X TP2 V4 Flash SGLang 8k1k MTP sweep / 新增 MI355X TP2 V4 Flash SGLang 8k1k MTP 扫描
body:
## Summary

- Add `dsv4flash-fp4-mi355x-sglang-mtp`: DeepSeek-V4-Flash on MI355X at TP2, 8k1k fixed sequence, concurrency 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128. Companion to [B300 #3516](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/pull/3516) and [B200 #3517](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/pull/3517).
- Bundled MTP through `EAGLE` with 2 steps, top-k 1, and 3 draft tokens, matching the other two PRs.
- CUDA/HIP graphs are disabled (`cuda-graph-backend-decode: disabled`, `cuda-graph-backend-prefill: disabled`), so decode, prefill, and EAGLE target-verify/draft all run eagerly; startup reports zero capture time for every graph phase.
- Image `lmsysorg/sglang-rocm:v0.5.20-rocm720-mi35x-20260926`, the newest ROCm 7.2.0 MI35x build.
- Serving flags and ROCm env follow SGLang's [MI355X Flash FP4 low-latency recipe](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/8ca82118e0e1a0a1b49f85f675843b19ebb388ba/docs/src/snippets/configs/deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4.jsx) (`dsv4` attention, page 256, fp8 KV, shared-expert fusion, mem-fraction 0.90, SWA ratio 0.15, chunked prefill 16384), reduced from TP8 to TP2. Radix cache is disabled for the fixed-sequence workload; admission and the decode graph batch are pinned to each concurrency.
- Weights and KV stay on GPU, with real speculative verification. No engine patches, external draft, CPU offloading, or simulated acceptance.
- Includes the same `--dsv4` fixed-sequence client passthrough and test as #3516/#3517 (identical content), so this PR stands alone.

## Validation

- GPU sweep and evals: pending (`full-sweep-fail-fast`).

---

## 摘要

- 新增 `dsv4flash-fp4-mi355x-sglang-mtp`：DeepSeek-V4-Flash 在 MI355X 上以 TP2 运行 8k1k 固定序列，并发为 1、2、4、8、16、32、64、128，与 [B300 #3516](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/pull/3516) 和 [B200 #3517](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/pull/3517) 配套。
- 通过 `EAGLE` 使用原生 MTP（2 steps、top-k 1、3 draft tokens），与另外两个 PR 一致。
- 关闭 CUDA/HIP graph（`cuda-graph-backend-decode: disabled`、`cuda-graph-backend-prefill: disabled`），decode、prefill 及 EAGLE 验证/draft 均以 eager 模式运行；启动日志中各 graph 阶段捕获耗时均为 0。
- 镜像为 `lmsysorg/sglang-rocm:v0.5.20-rocm720-mi35x-20260926`。Serving 参数与 ROCm 环境变量沿用 SGLang MI355X Flash FP4 低延迟配方，由 TP8 改为 TP2；固定序列负载关闭 radix cache。
- 权重和 KV 保留在 GPU，采用真实验证；不修改引擎、不使用外部 draft、不卸载至 CPU、不模拟接受长度。
- 包含与 #3516/#3517 相同的 `--dsv4` 客户端参数透传及测试，可独立合并。

## 验证

- GPU 扫描与评测：待 CI（`full-sweep-fail-fast`）。

## Summary

- Bump `qwen3.5-fp4-mi355x-sglang-agentic-mtp` from `lmsysorg/sglang-rocm:v0.5.19-rocm720-mi35x-20260917` to `lmsysorg/sglang-rocm:v0.5.20-rocm720-mi35x-20260920`.

## Details

HiCache stays `kernel` / `page_first`, ratio 1.5, `write_through`. Model stays `amd/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-MXFP4-AttnFP8-V2`. Without AITER allreduce fusion, collectives use the existing `ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION=INT4` path.

title: perf(dsv4): repin MI355X vLLM AgentX to the 2026-09-20 ROCm nightly / 将 MI355X vLLM AgentX 重新固定至 2026-09-20 ROCm nightly
body:
## Description

Repin the DSV4 MI355X vLLM AgentX recipe (`dsv4-fp4-mi355x-vllm-agentic-mtp`) to the newest published ROCm nightly, `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100-d05da62e9ccdf8e342b15bf6785d83224cc165af` (digest `sha256:461e9c79…`, Docker Hub pushed `2026-09-20T06:32:10Z`, tag commit vllm-project/vllm@d05da62e), up from `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-eed1f3d0c6043bd494424a22443ee198dd56f657` on `main` (pinned in #3071).

The original revision of this PR pinned the 2026-09-15 build `nightly-rocm100-cd10ed6f…`. That tag is now five nightlies old, so the pin moved forward to the current one. `main` has also been merged into the branch, which moved this PR's `perf-changelog.yaml` entry to the physical end of the file; `main`'s changelog bytes are preserved byte-for-byte.

### What the new nightly adds

`d05da62e` is 294 upstream commits ahead of `cd10ed6f` and 352 ahead of the CSA merge commit. Besides [vllm-project/vllm#51794](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51794), which enables CSA (Compressed Sparse Attention) multi-stream overlap for DeepSeek-V4 on ROCm so the two compressor `wkv_gate` GEMMs run on aux HIP streams instead of serially on the main stream during decode, the range brings in:

| Upstream PR | Change |
| --- | --- |
| [#57132](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57132) | Reverts the DeepSeek-V4 accuracy breakdown on ROCm (accuracy-relevant for the eval leg) |
| [#57465](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57465) | Fixes fused MoE expert distribution for DeepSeek V4 |
| [#56853](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56853) | Enables HCA dual-stream overlap for DeepSeek-V4 |
| [#50455](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50455) | Fixes the sparse-indexer logits collapse on gfx950/gfx942 |
| [#56743](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56743), [#57434](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57434) | gfx950 decode top-k optimization and ragged-metadata reuse across layers |

title: Add B300 Dynamo+SGLang AgentX configs for DeepSeek V4 with NIXL KV transfer / 添加使用 NIXL KV 传输的 DeepSeek V4 B300 Dynamo+SGLang AgentX 配置
body:
[by Claude Code]

## Summary

Adds DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813 FP4 B300 Dynamo+SGLang AgentX recipes. The recipes come from #3631, with disaggregated KV transfer over NIXL instead of Mooncake, and now run on `lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-efa-20261019-3c560089`.

- **Points:** aggregate TP8 c1, TP4 c4, TP4 c8 (HiCache) and DEP8 c384 (HiCache); disaggregated 1P1D DEP8 c64/c240 and 1P2D DEP8 c64 (HiCache prefill). Topology, concurrency, cache sizes and memory fractions are unchanged.
- **Image:** `nightly-dev-efa-20261019-3c560089`, the AWS EFA variant of the 2026-10-19 nightly (sgl-project/sglang#41006), replaces `nightly-dev-20260916-c9a8fba9`.
  - On `nightly-dev-20261013-7224fce1`, the disaggregated workers failed at NIXL startup with `createBackend: unsupported backend 'LIBFABRIC'`. The LIBFABRIC plugin of NIXL 1.5.0 needs libfabric's `FABRIC_1.7` symbol version, and the regular image ships only Ubuntu's libfabric 1.17, which stops at `FABRIC_1.6`. The cluster no longer injects the host's libfabric into containers, so nothing newer was available.
  - The EFA variant adds AWS EFA installer 1.50.0 (libfabric 2.6.0) and puts `/opt/amazon/efa/lib` first on `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`. Its build checks that the NIXL plugin resolves libfabric there.
- **Attention DP:** DEP8 workers set `attn-dp-size: 8` in place of `dp-size: 8` + `enable-dp-attention: true`, which sgl-project/sglang#41818 deprecated.
- **Dynamo:** the recipes use the image's bundled Dynamo `1.6.0.dev20261018` (`dynamo.install: false`), which is also the router version in the master config.
  - It includes ai-dynamo/dynamo#16005, which counts attention-DP ranks from `attn_dp_size`. In this SGLang, both DP spellings resolve to `dp_size=1, attn_dp_size=8`. A Dynamo without that fix registers one DP rank per DEP8 worker and subscribes only to rank 0's KV events, so the KV router sends every request to DP rank 0.
  - The previous revision built Dynamo `b208989fbe` from source, because the 1013 image's bundled `1.6.0.dev20261010` predated that fix.
- **Disaggregated KV transfer:** NIXL with the LIBFABRIC backend (`SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_NIXL_BACKEND=LIBFABRIC`, which the EFA image also sets by default). The image's NIXL 1.5.0 ships the plugin and the image ships the libfabric it needs, so there is no setup script, waiver or package change.
  - Both disaggregated workers set `FI_EFA_USE_UNSOLICITED_WRITE_RECV=0`. NIXL's LIBFABRIC backend disables the EFA provider's unsolicited write recv only when built against libfabric 2.3 or newer. The image's NIXL is not (its "Successfully disabled unsolicited write recv" log line never appears), so with the image's libfabric 2.6 the feature stays on.
  - With it on, the previous sweep of this PR (run 39191181928, two attempts of 1P1D c240) had about 1.4% of requests time out on decode after 900 s. Prefill had already sent their KV, but the completions never reached decode. Throughput per GPU fell from about 60k (0916 image) to 44k tok/s.
- **Image behavior to note:**
  - This SGLang fuses the shared expert into the DeepGEMM Mega-MoE kernel by default (sgl-project/sglang#39313), so DEP8 throughput may differ from earlier runs of these recipes for that reason too.
  - The EFA image sets `NCCL_NET_PLUGIN=ofi` and `NCCL_TUNER_PLUGIN=ofi` (aws-ofi-nccl 1.21.1) by default. Every worker in these recipes fits on one node.
- No recipe enables the W4A4 MXFP4 Mega-MoE path. Prefill and decode use the same DSpark K=6 method.
- On `b300-dsxe`, Dynamo+SGLang serves DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813 from the node-local NVMe copy (`DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813@scratch`), as vLLM already does.
- **Aggregate DEP8 c384 scheduling:** adopts the scheduling settings of the single-node SGLang EAGLE DEP8 recipe (`dsv4-fp4-b300-sglang-agentic-hicache-eagle`): `enable-mixed-chunk: true`, `schedule-policy: shortest-prefill-first`, `SGLANG_ENABLE_DP_SPEC_PREFILL_COORDINATION=1` and `prefill-decode-interval: 32` (was 20).
  - In run 39191181928 this point queued prefills behind decode: TTFT p50 33.5 s and p90 89 s, against 2.9 s and 12.7 s for the EAGLE standalone c384 point.
  - The gap came from these settings, not from Dynamo routing. About 96% of requests followed session affinity, and uncached prefill per DP rank was within ±3%. The DSpark standalone recipe this point was ported from has the same gap.
  - With mixed chunk, a step carries at most 8192 prefill tokens plus 96 one-token decodes per rank, within the existing `SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_MEGA_MOE_NUM_MAX_TOKENS_PER_RANK=8320`.
- **Recipe format:** the master config selects the recipes with `srt-recipe-dir` and `srt-recipe` (#3805), and the recipes are fragments without the keys the launcher binds (#3818), as on current `main`.

<details>
<summary>Settings removed or renamed since the 0916 image</summary>

Checked against the SGLang source at `7224fce1` and the Dynamo source at `b208989fbe`, then rechecked for the current image. Between SGLang `7224fce1` and `3c560089`, no arg or env var these recipes use was renamed, removed or given a new default. Between Dynamo `b208989fbe` and the bundled `1.6.0.dev20261018`, the Dynamo flags and env vars the recipes set, and the defaults cited below, are unchanged. Topology declarations (`tp-size`, `ep-size`, and `dp-size: 1` on TP points) are kept.

| Setting | Roles | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `SGLANG_OPT_SWA_SPLIT_LEAF_ON_INSERT`, `SGLANG_OPT_USE_JIT_NORM`, `SGLANG_OPT_USE_DEEPGEMM_MEGA_MOE`, `SGLANG_DSV4_MHC_PREWARM` | various | The image no longer reads them. `moe-a2a-backend: megamoe` selects Mega-MoE, and MHC prewarm always runs. |
| `SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_MEGA_MOE`, `NCCL_TIMEOUT` | disagg | Never defined: the first is a misspelling, and the second is not an NCCL variable. |
| `SGLANG_DEFAULT_THINKING`, `SGLANG_DSV4_REASONING_EFFORT`, `SGLANG_REQUEST_STATE_WAIT_TIMEOUT` | all, disagg | Only SGLang's own HTTP server reads them. Behind Dynamo, the frontend applies the chat template with thinking and reasoning effort taken from the request, and the worker calls the engine directly. |
| `SGLANG_RAGGED_VERIFY_MODE=static`, `SGLANG_JIT_DEEPGEMM_PRECOMPILE=1`, `SGLANG_OPT_UNIFIED_CACHE_FREE_OUT_OF_WINDOW_SLOTS=1`, `SGLANG_OPT_USE_CUSTOM_ALL_REDUCE_V2=1`, `SGLANG_OPT_USE_ONLINE_COMPRESS=0`, `SGLANG_OPT_USE_JIT_INDEXER_METADATA=1`, `SGLANG_OPT_USE_TOPK_V2=True` | various | Defaults on B300. |
| `attention-backend: dsv4`, `page-size: 256` | various | Set by SGLang's DeepSeek-V4 model override. |
| `speculative-num-steps: 1`, `speculative-eagle-topk: 1`, `speculative-num-draft-tokens: 7` | all | Derived by DSpark from `speculative-dspark-block-size: 6`, which also selects the golden acceptance length. |
| `swa-full-tokens-ratio: 0.1`, `hicache-write-policy: write_through` | TP agg | Defaults for this model. |
| `cuda-graph-max-bs-prefill` | disagg prefill | SGLang disables the prefill CUDA graph for DeepSeek-V4. |
| `disable-shared-experts-fusion` | agg DEP8 | DeepSeek-V4 only fuses shared experts into the routed weights when enforced. Mega-MoE's in-kernel fusion is controlled by `SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_MEGA_MOE_FUSE_SHARED_EXPERTS`, not by this flag. |
| `incremental-streaming-output`, `enable-cache-report` | agg DEP8, all | Dynamo always turns incremental streaming on. The cache report only affects SGLang's OpenAI server. |
| Frontend `active-decode-blocks-threshold`, `active-prefill-tokens-threshold`, `active-prefill-tokens-threshold-frac` set to `"None"` | frontend | Dynamo's router rejection thresholds are off by default. |
| `SGLANG_OPT_SWA_RELEASE_LEAF_LOCK_AFTER_WINDOW` → `SGLANG_OPT_RELEASE_PREFILL_SWA` | disagg | Renamed in the image. The new name defaults to off, so the setting is kept under the new name. |

</details>

<details>
<summary>Recipe details (carried over from #3631)</summary>

### Aggregate DEP8 c384

Ported from the single-node SGLang DEP8 c384 point (`dsv4-fp4-b300-sglang-agentic-hicache-mtp`, `benchmarks/single_node/srt-slurm-recipes/dsv4/sglang/b300-fp4-mtp/agentic.yaml`, `override_dep8_c384`):

- **Engine settings kept:** DP8 attention + EP8 Mega-MoE, FP4 indexer, DP LM head, local control broadcast, prefill delayer (interval now 32, see above), `stream-interval: 20`, `chunked-prefill-size: 65536` with `SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_MEGA_MOE_NUM_MAX_TOKENS_PER_RANK=8320`, `max-running-requests: 768` (96 per DP rank, twice concurrency), `mem-fraction-static: 0.88`, `swa-full-tokens-ratio: 0.075`, HiCache ratio 3 (`write_back`, `direct`, `page_first_direct`), DSpark K=6.
- **Decode graph limit:** `cuda-graph-max-bs-decode: 96`, the per-rank request cap (768 / 8).
- **Routing:** the Dynamo KV router replaces the SGLang router's DP-aware consistent hashing. Sessions stay sticky through `X-Dynamo-Session-ID`, and each DP rank publishes KV events (`kv-events-config`). The frontend sets `DYN_TCP_REQUEST_TIMEOUT: "60"`, as the disaggregated recipes do, so the c384 warmup burst does not exceed Dynamo's 5 s request-plane ack timeout.
- **Dropped:** settings that only apply to SGLang's own HTTP server and have no effect behind the Dynamo frontend: `tokenizer-worker-num`, tool-call and reasoning parsers, chat template, `skip-server-warmup`, `SGLANG_TIMEOUT_KEEP_ALIVE`.

### Gap-filling points: agg TP4 c8 and disagg 1P2D DEP8 c64

- **Agg TP4 c8:** the TP4 c4 recipe with `max-running-requests: 16` and `cuda-graph-max-bs-decode: 16`, plus a HiCache DRAM tier (`hicache-ratio: 2.75`, `write_through`, `direct`, `page_first_direct`), because TP4 c4 already fills about 60% of the GPU KV pool.
- **Disagg 1P2D DEP8 c64:** the 1P1D c64 recipe with a second decode worker (3 nodes), which halves each decode rank's load.

### NIXL instead of Mooncake

On AWS EFA, Mooncake needs the separate `mooncake-transfer-engine-efa-cuda13` wheel in place of the image's Mooncake package, which #3631 installed during container setup ([review](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/pull/3631#discussion_r4201491559)). NIXL ships its own LIBFABRIC plugin, and the EFA image provides the libfabric it needs, so these recipes drop that setup script, its waiver and the Mooncake-only settings (`MOONCAKE_PROTOCOL`, `MC_MS_FILTERS`, `WITH_NVIDIA_PEERMEM`). The NIXL LIBFABRIC settings come from #3597.

</details>

<details>
<summary>AI model disclosure</summary>

- Claude Opus 5.5 (`claude-opus-5-5`, via Claude Code), including delegated read-only sub-agents on the same model (two per image update, and one for the KV-transfer analysis):

## 摘要

新增 DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813 FP4 B300 Dynamo+SGLang AgentX 配方。配方沿用 #3631，分离式 KV 传输由 Mooncake 改为 NIXL，现运行于 `lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-efa-20261019-3c560089`。

- **测试点：**聚合式 TP8 c1、TP4 c4、TP4 c8（HiCache）与 DEP8 c384（HiCache）；分离式 1P1D DEP8 c64/c240 与 1P2D DEP8 c64（prefill 使用 HiCache）。拓扑、并发、缓存大小与显存比例均不变。
- **镜像：**以 2026-10-19 nightly 的 AWS EFA 变体 `nightly-dev-efa-20261019-3c560089`（sgl-project/sglang#41006）取代 `nightly-dev-20260916-c9a8fba9`。
  - 在 `nightly-dev-20261013-7224fce1` 上，分离式 worker 在 NIXL 启动时报错 `createBackend: unsupported backend 'LIBFABRIC'`。NIXL 1.5.0 的 LIBFABRIC 插件需要 libfabric 的 `FABRIC_1.7` 符号版本，而常规镜像只带有 Ubuntu 的 libfabric 1.17，最高只到 `FABRIC_1.6`。集群也已不再把宿主机的 libfabric 注入容器，因此没有更新的版本可用。
  - EFA 变体加入 AWS EFA 安装包 1.50.0（libfabric 2.6.0），并把 `/opt/amazon/efa/lib` 放在 `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` 最前。镜像构建时会检查 NIXL 插件是否从该目录解析 libfabric。
- **注意力 DP：**DEP8 worker 改用 `attn-dp-size: 8`，取代已被 sgl-project/sglang#41818 弃用的 `dp-size: 8` + `enable-dp-attention: true`。
- **Dynamo：**配方使用镜像自带的 Dynamo `1.6.0.dev20261018`（`dynamo.install: false`），主配置中的 router 版本也记为该版本。
  - 该版本包含 ai-dynamo/dynamo#16005，按 `attn_dp_size` 计算注意力 DP rank。在该版本 SGLang 中，两种 DP 写法都会解析为 `dp_size=1, attn_dp_size=8`。缺少该修复的 Dynamo 会为每个 DEP8 worker 只注册一个 DP rank，并且只订阅 rank 0 的 KV 事件，KV 路由器会把所有请求发往 DP rank 0。
  - 上一版本从源码构建 Dynamo `b208989fbe`，因为 1013 镜像自带的 `1.6.0.dev20261010` 早于该修复。
- **分离式 KV 传输：**使用 LIBFABRIC 后端的 NIXL（`SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_NIXL_BACKEND=LIBFABRIC`，EFA 镜像也默认设置该值）。镜像中的 NIXL 1.5.0 自带该插件，镜像也提供其所需的 libfabric，因此无需初始化脚本、豁免文件或软件包改动。
  - 两个分离式 worker 均设置 `FI_EFA_USE_UNSOLICITED_WRITE_RECV=0`。NIXL 的 LIBFABRIC 后端仅在基于 libfabric 2.3 及以上版本构建时才会关闭 EFA provider 的 unsolicited write recv。镜像中的 NIXL 并非如此（日志中从未出现 "Successfully disabled unsolicited write recv"），因此在镜像的 libfabric 2.6 下该功能保持开启。
  - 开启时，本 PR 上一次扫描（运行 39191181928 的 1P1D c240 两次尝试）中约 1.4% 的请求在 decode 端等待 900 秒后超时：prefill 已发出其 KV，但完成通知始终未到达 decode。每 GPU 吞吐由约 60k（0916 镜像）降至 44k tok/s。
- **需注意的镜像行为：**
  - 该版本 SGLang 默认把共享专家融合进 DeepGEMM Mega-MoE kernel（sgl-project/sglang#39313），因此 DEP8 吞吐与这些配方早先的结果相比，也可能因此有所不同。
  - EFA 镜像默认设置 `NCCL_NET_PLUGIN=ofi` 与 `NCCL_TUNER_PLUGIN=ofi`（aws-ofi-nccl 1.21.1）。这些配方中的每个 worker 都位于单个节点内。
- 所有配方均不启用 W4A4 MXFP4 Mega-MoE 路径。Prefill 与 decode 使用相同的 DSpark K=6 方法。
- 在 `b300-dsxe` 上，Dynamo+SGLang 从节点本地 NVMe 副本（`DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813@scratch`）加载 DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813，与 vLLM 现有做法相同。
- **聚合式 DEP8 c384 调度：**采用单节点 SGLang EAGLE DEP8 配方（`dsv4-fp4-b300-sglang-agentic-hicache-eagle`）的调度设置：`enable-mixed-chunk: true`、`schedule-policy: shortest-prefill-first`、`SGLANG_ENABLE_DP_SPEC_PREFILL_COORDINATION=1`，并将 `prefill-decode-interval` 由 20 改为 32。
  - 在运行 39191181928 中，该测试点的 prefill 排在 decode 之后：TTFT p50 为 33.5 秒、p90 为 89 秒，而 EAGLE 单机 c384 测试点为 2.9 秒与 12.7 秒。
  - 差距来自上述设置，而非 Dynamo 路由：约 96% 的请求按会话亲和路由，各 DP rank 的未缓存 prefill 量相差不超过 ±3%。该测试点所移植的 DSpark 单机配方也有同样的差距。
  - 启用 mixed chunk 后，每个 rank 每步最多包含 8192 个 prefill token 与 96 个单 token decode，仍在现有 `SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_MEGA_MOE_NUM_MAX_TOKENS_PER_RANK=8320` 之内。
- **配方格式：**与当前 `main` 一致，主配置使用 `srt-recipe-dir` 与 `srt-recipe` 选择配方（#3805），配方为片段形式，不含由启动器绑定的键（#3818）。

### 自 0916 镜像以来删除或重命名的设置

均已对照 SGLang `7224fce1` 与 Dynamo `b208989fbe` 源码核实，并针对当前镜像重新核对。在 SGLang `7224fce1` 与 `3c560089` 之间，这些配方使用的参数与环境变量均未重命名、删除或改变默认值。在 Dynamo `b208989fbe` 与镜像自带的 `1.6.0.dev20261018` 之间，配方设置的 Dynamo 参数与环境变量以及下文引用的默认值均无变化。拓扑声明（`tp-size`、`ep-size` 以及 TP 测试点上的 `dp-size: 1`）予以保留。

- 镜像已不再读取：`SGLANG_OPT_SWA_SPLIT_LEAF_ON_INSERT`、`SGLANG_OPT_USE_JIT_NORM`、`SGLANG_OPT_USE_DEEPGEMM_MEGA_MOE`、`SGLANG_DSV4_MHC_PREWARM`。Mega-MoE 由 `moe-a2a-backend: megamoe` 选择，MHC 预热始终执行。
- 从未定义：`SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_MEGA_MOE`（拼写错误）与 `NCCL_TIMEOUT`（并非 NCCL 变量）。
- 仅 SGLang 自身 HTTP 服务端读取：`SGLANG_DEFAULT_THINKING`、`SGLANG_DSV4_REASONING_EFFORT`、`SGLANG_REQUEST_STATE_WAIT_TIMEOUT`。在 Dynamo 之后，前端按请求中的思考模式与推理强度套用聊天模板，worker 直接调用引擎。
- B300 上的默认值：`SGLANG_RAGGED_VERIFY_MODE=static`、`SGLANG_JIT_DEEPGEMM_PRECOMPILE=1`、`SGLANG_OPT_UNIFIED_CACHE_FREE_OUT_OF_WINDOW_SLOTS=1`、`SGLANG_OPT_USE_CUSTOM_ALL_REDUCE_V2=1`、`SGLANG_OPT_USE_ONLINE_COMPRESS=0`、`SGLANG_OPT_USE_JIT_INDEXER_METADATA=1`、`SGLANG_OPT_USE_TOPK_V2=True`。
- 由 SGLang 的 DeepSeek-V4 模型覆盖设置：`attention-backend: dsv4`、`page-size: 256`。
- 由 DSpark 根据 `speculative-dspark-block-size: 6` 推导：`speculative-num-steps: 1`、`speculative-eagle-topk: 1`、`speculative-num-draft-tokens: 7`。golden 接受长度同样由 block size 选择。
- 该模型的默认值：TP 聚合配方中的 `swa-full-tokens-ratio: 0.1` 与 `hicache-write-policy: write_through`。
- SGLang 对 DeepSeek-V4 关闭 prefill CUDA graph：`cuda-graph-max-bs-prefill`。
- `disable-shared-experts-fusion`：DeepSeek-V4 仅在强制时才把共享专家融合进路由专家权重；Mega-MoE 的 kernel 内融合由 `SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_MEGA_MOE_FUSE_SHARED_EXPERTS` 控制，而非此参数。
- `incremental-streaming-output` 由 Dynamo 强制开启；`enable-cache-report` 只影响 SGLang 的 OpenAI 服务端。
- 前端设为 `"None"` 的 `active-decode-blocks-threshold`、`active-prefill-tokens-threshold`、`active-prefill-tokens-threshold-frac`：Dynamo 路由拒绝阈值默认关闭。
- `SGLANG_OPT_SWA_RELEASE_LEAF_LOCK_AFTER_WINDOW` 在镜像中重命名为 `SGLANG_OPT_RELEASE_PREFILL_SWA`。新名称默认关闭，因此以新名称保留该设置。

### 配方细节（沿用自 #3631）

**聚合式 DEP8 c384**：移植自单节点 SGLang DEP8 c384 测试点（`dsv4-fp4-b300-sglang-agentic-hicache-mtp`，`benchmarks/single_node/srt-slurm-recipes/dsv4/sglang/b300-fp4-mtp/agentic.yaml`，`override_dep8_c384`）。

- **保留的引擎设置：**DP8 注意力 + EP8 Mega-MoE、FP4 indexer、DP LM head、local control broadcast、prefill delayer（间隔现为 32，见上文）、`stream-interval: 20`、`chunked-prefill-size: 65536` 配合 `SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_MEGA_MOE_NUM_MAX_TOKENS_PER_RANK=8320`、`max-running-requests: 768`（每个 DP rank 96，为并发数两倍）、`mem-fraction-static: 0.88`、`swa-full-tokens-ratio: 0.075`、HiCache 比例 3（`write_back`、`direct`、`page_first_direct`）、DSpark K=6。
- **Decode CUDA graph 上限：**`cuda-graph-max-bs-decode: 96`，即每个 rank 的请求上限（768 / 8）。
- **路由：**以 Dynamo KV 路由器取代 SGLang 路由器的 DP 感知一致性哈希。会话通过 `X-Dynamo-Session-ID` 保持亲和，各 DP rank 发布 KV 事件（`kv-events-config`）。前端与分离式配方一样设置 `DYN_TCP_REQUEST_TIMEOUT: "60"`，避免 c384 预热突发请求超过 Dynamo 请求平面默认 5 秒的确认超时。
- **移除：**仅适用于 SGLang 自身 HTTP 服务端、在 Dynamo 前端之后不起作用的设置：`tokenizer-worker-num`、工具调用与推理解析器、聊天模板、`skip-server-warmup`、`SGLANG_TIMEOUT_KEEP_ALIVE`。

**补充测试点：**

- **聚合式 TP4 c8：**基于 TP4 c4 配方，`max-running-requests: 16`、`cuda-graph-max-bs-decode: 16`，并增加 HiCache DRAM 层（`hicache-ratio: 2.75`、`write_through`、`direct`、`page_first_direct`），因为 TP4 c4 已占用约 60% 的 GPU KV 池。
- **分离式 1P2D DEP8 c64：**即 1P1D c64 配方增加第二个 decode worker（共 3 个节点），使每个 decode rank 的负载减半。

**以 NIXL 取代 Mooncake：**在 AWS EFA 上，Mooncake 需要用单独的 `mooncake-transfer-engine-efa-cuda13` wheel 替换镜像自带的 Mooncake 包，#3631 在容器初始化时完成这一替换（[review](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/pull/3631#discussion_r4201491559)）。NIXL 自带 LIBFABRIC 插件，EFA 镜像也提供其所需的 libfabric，因此这些配方移除了该初始化脚本、其豁免文件以及仅供 Mooncake 使用的设置（`MOONCAKE_PROTOCOL`、`MC_MS_FILTERS`、`WITH_NVIDIA_PEERMEM`）。NIXL LIBFABRIC 设置来自 #3597。

### AI 模型披露

- Claude Opus 5.5（`claude-opus-5-5`，通过 Claude Code），包括使用同一模型的只读委派子代理（每次镜像更新各两个，另有一个用于 KV 传输分析）：
  - **最新更新：**根据运行日志及 SGLang、NIXL、libfabric 源码诊断 c240 KV 传输超时与 DEP8 c384 的 TTFT 差距；在分离式 worker 上设置 `FI_EFA_USE_UNSOLICITED_WRITE_RECV=0`；为 DEP8 c384 采用 EAGLE 配方的调度设置；合并 `main`；更新变更日志条目与本说明。
  - **EFA 镜像更新：**合并最新 `main`，并改用其 `srt-recipe` 选择方式与片段格式；对照 SGLang `3c560089` 与镜像自带的 Dynamo 审查配方参数与环境变量；检查 EFA 镜像中的 libfabric、NIXL 插件与 Dynamo；将配方迁移到 `nightly-dev-efa-20261019-3c560089` 及其自带的 Dynamo；更新变更日志条目与本说明。
  - **1013 镜像更新：**合并 `main`；对照 SGLang `7224fce1` 以及镜像自带与固定版本的 Dynamo 源码审查所有配方参数与环境变量；将配方迁移到 `nightly-dev-20261013-7224fce1`；DEP8 worker 改用 `attn-dp-size`；固定 Dynamo 版本；删除或重命名相关设置。
  - **此前：**将 #3631 的提交 rebase 到 `main`，将分离式配方由 Mooncake 切换为 NIXL，并移除 Mooncake 初始化脚本与豁免文件。
- 沿用自 #3631 的提交：
  - GPT-5（Codex，包括一个委派代理）：最初提交与 Mooncake 配置。
  - GPT-6（Codex）：诊断并准备了前序运行时修复。
  - Claude Opus 5.5：DeepGEMM 快速预热与节点本地权重路径修复、聚合式 DEP8 c384 配方、TP4 c8 与 1P2D c64 测试点，以及本 PR 移除的 Mooncake 豁免文件。

title: [AMD] Enable triton DSA backends and top-k v2 path for glm5.2-fp4 in MI355X
body:
## Summary
- `--dsa-prefill-backend` / `--dsa-decode-backend`: `tilelang` → `triton` (requires sgl-project/sglang PR #30575, commit `8a6ab89bf0b90304b3b454a833fcdcaefb777c29`)
- `lmsysorg/sglang-rocm:v0.5.16-rocm720-mi35x-20260728` → `lmsysorg/sglang-rocm:v0.5.19-rocm10-mi35x-20260910`
- `SGLANG_OPT_USE_TOPK_V2`: `false` → `true` (sgl-project/sglang PR #36684, PR #36851 add the gfx950 path) No impact on performance because upstream SGLang already enable

Model, runner, and search space (TP4/EP4 HiCache vs TP8/EP1 GPU-resident arms), MTP speculative decoding with the committed golden acceptance length, and the concurrency grids are unchanged.

Unofficial local, MI355X TP4/EP4. Baseline is the `v0.5.19-rocm10-mi35x-20260908` image-only bump from #2917, not the CI curve. Δ = this PR / 0908 baseline (higher is better).


| conc | 0908 tput | this PR tput | Δ tput | 0908 intvty | this PR intvty | Δ intvty |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 3410.7 | 3659.4 | +7.3% | 152.8 | 166.4 | +8.9% |
| 2 | 3854.9 | 4032.8 | +4.6% | 120.2 | 135.8 | +12.9% |
| 4 | 5746.1 | 5989.9 | +4.2% | 122.9 | 125.3 | +2.0% |
| 8 | 10127.5 | 10571.9 | +4.4% | 75.5 | 87.4 | +15.8% |
| **10** | **12982.8** | **13099.8** | **+0.9%** | **64.1** | **71.6** | **+11.7%** |
| 12 | 12344.9 | 12875.7 | +4.3% | 57.5 | 67.8 | +17.9% |
| 16 | 10888.2 | 11599.8 | +6.5% | 23.3 | 24.9 | +6.8% |

No regression at any concurrency: throughput is +0.9% to +7.3% (mean +4.6%) and P90 interactivity +2.0% to +17.9% (mean +10.9%). The headline conc 10 point is throughput-neutral (+0.9%) and buys +11.7% on the interactivity tail, which is the shape you would expect if the change is mostly a decode-path win rather than a prefill one — at 90-210k input against a few hundred output tokens these points are overwhelmingly prefill-bound, so per-chip throughput barely moves while TPOT does.

The delta is not attributable to one switch. Top-k v2, the triton DSA backends, and a two-day image delta (0908 → 0910) all sit between the two columns; the sweep measures their sum, which is what the recipe ships.


## Test plan
- [x] `validate_perf_changelog.py` against `upstream/main`
- [ ] Single-arm smoke at TP4 conc 1 on the 0910 image (server starts, `--dsa-*-backend triton` accepted, no decode-time memory fault)
- [ ] Full AgentX sweep (`full-sweep-fail-fast`)
- [ ] Accuracy / eval run unchanged versus the 0908 baseline

## Risk

Low-to-moderate. This is a benchmark recipe change with no application logic, but unlike a pure image bump it flips three coupled switches at once: the top-k v2 kernel, the DSA prefill/decode backends, and the container. If the sweep regresses or crashes, bisect in that order — the DSA backend switch is the most likely culprit, since the previous attempt to move ROCm DSA decode off the default hit a GPU memory fault in the a8w8 qseqlen1 persistent kernel.

The `v0.5.19-rocm10-mi35x-20260910` tag uses a `rocm10` segment rather than the `rocm720` naming every other MI355X image in `configs/amd-master.yaml` carries; worth a reviewer confirming that is the intended tag family.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Benchmark-only, but it couples a container bump with DSA backend and kernel-path switches where prior ROCm DSA decode changes caused GPU faults; wrong image tag or silent fallback would skew CI sweeps.
> 
> **Overview**
> Updates the **GLM-5.2 FP4 MI355X SGLang agentic-MTP** benchmark recipe to align with newer upstream SGLang ROCm support, without changing TP/EP arms, HiCache sizing, MTP settings, or concurrency grids.
> 
> In `glm5.2_fp4_mi355x_sglang_mtp.sh`, **`SGLANG_OPT_USE_TOPK_V2`** flips from `false` to `true` now that gfx950 can use the fused DSA top-k v2 path (upstream PRs #36684 / #36851). **`--dsa-prefill-backend`** and **`--dsa-decode-backend`** move from `tilelang` to **`triton`**, which requires SGLang at or past PR #30575.
> 
> `configs/amd-master.yaml` bumps the pinned image from **`v0.5.16-rocm720-mi35x-20260728`** to **`v0.5.19-rocm10-mi35x-20260910`** so startup accepts the triton DSA flags and ships the ROCm top-k v2 build. **`perf-changelog.yaml`** records the same rationale for `glm5.2-fp4-mi355x-sglang-agentic-mtp`.
>

DeepEP V2.5 introduces dedicated communication buffers for EP, PP, Engram, and bucket collectives, together with new primitives for redundant-expert load balancing. GPU kernels are now compiled through DeepJIT, while installation builds the host C++ extension.
This release also fully removes V1 and its NVSHMEM dependency.
New Features
Dedicated buffer APIs
@LyricZhao
Split ElasticBuffer into EPBuffer, EngramBuffer, PPBuffer, and BucketBuffer, sharing the BufferBase lifecycle.
Add BufferAllocator for planning symmetric tensor allocations before buffer construction.
Expert load balancing
@cqzhangyu
@LyricZhao
Add EPBuffer.lb_prefetch_weights to transfer expert weights and quantization scales to redundant expert slots over NVLink.
Add EPBuffer.lb_reduce_grads to accumulate redundant experts’ FP32 gradients into the original experts.
These primitives support the dynamic expert-replication approach explored by MoonEP and UltraEP. Replication planning and token rerouting are supplied by the integrating framework.
Bucket collectives for CP and DP
@jason-huang03
@bucket-xv
@cqzhangyu
@dromniscience
@sphish
Batched all-gather, reduce-scatter, and all-reduce across NVLink, RDMA, and hybrid domains.
Sessions for communicating ordinary PyTorch tensors through temporary bucket storage.
EP improvements
@LyricZhao
Deferred dispatch/combine epilogues for communication-computation overlap.
Cached expanded layouts and zero padding between experts.
Engram
@tianr22
@sphish
Multi-layer storage on GPU or CPU, with one completion hook per layer.
Build and runtime
@LyricZhao
Move GPU kernel compilation to DeepJIT.
Remove installation-time NVCC compilation and GPU architecture selection.
Notes
Migrate from ElasticBuffer to the dedicated buffer APIs.
V1 APIs, legacy documentation, and NVSHMEM support have been removed.
Bucket collectives, Engram, and PP remain experimental.
Requires NVIDIA Hopper or newer GPUs, CUDA 13.1+, NCCL 2.32.3+, PyTorch 2.10+ with CUDA support, Python 3.10+, and a C++20 compiler.
