title: EmuGEMM: Fused Tensor Core Kernels for Precision Emulation in Matrix Multiplication
body: Modern GPUs devote an increasing silicon budget to low-precision matrix-multiplication units, widening the precision-throughput gap for scientific computing workloads. Ozaki Schemes I and II offer an alternative by reconstructing high-precision general matrix multiplication (GEMM) from low-precision operations, yet existing implementations leave substantial performance untapped. In particular, intermediate results are repeatedly materialized in global memory, making data movement the dominant bottleneck. We present EmuGEMM, fused integer Tensor Core kernels for NVIDIA Hopper and Blackwell GPUs that eliminate redundant memory round-trips in both Ozaki schemes. Using Scheme I, EmuGEMM sustains up to 1,639 Top/s on Hopper (83% of INT8 peak) and 3,654 Top/s on Blackwell (81%). For large matrices, EmuGEMM surpasses cuBLAS TF32 throughput by up to 1.4x on Hopper and 1.7x on Blackwell, at comparable accuracy. Using Scheme II, EmuGEMM extends to complex arithmetic and outperforms cuBLAS ZGEMM by up to 2.3x on Hopper and 5.5x on Blackwell.

title: Demystifying ARM SME to Optimize General Matrix Multiplications
body: General Matrix Multiplication (GEMM) is a critical kernel in high-performance computing and deep learning. While modern architectures like ARM's Scalable Matrix Extension (SME) introduce dedicated hardware for matrix operations, existing linear algebra libraries fail to fully exploit its potential, particularly for large matrices. This paper presents MpGEMM, an open-source library that leverages key architectural features of SME to optimize GEMM across multiple precisions. Through a systematic characterization of SME, we derive optimization guidelines that inform our design. MpGEMM employs cache-aware partitioning, efficient data packing with on-the-fly transposition, and specialized micro-kernels that utilize multi-vector loads and all available tile registers. Evaluated on an Apple M4 Pro with real-world workloads from DeepSeek and LLaMA, MpGEMM achieves an average speedup of 1.23x over the vendor-optimized Apple Accelerate library and significantly outperforms other open-source alternatives.

title: NeuPIMs: NPU-PIM Heterogeneous Acceleration for Batched LLM Inferencing
body:
Modern transformer-based Large Language Models (LLMs) are constructed with a
series of decoder blocks. Each block comprises three key components: (1) QKV
generation, (2) multi-head attention, and (3) feed-forward networks. In batched
processing, QKV generation and feed-forward networks involve compute-intensive
matrix-matrix multiplications (GEMM), while multi-head attention requires
bandwidth-heavy matrix-vector multiplications (GEMV). Machine learning
accelerators like TPUs or NPUs are proficient in handling GEMM but are less
efficient for GEMV computations. Conversely, Processing-in-Memory (PIM)
technology is tailored for efficient GEMV computation, while it lacks the
computational power to handle GEMM effectively. Inspired by this insight, we
propose NeuPIMs, a heterogeneous acceleration system that jointly exploits a
conventional GEMM-focused NPU and GEMV-optimized PIM devices. The main
challenge in efficiently integrating NPU and PIM lies in enabling concurrent
operations on both platforms, each addressing a specific kernel type. First,
existing PIMs typically operate in a "blocked" mode, allowing only either NPU
or PIM to be active at any given time. Second, the inherent dependencies
between GEMM and GEMV in LLMs restrict their parallel processing. To tackle
these challenges, NeuPIMs is equipped with dual row buffers in each bank,
facilitating the simultaneous management of memory read/write operations and
PIM commands. Further, NeuPIMs employs a runtime sub-batch interleaving
technique to maximize concurrent execution, leveraging batch parallelism to
allow two independent sub-batches to be pipelined within a single NeuPIMs
device. Our evaluation demonstrates that compared to GPU-only, NPU-only, and a
na\"ive NPU+PIM integrated acceleration approaches, NeuPIMs achieves 3times,
2.4times and 1.6times throughput improvement, respectively.

title: feat(klaud): pause a model on hardware after missing weights / feat(klaud): 权重缺失后暂停该硬件上的模型
body:
Found while monitoring [run 38919417043](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/38919417043): 2 of its 5 candidates ended `readiness-blocked` because the DeepSeek-R1 checkpoint is not staged (#4191: `DeepSeek-R1-0528-NVFP4-v2` on b200-nscale; #4188: `/mnt/numa1/models/DeepSeek-R1-0528` on gb200-nv). That is not new. 24 Klaud PRs in the last week (#3848 … #4191) were readiness-blocked on DSR1 B200 families. The ones I checked (#4130, #4135, #4191) each used a GPU run to hit the same missing checkpoint [INFERENCE: the rest likely did too]. This repeats because cooldown is per candidate (family + image) and every new family or image counted as untried.

- **Reason code:** `CandidateOutcome` accepts `reason-code: weights-missing`, only together with `readiness-blocked`. Baseline codes still require `failed@baseline`. The prompt asks for it when the checkpoint itself is missing on the target cluster.
- **Planner:** while reading recent outcomes, any `weights-missing` candidate's source `(model, precision, hardware)` is looked up in that wave's `klaud-plan` `candidates.json`. The planner then skips every candidate with the same triple for the cooldown window (24h, the existing `cooldown_hours`). Precision is part of the key, since FP4 and FP8 use different checkpoints.
- **Unchanged:** other readiness blocks (image pulls, mounts) still cool down only their own candidate.

Tests: the cooldown test adds a `weights-missing` candidate next to an ordinary `readiness-blocked` one and checks that only the former blocks its triple. A new test checks which reason codes pair with which outcomes. Each of 4 mutations fails a test.

The real fix is to stage the checkpoints (on the infra list). This only stops Klaud from paying for the same discovery several times a day.

<details>
<summary>中文</summary>

在监控 [run 38919417043](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/38919417043) 时发现：5 个候选中有 2 个因 DeepSeek-R1 检查点未暂存而以 `readiness-blocked` 结束（#4191：b200-nscale 上的 `DeepSeek-R1-0528-NVFP4-v2`；#4188：gb200-nv 上的 `/mnt/numa1/models/DeepSeek-R1-0528`）。这并非新问题：过去一周有 24 个 Klaud PR（#3848 … #4191）在 DSR1 B200 配置族上被 readiness-blocked；我检查过的（#4130、#4135、#4191）都花了一次 GPU 运行撞上同一个缺失的检查点（其余推测相同）。这会反复发生，因为冷却以候选（配置族 + 镜像）为单位，每个新的配置族或镜像都被视为未尝试。

- **原因代码：** `CandidateOutcome` 接受 `reason-code: weights-missing`，且只能与 `readiness-blocked` 搭配；基线代码仍要求 `failed@baseline`。提示词要求在目标集群上缺少检查点本身时使用它。
- **规划器：** 读取近期结果时，会在该轮 `klaud-plan` 的 `candidates.json` 中查找 `weights-missing` 候选的来源 `(model, precision, hardware)`，并在冷却窗口内（24 小时，即现有的 `cooldown_hours`）跳过三元组相同的所有候选。精度是键的一部分，因为 FP4 与 FP8 使用不同的检查点。
- **不变：** 其他就绪问题（镜像拉取、挂载）仍只冷却其自身的候选。

测试：冷却测试新增一个 `weights-missing` 候选与一个普通 `readiness-blocked` 候选，确认只有前者阻止其三元组；新测试检查原因代码与结果的搭配。4 种变异各自使测试失败。

根本解决办法是暂存这些检查点（已在基础设施清单中）；本 PR 只是避免 Klaud 每天多次为同一发现付出代价。

</details>

<summary>AI model disclosure</summary>

Prepared with `anthropic/claude-opus-5-5`, which investigated the run, made the change and tests, and drafted this description. No delegated agents were used.

</details>

title: Add Kimi K3 B300 EFA AgentX sweep / 新增 Kimi K3 B300 EFA AgentX 扫描
body:
**Host freezes: trigger isolated to degraded EFA devices on long-running nodes.** A standalone Mooncake-over-EFA reproducer (no vLLM or NIXL; production store config: 8 ranks/node, 160 GB THP segments, GPU buffer registered with EFA) froze every node that had run since Oct 6-14 (3/3, within 30 s to 5 min of traffic) and none of the rebooted nodes (0/7), with either the CUDA VMM or the `cudaMalloc` allocator; a sweep job also froze node 09. Every long-running node checked reports `reg_mr_err=46` on each EFA device from earlier registration failures; rebooted nodes report none, and the current workload creates none. Those nodes are excluded until operators reboot them, and the setup script refuses any node whose EFA devices report failed registrations. Disaggregated jobs no longer requeue (one hung job previously moved across four node sets). The disaggregated workers also drop `enable-cumem-allocator` and set `NCCL_CUMEM_ENABLE=0`, since Mooncake moved ~2 GB/s per rank into VMM buffers versus 14-27 GB/s into `cudaMalloc` buffers on healthy nodes. The setup script installs the pinned `aiconfigurator-core` wheel, verified against its published SHA256, before Dynamo's source install pulls its intermittently failing placeholder package.

Bring the Kimi K3 DSpark AgentX search space from #4047 to B300: ten DCP disaggregated points and three low-latency aggregate points, with one eight-GPU node per DCP8 worker.

Use EFA for NIXL and Mooncake, preserving the model, concurrency matrix, golden acceptance selection and eval coverage. The setup builds a pinned THP-enabled Mooncake client with host-chunk collapse and backports upstream libfabric CUDA VMM synchronization fixes. It also adds a default-on opt-out for vLLM's NVLink-only latent-MoE tail. These serving-stack changes require a patch waiver.

The two-node TP16 point uses stock decode and portable collectives, with custom allreduce, GEMM-AR and the fused latent-MoE tail disabled. These fused paths require GPU multicast across the TP group, which is unavailable across EFA-connected nodes. Single-node TP8 points retain their fused paths.

The [current sweep](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/39258024329) has passed all three aggregate benchmarks and their tool-schema evals; **the full sweep is not yet green**. The 2P3D c192 job failed before serving because two workers downloaded an `aiconfigurator-core` wheel that failed its published SHA256 check; this is being treated as a transient installation failure pending retry, with no installer change or checksum bypass. The registration fix passes local full-model Dynamo prefill startup and fresh-image wheel validation at unchanged capacity; the public disaggregated path remains unverified. A scheduler exclusion avoids a node with a separately reproduced pre-container task-launch failure.

<details><summary>Validation details</summary>

Current-head results, with one-hour profiling submission windows and unchanged native result and power gates:

| Configuration | GPUs | Total TPS/GPU | P90 ITL | P90 TTFT | Valid profiled requests | Tool eval |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| TP8/DCP8 c2 | 8 | 2,681.25 | 3.43 ms | 1.32678 s | 417 | 403/408 |
| TP8/DCP8 c4 | 8 | 4,028.18 | 4.87 ms | 1.60057 s | 621 | 404/408 |
| TP16/DCP16 c1 | 16 | 568.12 | 12.83 ms | 1.88693 s | 177 | 401/408 |

All three power bundles report valid coverage and package integrity, with no validation failures. Native content validation excluded one, three and one profiling records, respectively. The c2 job also cancelled one outstanding request after its end-of-window grace deadline; it still passed the native gate. The TP16 runtime config confirms the portable fallback was used.

Tool eval residual failures concern generated tool calls or arguments, not API/backend rejection. These evals use no Mooncake connector and do not establish external-cache correctness. In an earlier [sweep](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/39216083365), the same 1P2D GSM8K configuration completed with 97.35% strict-match accuracy over 1,319 questions.

A local DCP8 1P1D stability run completed one hour of AgentX profiling with 4,517 valid requests, zero profiling errors and successful result validation. It used real acceptance and is not a controlled performance comparison against the synthetic-acceptance sweep. The local TP16 checks establish serving functionality, not completed benchmark or accuracy validation.

The host-collapse fix passes an eight-client mixed-backing registration reproducer and full-model Dynamo prefill startup with all eight 160 GiB mappings fully huge-page-backed. A fresh-image build installed `0.3.13.post1+gc3fa13ec.collapse1`; its separate 8 GiB Store sanity check passed a 5,632-byte put/get. Cross-node 8 MiB GPU-to-host WRITE, host-to-GPU READ and GPU-to-GPU READ also passed with CUDA VMM enabled and aligned 8 GiB host regions. These local checks do not establish full disaggregated sweep completion.

</details>

<details><summary>中文</summary>

**主机冻结：触发条件定位为长时间运行节点上已退化的 EFA 设备。** 独立的 Mooncake-over-EFA 复现程序（不含 vLLM 和 NIXL，采用生产配置：每节点 8 个 rank、160 GB THP 段、GPU 缓冲区注册到 EFA）使所有自 10 月 6–14 日以来未重启的节点冻结（3/3，流量开始后 30 秒至 5 分钟），而重启过的节点均未冻结（0/7），与使用 CUDA VMM 还是 `cudaMalloc` 无关；一个扫描作业也导致节点 09 冻结。所检查的长时间运行节点的每个 EFA 设备都记录了 `reg_mr_err=46`（来自早期的内存注册失败）；重启过的节点为 0，当前负载也不会产生新的注册失败。在运维重启前排除这些节点，启动脚本也会拒绝任何 EFA 设备存在注册失败记录的节点。分离式作业不再自动重新排队（此前一个挂起的作业曾辗转四组节点）。分离式 worker 去掉 `enable-cumem-allocator` 并设置 `NCCL_CUMEM_ENABLE=0`，因为在健康节点上 Mooncake 写入 VMM 缓冲区每 rank 仅约 2 GB/s，写入 `cudaMalloc` 缓冲区则为 14–27 GB/s。启动脚本在 Dynamo 源码安装前，先安装经官方 SHA256 校验的固定版本 `aiconfigurator-core` wheel，避免其占位包间歇性下载失败。

将 #4047 的 Kimi K3 DSpark AgentX 配置空间移植到 B300：包含十个 DCP 分离式推理性能点和三个低延迟聚合式推理性能点，每个 DCP8 worker 使用一个八卡节点。

NIXL 和 Mooncake 使用 EFA，保持模型、并发矩阵、标准合成接受率选择和评估覆盖范围不变。启动脚本构建支持 THP 和主机内存块折叠的固定版本 Mooncake，并回移 libfabric 上游的 CUDA VMM 同步修复；另外为 vLLM 依赖 NVLink 的 latent-MoE tail 增加默认开启的开关。这些推理栈修改需要补丁豁免。

双节点 TP16 配置使用常规解码和可跨节点使用的集合通信，关闭 custom allreduce、GEMM-AR 和融合 latent-MoE tail。这些融合路径依赖 TP 组内 GPU 多播，而 EFA 连接的节点间不支持该能力。单节点 TP8 配置保留融合路径。

新一轮扫描的三个聚合式性能测试均已通过原有结果和功耗验证：TP8 c2 为 2,681.25 TPS/GPU，TP8 c4 为 4,028.18 TPS/GPU，TP16 c1 为 568.12 TPS/GPU；工具调用评估分别为 403/408、404/408 和 401/408。原有内容校验分别排除了一、三、一条 profiling 记录；c2 在测量窗口结束后的宽限期截止时取消了一条未完成请求，仍通过原有门槛。2P3D c192 在服务启动前失败，原因是两个 worker 下载的 `aiconfigurator-core` 软件包未通过官方 SHA256 校验；暂按偶发安装失败处理，等待重试，不修改安装流程或绕过校验。完整扫描尚未全部通过，公开分离式推理路径仍待验证。调度排除规则已避开可独立复现容器启动前任务创建失败的故障节点；内存注册修复已通过本地完整模型 Dynamo prefill 启动和全新镜像的软件包验证，缓存容量与评估要求未降低。

</details>

body:
## Changes

`dsv41flash-fp4-mi355x-vllm-agentic-dspark`:

- Repin the image to `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100-0cbac6cd1305f710e12193596b27488397bcb205`, in both the recipe and `amd-master.yaml`.

Every other serving and benchmark setting is unchanged from [#3571](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/pull/3571). This PR also appends one `perf-changelog.yaml` entry and updates the English and Chinese configuration guides.

## INT4 quick reduce in the GSM8K eval

The single eval row (TP4, concurrency 64) runs on a server started from this recipe, so the role `env` applies to it.

Quick reduce only takes tensors above a size threshold. At TP4 that threshold is 2 MiB, or 205 tokens of BF16 hidden size 5120. Prefill chunks (8192–16384 tokens) and c64 decode steps (64 × (1+5) = 384 tokens) are above it, so the eval exercises INT4 in both phases.

**Runtime check:** in the eval job's engine log, `Using [...] all-reduce backends (in dispatch order)` must list `QUICK_REDUCE` before `AITER_CUSTOM`/`CUSTOM`. Compare GSM8K against the #3571 baseline of 0.9712 strict.

## Summary

Document and exercise the lifetime contract of **ordinary independently allocated receive outputs** from compact `dispatch(do_cpu_sync=False)`.

- Add a README paragraph explaining valid receive prefixes, output ownership versus stream readiness, the explicit ready-event/`record_stream` handoff, and why a prefix view retains the full capacity allocation.
- Add a 166-line standalone native regression for saved-view backward after later dispatches and delayed cross-stream consumers under allocator pressure.

No production Python/C++/CUDA implementation, default, or API changes. The internal dispatch copy epilogue still runs. This is not borrowed communication-buffer storage or a zero-copy dispatch implementation.

## Regression coverage

The new `tests/ep/test_recv_lifetime.py` uses the independent NCCL dispatch reference and requires bitwise equality of payloads, local expert indices, routing weights, source-token metadata, and the saved-activation weight gradient.

Each process run covers:

- Deterministic dispatch off/on; output allocation on the compute/communication stream.
- Uneven inputs, balanced routes, masked routes, and highly skewed routing with empty receivers.
- Two selected experts on the same destination rank, distinguishing unique receive rows from token/expert assignments.
- A prefix saved with `ctx.save_for_backward`, followed by three additional dispatches through the same buffer before backward.
- A delayed reader on another stream, dropping the original receive allocation references and allocating/filling four same-capacity tensors on the allocation stream. The copy destination and allocator warm-up are prepared before the delay. Pressure writes must finish while a **pre-read** event is still pending; a pending post-copy event alone is insufficient.

Scheduling can miss the pressure window. All ranks agree on numerical correctness and window validity, then retry in collective lockstep with a longer delay (at most three attempts). Actual corruption fails immediately; an inconclusive window is never silently reported as coverage.

The consumer handoff uses a CUDA event captured **after the first dispatch-event wait**, including its deterministic-sort hook. It does not depend on repeated waits on the original `EventOverlap`; that is separate from this lifetime coverage.

## Validation

### Current polished revision

Head: `97fa6d18ff717df99acbdbb862325bda3d4a0d46`, based on public main `b5a33eefda39485f438dc764695b71ba7b9249b6`.

The current 166-line test passed on H200 with PyTorch `2.13.0+cu132`, CUDA 13.2 and NCCL 2.32.3. Each native lifetime policy was run once with eight ranks: 24 distributed saved-prefix/backward cases in total, with 24 valid delayed-consumer allocator-pressure windows. This is positive coverage of the current reorganized test; the historical negative and scheduling controls below were not rerun against this revision.

```bash
EP_AVOID_RECORD_STREAM=0 python tests/ep/test_recv_lifetime.py --num-processes 8 --num-tokens 64 --hidden 512
EP_AVOID_RECORD_STREAM=1 python tests/ep/test_recv_lifetime.py --num-processes 8 --num-tokens 64 --hidden 512
```

### Historical validation of the earlier test version

Tested commit: `01c31d0d75f155ca00ba933a6b9ab7a01459169e`, based on upstream `93eb6eb238127e96c6d7a4a625a6dad158348509`. The results in this subsection belong to that earlier test version, not to a rerun of the current 166-line test.

One node, eight NVIDIA H200 GPUs in a single NVLink domain; PyTorch `2.13.0+cu132`, CUDA runtime 13.2, loaded NCCL 2.32.3. The unchanged upstream native extension and the tested source archive/test-file hashes were verified. No borrowed-view implementation or event-wrapper patch was included.

Both native lifetime policies were run in fresh processes, three repeats each, using the same two command lines above.

Validation controls: `EP_DISABLE_GIN=1`, `EP_REUSE_NCCL_COMM=0`, `EP_BUFFER_DEBUG=0`, `NCCL_NET_PLUGIN=none`, `CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG=:4096:8`. Seed 42; deterministic PyTorch algorithms enabled with uninitialized-memory filling disabled.

| Native record-stream policy | Fresh repeats per arm | Positive rank/cases | Exact saved-view gradients | Deleted-record rejections | Forced-retry passes |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `EP_AVOID_RECORD_STREAM=0` | 3 | 288/288 | 288/288 | 96/96 | 96/96 |
| `EP_AVOID_RECORD_STREAM=1` | 3 | 288/288 | 288/288 | 96/96 | 96/96 |

Two additional controls were run outside the PR using that exact earlier public test source, without changing DeepEP's implementation:

- **Negative control:** AST-remove exactly the consumer-side `prefix.record_stream(reader)` expression from `cross_stream_pressure`. For balanced nonempty receives, run both deterministic modes and both allocation streams. All 24 distributed cases were rejected by the specific `CROSS_STREAM_RECEIVE_MISMATCH` assertion; actual local data corruption was observed in all 192 rank/cases. Other assertions or an ineffective window do not count as detection.
- **Scheduling control:** synchronize only rank 0 immediately before its first `pending_before` query. All ranks must retry attempt 0 together and pass on a later effective attempt. All 24 distributed cases / 192 rank/cases passed.

An earlier draft's post-copy-event stress missed the deleted-record mutation. That draft is not the sensitivity evidence above; the pre-read/completed-pressure ordering and destination preallocation were added before rerunning all historical arms.

All eighteen historical fresh launches exited successfully. Source/input hashes, exact per-rank coverage, control mutation identities and completion/exit sentinels were audited from downloaded logs. Archive SHA256: `834a31fa761e439678244ae49cdaf98491ead5fb23b4724500ba038366eac777`.

Local checks for that earlier revision: Python compilation, Ruff 0.6.5, YAPF 0.40.2 (no diff), and `git diff --check` passed.

## Scope

This establishes component lifetime/gradient correctness for ordinary compact BF16 receives in one physical NVLink domain. It does not establish full-model convergence, training throughput gains, borrowed-storage safety, FP8/expanded layouts, or multi-node hybrid routing. Capacity-retention assertions deliberately distinguish logical tensor bytes from retained storage bytes.

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash stores each KV token as 528B: 512B of FP8 E4M3 covering
the full 512-wide K (rope lanes quantized, no BF16 rope segment) plus a 16B
footer of 16 UE8M0 scales over 32-wide groups (the
deepseek-ai/FlashMLA#221
layout, SM100-only there). Add ModelType::DSV4_1 on top of the ScaleSpec
groundwork: GLM53_NOPE-style geometry (D_ROPE=0) composed with a 32-wide
UE8M0 footer.

Kernel side the format is simpler than DSV4 (one 512B bulk per row, a single
unified block-scaled FP8 QK pass, no rope MMA paths). The two new mechanics:

- the 16B footer row generalizes the scale gather from one uint64_t to a
  width-selected load (uint4) in both the prefill IO helper and the decode
  kernel's staged gather;
- the 32-wide groups constrain the XV W-fold (one scale group per W buffer),
  so an 8-warp XV split would floor NT_PER_WARP_XV to 0: decode runs a
  4-math-warp tile at BI=64 (the DOTS3_SWA halving precedent) and prefill is
  SG-only on the BI=32 producer/consumer tile. The ComputeTraits/SmemLayout
  aliases now take the XV warp count so the NT_PER_WARP_XV assert evaluates at
  the warp count the XV MMA actually runs at.

Selection is explicit everywhere (d_qk=512 collides with DSV4, the 528B
payload with GLM53_NOPE): the functional API gains kv_scale_format=
"ue8m0_g32", the TRTLLM-compat entry kv_cache_format="fp8_dsv41", and the
decode-dsv4 FFI takes an explicit model_type (-1 keeps the legacy width
inference, matching the paged-entry kAuto convention). Dual-cache decode is
supported like DSV4; dual-cache prefill (MG_DUAL) is intentionally not
instantiated. Calibration keys a new dsv4_1 family at topk 512.

Tests: decode matrix (dedicated/runtime-H heads, partial-tail topk, sinks),
SG prefill, dual-cache through the TRTLLM entry, poisoned-slot-0 NaN safety
on both gather paths, dispatch/plan/envelope coverage. 666 passed on RTX PRO
6000 (SM120).

Upstream restructured csrc/ into csrc/kernels/<arch>/<op>/, turned the
csrc/api/*.h header-only interfaces into .cpp translation units with their
own pybind registration, replaced the per-kernel format constants with a
KVCacheFormat<ModelType> descriptor, and renamed MODEL1 to DeepSeek-V4.
The fork's changes were carried onto that structure:

* libtorch build: dropped the csrc/flashmla_utils.h shim -- upstream's
  includes are now "kernels/utils.h", which no longer collides with
  sgl-kernel's bare utils.h. csrc/api/common.h keeps Python-free headers
  under FLASH_MLA_LIBTORCH_ONLY, and the register_* functions that upstream
  moved into csrc/api/*.cpp are guarded by the same macro, so a libtorch-only
  build still compiles the interface TUs without Python.
  csrc/python_api.cpp declares the three interfaces extern instead of
  including the (now non-header) api files.

* B200 V3.2 accuracy: upstream still narrows V3.2's inline fp32 KV scales to
  1-byte ue8m0 in the index warp, which drops the mantissa. The bf16-scale
  fix is ported into the generic KVBlockDequantizer through one new format
  constant, KVCacheFormat::SCALE_SMEM_BYTES (2 for the V3.2 formats, 1
  otherwise). NUM_INDEX_BUFS stays 2 for V3.2, keeping the scale smem
  footprint identical to upstream.

* V32_NO_ROPE: expressed as a KVCacheFormat (d_qk 512, no RoPE, V3.2's
  inline fp32 scales) instead of ad-hoc constants, so the sm100 head64 kernel
  reuses the D_BF16 == 0 path upstream added for V4.1. NOTE V3.2-no-RoPE and
  V4.1 are both 528 B per token with d_qk 512, so the shape alone can no
  longer identify the format: sparse_decode_fwd / flash_mla_with_kvcache take
  a new optional kv_format argument, and auto-detection reads 528 B as
  V3.2-no-RoPE so that callers written before V4.1 keep working.

* sm90 dense decode HEAD_DIM_K=512 and the decode-meta low-smem fallback
  carried over with no semantic change.

Deleted csrc/kernels/sm90/decode/sparse/components/config.h: nothing includes
it any more and its hardcoded V3.2 constants are misleading.

title: refactor(moe_ep)!: move the MoE all-to-all ops out of flashinfer.comm into their moe_ep backends; retire backend="trtllm" and the moe_comm bench; SM107 one-sided build fix
body:
## 📌 Description

Follow-up to #6047. Now that `flashinfer.moe_ep` owns the MoE all-to-all backends, this removes what stayed behind in `flashinfer.comm` for the old paths, and fixes the NVLink one-sided module on GR100. After it, every `MoEEpCommunication` backend owns its kernels under `flashinfer/moe_ep/backends/split/comm/<backend>/` (as `nvlink_one_sided` already did), and `flashinfer/comm/` keeps no MoE all-to-all code. Five commits:

### 1. `fix(moe_ep)`: native `sm_107a` for the NVLink one-sided module

`gen_nvlink_one_sided_alltoall_module` (then `gen_moe_ep_nvlink_one_sided_module`) inherited the global JIT arch flags, which map SM107 to `sm_100f` while the bundled CUTLASS lacks `Sm107`. The driver rejects that code on GR100 (`Mercury Validator: Validation failed for SM 107`), so the first launch failed with `cudaErrorUnknown`. These kernels use no CUTLASS, so the module now passes `get_nvcc_flags_list()` and builds every target natively. Verified on an 8x GR100 node: fence and CFT both run (`bench_moe_ep_comm.py`, EP4).

### 2. `refactor(bench)!`: remove the `moe_a2a_dispatch_combine` routine

`benchmarks/routines/moe_comm.py` timed the functional `moe_a2a_*` ops with the `backend="trtllm"` kernels, which no `moe_ep` backend uses (it was marked deprecated in #6047).

- `benchmarks/moe_ep/core/comm/bench_moe_ep_comm.py` covers MoE communication and gains `--quant fp8_block_scale` (DeepSeek FP8: E4M3 plus one FP32 scale per 128 elements, `QuantFormat.DeepSeekFp8`). `benchmarks/moe_ep/bench_moe_ep.py` covers dispatch + MoE + combine.
- Removed with it: the routine's registration in `flashinfer_benchmark.py`, its output columns, its README section and sample test-list entries, and four `moe_utils.py` helpers only it used.
- Not carried over: `--use_lora` (a per-token int32 payload). `MoEEpCommunication.dispatch()` has no extra-payload argument, so the communication bench cannot express it.

### 3. `refactor(comm)!`: remove the `backend="trtllm"` kernels; move the Cake sources

- The legacy kernels (`communicationKernels/moeAlltoAllKernels.cu`) are deleted, together with the seven per-phase sources `moeAlltoAll{PrepareDispatch,Dispatch,StageCombine,PublishCombine,Combine,QuantizeCombine,Sanitize}.cu`, which no module compiled.
- The Cake sources leave `nv_internal` and follow the other Cake ops:

  | Before | After |
  |---|---|
  | `csrc/trtllm_moe_alltoall.cu` | `csrc/cake_moe_alltoall.cu` |
  | `csrc/nv_internal/.../communicationKernels/moeAlltoAllFusedKernels.cu` | `csrc/cake_moe_alltoall_dispatch.cu` |
  | `csrc/nv_internal/.../communicationKernels/moeAlltoAllKernels.h` | `csrc/cake_moe_alltoall_dispatch.cuh` |
  | `csrc/nv_internal/tensorrt_llm/thop/moeAlltoAllMeta.h` | `csrc/cake_moe_alltoall_meta.h` |
  | `csrc/generated/mnnvl_moe_alltoall_sm10{0,3}.cu` | `csrc/generated/moe_alltoall/cake_moe_alltoall_sm10{0,3}.cu` (renamed in commit 7) |

### 4. `refactor(moe_ep)!`: move the Cake and two-sided all-to-all ops into their backends

The Cake and NVLink two-sided backends still drove their kernels through function layers in `flashinfer.comm` (`trtllm_moe_alltoall.py`, `trtllm_alltoall.py`), left over from before `flashinfer.moe_ep`. This completes the move announced when `MoeAlltoAll` / `MnnvlMoe` were deprecated in #5532 ("their implementations will move into those classes").

- **Cake:** `cake/kernels.py` loads the per-architecture module and holds the kernel-level `initialize` / `dispatch` / `combine` / `sanitize_expert_ids` / `workspace_size_per_rank` / `wrap_workspace` / `active_rank_mask` operations; `CakeAlltoAll` calls them directly. Removed: `flashinfer/comm/trtllm_moe_alltoall.py`, the `flashinfer.comm.moe_a2a_*` re-exports, the `backend` argument, and the per-architecture torch custom ops. JIT: `gen_moe_alltoall_module` → `gen_cake_alltoall_module`, modules `cake_alltoall_sm100a` / `_sm103a` (named in commit 8). Combine-output quantization stays available at the kernel level (`kernels.combine(output_dtype=..., output_scales=...)`).
- **NVLink two-sided:** `nvlink_two_sided/kernels.py` holds `prepare` / `alltoallv`, the workspace sizes and `set_max_usable_sm_count`; `NVLinkTwoSidedAlltoAll` calls them directly. Removed: `flashinfer/comm/trtllm_alltoall.py`, and the `moe_comm_prepare_indices` / `moe_local_gather` ops with their kernels, which only their tests used.

  | Before | After |
  |---|---|
  | `csrc/trtllm_alltoall.cu` | `csrc/nvlink_two_sided_alltoall.cu` |
  | `csrc/trtllm_alltoall_prepare.cu` | `csrc/nvlink_two_sided_prepare.cu` |
  | `include/flashinfer/comm/trtllm_alltoall.cuh` | `csrc/nvlink_two_sided_alltoall.cuh` |
  | `include/flashinfer/comm/trtllm_alltoall_prepare.cuh` | `csrc/nvlink_two_sided_prepare.cuh` |
  | namespace `flashinfer::trtllm_alltoall` | `flashinfer::nvlink_two_sided` |
  | `gen_comm_alltoall_module()`, module `comm` | `gen_nvlink_two_sided_alltoall_module()`, module `nvlink_two_sided_alltoall` |

- Both backends keep their workspace sharing unchanged (Cake: refcounted per layout; two-sided: per `(ep_rank, ep_size)` for the process).
- Kernel-level tests import the new modules. `test_trtllm_moe_alltoall.py` → `test_cake_moe_alltoall.py`, `test_trtllm_alltoall.py` → `test_nvlink_two_sided_alltoall.py` (same directory, so CI routing is unchanged; `task_test_single_node_comm_kernels.sh` updated).

### 5. `docs(moe_ep)`: document the expert-parallel communication backends

New `docs/api/moe_ep_communication.rst` ("flashinfer.moe_ep: Expert-Parallel Communication") with `MoEEpCommunication`, `create_communication`, `BootstrapConfig` and the three NVLink backends and their configs; the checkpoint/restore notes move there from the removed `flashinfer.comm` "MNNVL A2A (Throughput Backend)" section. The architecture doc now points at the backends' own kernels and says that instances of one EP group share a workspace per layout.

### 6. `test(comm)`: name the Cake all-to-all tests and driver after Cake

`test_mnnvl_moe_alltoall.py` is the multi-GPU MNNVL test of the Cake kernels, the counterpart of the single-GPU `test_cake_moe_alltoall.py`; it becomes `test_cake_moe_alltoall_multi_gpu.py` (`task_test_multi_node_comm_kernels.sh` updated). `test_mnnvl_moe_alltoall_fused_adapter.py` → `test_cake_moe_alltoall_fused_adapter.py`, `test_moe_a2a_recv_view_cache.py` → `test_cake_moe_alltoall_recv_view_cache.py`, `moe_a2a_driver.MoeA2ADriver` → `cake_a2a_driver.CakeA2ADriver`.

### 7. `refactor(comm)`: give the generated Cake MoE all-to-all sources the `cake_` prefix

`mnnvl_moe_alltoall_sm10{0,3}.cu` → `cake_moe_alltoall_sm10{0,3}.cu`, matching `csrc/generated/dcp_alltoall/cake_*` and `csrc/generated/ulysses/cake_*`. Also `benchmarks/README.md` now says MoE communication has no `flashinfer_benchmark.py` routine *yet*.

### 8. `refactor(moe_ep)`: name the all-to-all sources and modules after their backends

Drops the `moe_ep_` prefix so the names follow `NVLinkOneSidedAlltoAll`, `NVLinkTwoSidedAlltoAll` and `CakeAlltoAll`:

| Before | After |
|---|---|
| `csrc/moe_ep_nvlink_{one,two}_sided_*` | `csrc/nvlink_{one,two}_sided_*` (namespace `flashinfer::nvlink_two_sided`) |
| module `moe_ep_nvlink_{one,two}_sided_alltoall`, `gen_moe_ep_nvlink_{one,two}_sided_module` | module `nvlink_{one,two}_sided_alltoall`, `gen_nvlink_{one,two}_sided_alltoall_module` |
| module `moe_ep_cake_alltoall_{sm100a,sm103a}`, `gen_moe_ep_cake_module` | module `cake_alltoall_{sm100a,sm103a}`, `gen_cake_alltoall_module` |
| loaders `get_nvlink_{one,two}_sided_module`, `get_cake_module` | `get_nvlink_{one,two}_sided_alltoall_module`, `get_cake_alltoall_module` |

### 9. `ci(comm)`: cover the MoE expert-parallel communication backends

The comm-kernel lanes ran only the Cake kernel tests. `task_test_single_node_comm_kernels.sh` now also runs `tests/comm/test_nvlink_two_sided_alltoall.py` and `tests/moe_ep/run_tests.sh comm` (the `MoEEpCommunication` multirank test and `test_nvlink_one_sided.py`, on up to four GPUs). `task_test_multi_node_comm_kernels.sh` adds `tests/moe_ep/test_moe_ep_communication_multirank.py`, which can now be started by an MPI launcher (Open MPI, MPICH/Hydra, PMIx) as well as by torchrun: it maps the MPI rank, size and node-local rank to torch.distributed's `env://` variables at import.

title: feat(moe_ep)!: sync NVLinkOneSidedAlltoAll with TensorRT-LLM's kernels; remove the deprecated MoeAlltoAll/MnnvlMoe
body:
<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

Follow-up to #5532. `flashinfer.moe_ep.NVLinkOneSidedAlltoAll` now runs its own NVLink one-sided MoE all-to-all kernels, synced with TensorRT-LLM's (`cpp/tensorrt_llm/kernels/moe/communication/` plus the later one-sided changes), instead of wrapping the deprecated `flashinfer.comm.MoeAlltoAll`. The `MoEEpCommunication` interface from #5532 is unchanged.

It also completes the deprecation started in #5532. No `MoEEpCommunication` backend builds on `MoeAlltoAll` or `MnnvlMoe` any more, so both classes are **removed** (breaking; see *Removal and migration* below). `NVLinkOneSidedAlltoAll` and `CakeAlltoAll` take over `MoeAlltoAll`'s `checkpoint_prepare` / `checkpoint_restore`.

### What the new kernels bring

- **CFT counted writes.** On Blackwell systems whose driver exports the CUDA logical-endpoint API, dispatch and combine can push payloads over the NVLink fabric with `fabric.try_put.counted`. The receiver then waits on hardware byte counters instead of per-round completion flags, and the CFT dispatch also fills the padding rows' expert ids itself. The logical endpoint is bound to the existing MNNVL workspace, so no extra memory is allocated.
- **Up to 256 EP ranks** (was 64); the active-rank mask grows to four words.
- **Workspace laid out by phase.** Round state, dispatch control and payload, and combine control, input and the CFT receive inbox are separate regions with fixed capacities, which every op validates.
- **Routing and fan-out.**
  - Invalid expert ids are skipped during routing.
  - When `top_k > ep_size`, dispatch and combine fan out over a compact per-rank destination list.
  - Receive counters are double-buffered by round parity; the CFT dispatch publishes them right after routing.
- **Low-precision combine** pairs FP8 conversions.
- **Timeouts** are chosen on the host per launch.

### Python

- `NVLinkOneSidedAlltoAll` drives the new JIT module (`moe_ep_nvlink_one_sided_alltoall`) directly.
  - **Workspace sharing:** instances with the same layout share one workspace, which is freed when its last instance is destroyed. Instances on one workspace must run their rounds one after another; a dispatch while another instance's round awaits its combine raises.
  - **CFT setup:** endpoint creation and exchange run over the EP group's `CommBackend`, so no MPI is involved. Every rank agrees on CFT before the layout is fixed, and a failure on any rank falls back to the fence path on all ranks.
- `NVLinkOneSidedConfig` gains:
  - `cft`: `None` uses CFT automatically where supported, for steps up to `cft_max_tokens_for_dispatch` / `cft_max_tokens_for_combine` tokens (128 each); `True` uses it on every supported step; `False` never uses it;
  - `timeout_sec`: the bound on each wait for a peer;
  - `enable_pdl`: programmatic dependent launch, `None` enabling it on SM90+ as before (also on `CakeAlltoAllConfig`).
- `NVLinkOneSidedAlltoAll.active_rank_mask(ranks)` builds the 256-rank mask, and `cft_enabled` reports whether CFT is available to the instance.
- **`CakeAlltoAll`** is now a standalone `MoEEpCommunication` (it used to subclass `NVLinkOneSidedAlltoAll`). The generated Cake kernels implement the protocol of the functional `moe_a2a_*` ops, which it calls with `backend="cake"`; those ops are unchanged. `CakeAlltoAll` pins the combine region at the end of the workspace instead of using the offset each dispatch returns, which moves with the token count (the race #6376 fixed in `MoeAlltoAll`), and follows the same one-round-per-workspace rule.
- `benchmarks/moe_ep/core/comm/bench_moe_ep_comm.py` gets `--cft {auto,on,off}`.
- The module is in the AOT build list for SM90+.

### Checkpointing

`NVLinkOneSidedAlltoAll` and `CakeAlltoAll` gain `checkpoint_prepare()` and `checkpoint_restore(comm_backend)`, with the semantics `MoeAlltoAll` had (callers such as vLLM used to reach them through the former `.alltoall` accessor):

- **Prepare:** releases the physical MNNVL memory and keeps the virtual addresses reserved.
- **Restore:** remaps the memory over a fresh `CommBackend` and re-initializes the workspace. CUDA graphs captured before the checkpoint replay correctly afterwards.
- **Shared rules:** both calls are collective, and repeated calls do nothing.
- **CFT endpoints:**
  - `NVLinkOneSidedAlltoAll` also releases its CFT logical endpoints before the memory and recreates them afterwards.
  - Launches bake the endpoint IDs into their kernel parameters, so the endpoints keep their ID block reserved across the checkpoint (`moe_a2a_cft_release_endpoints`) and are recreated under the same IDs.
  - Restore verifies the IDs and raises if they changed.
- **CftLeManager fix:** it now tracks imported peer endpoints explicitly. It used to treat ID 0 as unset, and ID blocks start at 0, so the import of rank 0's endpoint was never destroyed. The kernels' copy in TensorRT-LLM has the same bug.
- The shared MNNVL helpers are `unmap_mnnvl_memory` / `remap_mnnvl_memory` in `nvlink_common`.

### Removal and migration

`MoeAlltoAll` and `MnnvlMoe` were deprecated in #5532, which ships in a release before this PR. No backend uses them after this PR:

- `NVLinkOneSidedAlltoAll` runs the new kernels above.
- `CakeAlltoAll` calls the functional `moe_a2a_*` ops with `backend="cake"`. Instances with the same geometry share a workspace, which the last one to be destroyed frees, as `NVLinkOneSidedAlltoAll` does.
- `NVLinkTwoSidedAlltoAll` calls `moe_prepare` / `moe_comm` from `flashinfer.comm.trtllm_alltoall` directly. Its FIFO positions persist in the workspace, so, as with `MnnvlMoe`, the workspaces stay with the process and are shared by every instance of the EP group.

This PR removes both classes, the `flashinfer.comm.MoeAlltoAll` export and `MoEAlltoallInfo`. The functional ops and their kernels stay. Migration:

| Removed | Use instead |
|---|---|
| `flashinfer.comm.MoeAlltoAll` | `flashinfer.moe_ep.NVLinkOneSidedAlltoAll` (newer kernels), `flashinfer.moe_ep.CakeAlltoAll` for `backend="cake"`, or the `moe_a2a_*` ops for arbitrary payload lists |
| `MoeAlltoAll.checkpoint_prepare` / `checkpoint_restore` | the methods of the same names on `NVLinkOneSidedAlltoAll` / `CakeAlltoAll` |
| `flashinfer.comm.trtllm_alltoall.MnnvlMoe` | `flashinfer.moe_ep.NVLinkTwoSidedAlltoAll`, or `moe_prepare` / `moe_comm` |

Tests and benchmarks that used the classes now use the replacements:

- Tests that drove the kernels through the classes use the functional ops, through `tests/comm/moe_a2a_driver.py` where they need per-round state. Class-only checks (method signatures, the workspace cache) are dropped.
- The `moe_a2a_dispatch_combine` routine of `flashinfer_benchmark.py` runs the functional ops.
- `bench_cute_dsl_moe_distributed.py` uses `NVLinkOneSidedAlltoAll`.

### Files

- `csrc/nv_internal/tensorrt_llm/kernels/moe/communication/`: kernels, CFT logical-endpoint manager, CUDA 13.4 feature gate. The paths mirror TensorRT-LLM's.
- `csrc/nv_internal/tensorrt_llm/thop/moe/communication/moeAlltoAllMeta.h`: workspace layout indices.
- `csrc/moe_ep_nvlink_one_sided_alltoall.cu`: TVM-FFI ops.
- `flashinfer/jit/comm.py`: `gen_moe_ep_nvlink_one_sided_module`.
- `flashinfer/moe_ep/backends/split/comm/{nvlink_one_sided,cake}/`.

## 🔍 Related Issues

Follow-up to #5532 and #4784.

## 🚀 Pull Request Checklist

### ✅ Pre-commit Checks

- [x] I have installed `pre-commit` by running `pip install pre-commit` (or used your preferred method).
- [x] I have installed the hooks with `pre-commit install`.
- [x] I have run the hooks manually and fixed any reported issues (run on the changed files).

## 🧪 Tests

- [x] Tests have been added or updated as needed.
- [x] All tests are passing (`unittest`, etc.).

Validated on B300 (CUDA 13.5, driver 620, where CFT counted writes are available):
- `tests/moe_ep/test_nvlink_one_sided.py` (new; `pytest` spawns one process per EP rank; also run by `run_tests.sh comm`): 44 passed. Ported from TensorRT-LLM's `test_nvlink_one_sided.py`: model-shaped round trips (MXFP8, blockwise FP8, NVFP4 and BF16 dispatch; top_k 3 to 16; EP4 and EP8; 1, 128 and 1024 tokens), BF16/FP8 combine with external or workspace input, a 4-rank round sequence with changing and zero token counts, a delayed rank and the CFT threshold (fence, CFT and automatic; eager and CUDA graph; PDL on and off), EPLB statistics and the workspace layout. The round sequence, combine, EPLB and model cases also run on Cake; with Cake's former moving combine offset the round sequence fails with mismatched outputs.
- The module also builds for `FLASHINFER_CUDA_ARCH_LIST="9.0a 10.0a 10.3a"`.
- `tests/moe_ep/test_moe_ep_communication_multirank.py` on 4 and 8 GPUs (`bash tests/moe_ep/run_tests.sh comm`), 18 passed each. The one-sided cases now run as a fence variant and a CFT variant:
  - dispatch/combine against a local reference at top_k 4 and 8 (rank-compact fan-out);
  - FP8 combine together with EPLB statistics and an all-active rank mask;
  - split-layer CUDA-graph replay;
  - Cake and two-sided, now off the removed classes, still pass;
  - checkpoint/restore around a captured split-layer CUDA graph for the fence, CFT and Cake paths (4 and 8 GPUs, 3 passed each).
- `tests/moe_ep/test_communication.py` (host-only, stubbed kernels): 31 passed. New cases cover workspace sizing by dispatch format, CFT selection and probe failures, `enable_pdl`, payload plumbing and sanitization, the rank mask, config validation, Cake's pinned combine region, and rejecting interleaved rounds on a shared workspace.
- `bash tests/moe_ep/run_tests.sh unit`: 961 + 1 + 23 passed, 141 skipped.
- The functional ops and their tests in `tests/comm`, now without the classes:
  - `test_trtllm_moe_alltoall.py` and `test_moe_a2a_recv_view_cache.py`: 167 passed;
  - `test_mnnvl_moe_alltoall.py` and `test_mnnvl_moe_alltoall_fused_adapter.py` (`mpirun -np 4`): 41 passed, 1 skipped; the fused adapter's two-rank cycle (`mpirun -np 2`): 24 passed;
  - `test_mnnvl_memory.py` (`mpirun -np 4`): 2 passed.
- `flashinfer_benchmark.py --routine moe_a2a_dispatch_combine --validate` (plain, `--quant_dtype nvfp4`, `--use_lora`) validates on 4 ranks.
- `bench_cute_dsl_moe_distributed.py --variants w4a16` runs on 8 GPUs.

## Reviewer Notes

- FlashInfer-only features of the old one-sided kernels stay available through the `moe_a2a_*` ops and are not ported, because `MoEEpCommunication` does not expose them:
  - combine output quantization (MXFP8/MXFP4/NVFP4);
  - the phased NVFP4 dispatch for hidden ≤ 2048 at EP4/8/16 (#4067).
- **CFT limits:**
  - only one workspace per process can bind the logical endpoints; others use the fence path;
  - payload rows must be multiples of 16 bytes, so top_k = 3 or 6 routing (12- or 24-byte id rows) dispatches over the fence path and only its combine can use CFT;
  - the kernels compile CFT in only with CUDA 13.4+ headers, and the feature is resolved from the driver at runtime.
- An instance with `enable_rank_mask=True` refuses CUDA-graph capture, because the mask would be frozen into the graph.

## Follow-ups (separate PRs)

- **Retire the legacy `backend="trtllm"` path of the `moe_a2a_*` ops** (JIT module `mnnvl_moe_alltoall`, kernels in `csrc/nv_internal/tensorrt_llm/kernels/communicationKernels/moeAlltoAllKernels.*`). No `moe_ep` backend uses it after this PR. Deprecate it first, then remove it together with its tests (`test_trtllm_moe_alltoall.py`, `test_mnnvl_moe_alltoall.py` / `moe_a2a_driver.py`, `test_moe_a2a_recv_view_cache.py`; keep the parts that apply to Cake), and change the `backend` default. The FlashInfer-only features listed above (combine output quantization, phased NVFP4 dispatch) need a decision before that: port them or drop them. Until then, note that the module-level `moe_a2a_dispatch` returns a combine offset that moves with `runtime_max_tokens_per_rank` and the payload sizes (for both `trtllm` and `cake`); callers that drive the ops directly must keep the combine region fixed themselves, as `CakeAlltoAll` does.
- **Retire `benchmarks/routines/moe_comm.py`** (`moe_a2a_dispatch_combine`), which times the legacy path. Communication-only cases move to `benchmarks/moe_ep/core/comm/bench_moe_ep_comm.py`, which needs `fp8_block_scale` (`DeepSeekFp8`) and an `--extra_payload_bytes` option (covers `--use_lora`). Dispatch + MoE + combine cases (`--real_math`) move to `benchmarks/moe_ep/bench_moe_ep.py`, which needs the NVLink backends (`nvlink_one_sided`, `cake`, `nvlink_two_sided`). Optionally register `bench_moe_ep_comm.py` as a `flashinfer_benchmark` routine.
- **Move the Cake MoE all-to-all sources out of `nv_internal`** (e.g. into `csrc/cake_moe_alltoall/`), and remove the per-phase files in `communicationKernels/` that no JIT spec compiles (`moeAlltoAllDispatch.cu`, `moeAlltoAllPrepareDispatch.cu`, `moeAlltoAllStageCombine.cu`, `moeAlltoAllPublishCombine.cu`, `moeAlltoAllCombine.cu`, `moeAlltoAllQuantizeCombine.cu`, `moeAlltoAllSanitize.cu`).
- **MNNVL handle selection** (see #5765): pick the handle type from the first real allocation (create/export, vote, import, vote, then map), fall back to POSIX on a single host, and share one cached decision between `MnnvlMemory` and `SymmDeviceMemory`. CFT should then follow the handle type the workspace actually uses.

title: perf(cake_ssd_combined): fused exact-scan programs, host routing, look-back chunk-parallel, exactpre family (SM100 / SM103)
body:
## Summary

This PR updates the generated Cake SSDCombined programs for B200 (sm_100a) and GB300 (sm_103a). It also updates the loader `flashinfer/mamba/cake_ssd_combined.py`. The baseline is the previous release, FlashInfer `36fd76859292ac2ac5aebd0892fc64715569b9da` (PR #6330 merge). The public API is unchanged.

### Program families

`csrc/cake_mamba_ssd_combined/` now holds 49 device sources and 5 host templates. The loader table lists 48 programs.

| Family | Device sources | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `exact_*` | 12 | Previous-release two-kernel exact scan, retained byte for byte. |
| `exactfused_*` | 12 | Fused single-launch exact scan: preprocess and scan in one launch. |
| `exactpre_*` | 12 | This release's two-kernel exact scan: standalone preprocess, then the main kernel. |
| `chunkpar_*` | 6 | Single-pass chunk-parallel scan with decoupled look-back (fixed Horner fold, range partition). |
| `chunkpar3_*` | 6 | Three-phase chunk-parallel program of the previous release. Its results are bitwise equal to that release. |
| preprocess | 1 | Metadata preprocess kernel. |

`exact_*` binds the 41 start arguments (`_MAIN_ARGS_START`). `exactfused_*` and `exactpre_*` bind all 44 (`_MAIN_ARGS`: the 41 plus `cu_seqlens`, `metadata_from_cu_seqlens`, `preprocess_status`). The look-back chunk-parallel main kernel takes six more arguments than the exact scan (`_MAIN_ARGS_CHUNKPAR`, 47) and the three-phase one four more (`_MAIN_ARGS_CHUNKPAR3`, 45).

The 13 retained files are the 12 `exact_*` device sources and `host/mamba_ssd_combined_sequence.cpp`. Their SHA-256 digests are pinned on the Cake side (`_MAMBA_SSD_COMBINED_RETAINED_START_FILES` in the export module, not in this PR) and checked by the Cake export tool `tools/export_cake_mamba_ssd_combined.py --check`; the FI test `test_source_retained_start_programs_are_the_round5_files` carries the same 13 digests and checks the shipped files against them.

### Host routing

The loader selects one program per call, in this order:

1. The chunk-parallel rule runs first. `FLASHINFER_CAKE_SSD_CHUNK_PARALLEL` forces or disables it.
2. `fused_selected` mirrors the Cake seed `fused_route`. Calls inside its window run `exactfused_*`. The window is: batched items <= 1024, chunks <= 16, (item, chunk) <= 2048; packed varlen items <= 256, (chunk, head) <= 512.
3. Other calls go to `two_kernel_family`, the mirror of the Cake seed `two_kernel_route` (`TWO_KERNEL_ROUTE_MIN_CHUNKS = 2`). It counts chunks per work item: batched `ceil(seqlen/128)`, varlen `ceil(ceil(packed_tokens/num_sequences)/128)` (num_sequences 0 -> 1). At >= 2 chunks the call runs `exactpre_*`. At one chunk it runs the retained `exact_*`.

`exactpre_*` lost the kernel A/B on one-chunk two-kernel calls. Those calls therefore keep the previous-release program by design.

`_exact_scan_variant` no longer selects the `_noring` twin for FP32-state varlen calls. In the 93-row gate, only nem_v8x64_float32 changes route.

### Trusted caller cumsum in the triple form (F1b)

- A seq_idx / chunk_indices / chunk_offsets ("triple") call can pass `seq_chunk_cumsum` with `update_seq_chunk_cumsum=False`. Inside the fused window, this call now takes the fused program, like the `cu_seqlens` form.
- On that call the preprocess grid is `(0,1,1)` and `metadata_from_cu_seqlens=0`. The kernel reads the caller's tables.
- A triple call that derives the table keeps the two-kernel programs.
- `_WorkspaceKey.caller_cumsum` records the case. It is derived from the call arguments alone.
- `prepare()` reads a given cumsum the way `run()` reads it by default. In the triple form that is a trusted table. In the `cu_seqlens` form it is the publishing buffer. `prepare()` and `run()` therefore resolve the same program.
- A triple-form `run(update_seq_chunk_cumsum=True)` is a different call shape. It runs the two-kernel program and is captured after one eager run.

### Launcher, API, branch

- `_load_generated_program` sets `-DTVM_FFI_CUBIN_LAUNCHER_USE_DRIVER_API=1` (driver-API launcher). Its bitwise check reads 38/38 on both archs.
- Public API unchanged: `CakeSSDCombined.run/prepare`, `PreparedSSDCombined`, `SSDCombined(backend="cake")`, `ssd_combined_fwd`.
- The sglang engine path passes `cu_seqlens` only. F1b does not touch that path.
- 22 commits on `36fd76859292`: 44 files, +72438 / −327. Changed paths: `csrc/cake_mamba_ssd_combined/**`, `flashinfer/mamba/cake_ssd_combined.py`, `tests/mamba/**`.
- Measured head: `31b444fb7fa402582ba60e0dbd694d54ef46e8ca`. PR head: `63e9d31b255ced943a0eb8ff028f76d29bb504b8`, three commits on top of the measured head that change comments and docstrings only (51 insertions / 50 deletions across the loader and the two test files; the executable code is identical: AST with docstrings masked and the comment-free token stream are equal for all three files, `csrc/` is byte-identical). Every measurement below was taken on the measured head.

### Labels used below

- **c9**: the same generated kernels with the loader at `b1cefa5e79f604c460653b3db0273bfcd7bab16f`. This loader predates the trusted-cumsum route.
- **F1b**: the same generated kernels with this PR's loader (measured at `31b444fb7fa402582ba60e0dbd694d54ef46e8ca`; the PR head `63e9d31b255ced943a0eb8ff028f76d29bb504b8` is code-identical, see above).

## Numerics

- `exact_*` and `chunkpar3_*` are bitwise the previous release.
- `exactfused_*` and `exactpre_*` read a prescaled decay factor table from shared memory. They update the state with a single-rounding FMA. The algorithm is the same, but the results are not bitwise the previous programs.
- `chunkpar_*` differs from the previous programs by the look-back re-association.

**P6 reading.** It replaces the former bitwise assertions between program families.

- Oracle: an fp64 token-by-token recurrence. Compared tensors: `out`, `final_states`, `checkpoint_states`.
- K = 8 fixed seeds per shape. The reference is the previous-release program on the same inputs.
- Hard clauses, per seed: outlier count (m1) and worst-element ulp distance (m2) must not exceed the reference.
- Statistical clauses, mean over seeds: p99.9 relative error (m3), RMS relative error (m4) and max absolute error (m5). Each must stay within the reference mean plus one seed-to-seed standard deviation.
- Result on the c9 tree: PASS on both archs. GB300: 131 rows plus 20 look-back rows. B200: 141 rows plus 25 look-back rows. F1b changes no kernel.

**Two packed-varlen metadata forms.** These forms are no longer bitwise equal in every case.

- A triple call with a trusted caller cumsum runs the same fused program as the `cu_seqlens` form. The tests assert the two bitwise equal inside the fused window.
- Consider a triple call that derives the table, with one-chunk items inside the fused window. It runs the retained `exact_*` two-kernel program. The `cu_seqlens` form runs `exactfused_*` there. The two differ only in the last rounding of `final_states`.

Derived triple vs `cu_seqlens` form, 6 cases x 2 repeats:

| Quantity | Result |
|---|---|
| `out` | bitwise equal, 6/6 |
| `final_states`, bf16 state | 0 diff |
| `final_states`, f16 state | <= 1 ulp (1–2 elements) |
| `final_states`, f32 state | max_abs <= 6.0e-8 (max_ulp 26 / 250 / 3217) |
| Error vs fp64 | identical across forms to 4 digits: 2.217e-3 / 3.965e-3 / 2.079e-3 / 2.627e-3 / 3.136e-3 |

Each form passes P6 on its own. The public API and both forms are unchanged. sglang passes `cu_seqlens` only.

**Determinism.** We ran 7 shapes x 20 launches. Each was repeated under background-stream load and with the grid knob at {1, 1/2, 1/4}. PASS on both archs.

## Tests

### GPU module + capture tests

`tests/mamba/test_cake_ssd_combined.py` and `tests/mamba/test_cake_ssd_combined_capture.py`:

| Loader head | GB300 (sm_103a) | B200 (sm_100a) |
|---|---|---|
| `7fdf10477bdd2680b38d79293e24723daf3b83cc` (comments-only over the measured head; the PR head `63e9d31b255ced943a0eb8ff028f76d29bb504b8` differs from it in comments only) | `492 passed, 2 skipped` in 2568.12s | `492 passed, 2 skipped` in 110.46s |
| `31b444fb7fa402582ba60e0dbd694d54ef46e8ca` (measured head, F1b) | `492 passed, 2 skipped` in 122.90s | `492 passed, 2 skipped` in 125.03s |
| `b1cefa5e79f604c460653b3db0273bfcd7bab16f` (c9) | `490 passed, 2 skipped, 0 failed` | `490 passed, 2 skipped, 0 failed` |

CPU-only subset (`-k "without_gpu or source_"`) at this head: `1 failed, 281 passed, 212 deselected`. Both driver-less environments give the same counts. The failure is `test_source_runner_forwards_softplus_and_checkpoint_count`, which needs a driver.

### New and changed tests

- The bitwise assertions between chunk-parallel and exact-scan programs are now P6 readings.
- `two_kernel_family` mirrors the Cake seed rule and has cross-check tests.
- `test_source_retained_start_programs_are_the_round5_files` pins the SHA-256 of the 13 retained files.
- The `cu_seqlens`-vs-triple test judges the derived triple against the `cu_seqlens` form under P6 (`_assert_two_forms_p6`). It adds a sanity check at the state-dtype tolerance. It asserts the trusted-table triple bitwise equal to the `cu_seqlens` form inside the fused window.
- The out-of-range `seq_idx` test pins one two-kernel family across its clean / flagged pair. It runs once per family (`exact`, `exactpre`).
- `test_cake_ssd_combined_chunk_parallel_is_bitwise_the_exact_scan[bf16_triple_*]` expects `exactfused` for the trusted-cumsum triple inside the fused window.
- New CPU-only route cases cover four triple variants: derived, trusted, rewritten buffer, outside the window. A new prepare-vs-run test checks that both resolve the same workspace key.
- New GPU capture form `triple_cumsum`: prepare -> capture -> three bitwise replays, with `preprocess_grid == (0,1,1)`.

### Lint and pre-commit

- Pinned ruff 0.12.8 over the loader and both test files: `format --diff` prints 0 lines, and `check` reports "All checks passed!".
- The repository's pinned pre-commit (16 hooks: 11 ran, including ruff and mypy; 5 had no matching files) passes on this head with 0 rewrites, both with the branch config and with the current `main` config. The branch changes exactly the 44 files listed above and no other file.

## Performance

### Protocol

- 93 rows per arch, timed with CUPTI, cold L2 and 3 interleaved rounds on an exclusive node.
- The baseline arm is the previous release. Ratio = previous-release time / candidate time, so > 1 means the candidate is faster.
- Each row has two band readings. The same-run A/A band is max(twin, rr, 0.005). The frozen band was pre-registered before this release's measurements. A row fails if it falls below 1 − band.
- The verdict pass runs the 7 chunk-parallel rows in their own process. The disclosure pass runs all rows in the original order.
- CuTe and stock Triton run as reference arms in the same gate.

### GB300 (sm_103a)

| Pass | Tree | Rows | Geomean | Below same-run band | Below frozen band | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Verdict pass | c9 | 93 | 1.1568 | 0 | 0 | PASS |
| Disclosure pass (original order) | c9 | 93 | 1.1564 | 0 | 0 | PASS |
| Verdict pass | F1b | 93 | 1.1876 | 0 | 0 | PASS |

All three passes report `fails=0`. The lowest rows all sit inside their same-run band:

- c9 verdict pass: nem_v160x128_float32 0.9996, nem_v64x128_float32 0.9999 (band 0.005).
- c9 disclosure pass: nem_v64x128_float32 0.9988 (band 0.005).
- F1b verdict pass: nem_v64x128_float32 0.9994, nem_v64x128_bfloat16 0.9998, nem_v160x128_bfloat16 1.0001, nem_v160x128_float32 1.0004 (band 0.005). Also perf_batched_1x64 1.0006 (band 0.0079).

The c9 verdict pass reports `errors=255`. All of them come from the reference arms:

- 162 x CuTe `state_dtype must be one of [bf16, f16]` on f32-state rows
- 81 x CuTe `seqlen % 128` constraints (9 rows x 3 processes x 3 rounds)
- 12 x a Triton initial-states batch constraint (2 rows x 6)

The candidate and previous-release arms have 0 errors. The F1b verdict pass also reports `errors=255`.

**Per-class ranges, GB300, c9 tree**

| Class | Rows | Verdict pass | Disclosure pass |
|---|---|---|---|
| Chunk-parallel | 7 | 1.0040–1.0804 | 1.0075–1.0821 |
| Fused single-launch | 27 | 1.0407–2.0529 | 1.0418–2.0574 |
| of which one-chunk batched | 16 | 1.1482–2.0529 | 1.1569–2.0574 |
| Two-kernel, one chunk per item | 31 | 0.9996–1.0639 | 0.9988–1.0701 |
| Two-kernel, >= 2 chunks per item | 28 | 1.0131–1.0684 | 1.0098–1.0551 |

**F1b vs c9 loader, GB300, 7-row A/B**

Both arms use the same Cake head. The run used 3 rounds, CUPTI, cold L2 and `BENCH_MS 300`. Times are the median call in µs. Ratio = c9-loader time / F1b time, so > 1 means F1b is faster.

| Row | F1b µs | c9 loader µs | Ratio | Kernels F1b / c9 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| perf_varlen_1x1 | 8.576 | 14.176 | 1.6530 | 1 / 2 |
| perf_varlen_4x1 | 8.704 | 14.592 | 1.6765 | 1 / 2 |
| perf_varlen_8x1 | 9.408 | 15.360 | 1.6327 | 1 / 2 |
| perf_varlen_32x1 | 15.008 | 21.184 | 1.4115 | 1 / 2 |
| perf_varlen_4x8 | 28.320 | 32.960 | 1.1638 | 1 / 2 |
| perf_varlen_8x8 | 29.504 | 33.568 | 1.1377 | 1 / 2 |
| short_varlen_64_60 | 11.520 | 17.344 | 1.5056 | 1 / 2 |

- Geomean 1.4383. 0 rows below either band, `fails=0`, PASS. Same-run bands are <= 0.0253.
- `errors=9` come from the CuTe arm on short_varlen_64_60: `seqlen (124) must be divisible by chunk_size (128)`.
- On the c9 loader each row runs the preprocess kernel (3.7–4.1 µs) plus the main kernel. On F1b each row runs `exactfused_*` alone, with preprocess grid 0.

**Reference-arm ratios on the same gate, GB300** (reference time / candidate time)

| Arm | c9 verdict pass | F1b verdict pass |
|---|---|---|
| CuTe | min 2.379, geomean 4.269 | min 2.385, geomean 4.394 |
| stock Triton | min 3.290, geomean 14.616 | min 3.236, geomean 14.931 |

`errors` on reference arms are shape constraints of those arms, not candidate failures.

### B200 (sm_100a)

Same gate, same 93 rows, exclusive B200 node.

- c9 verdict pass: 93 rows, geomean 1.1052, 0 rows below the same-run band, 0 below the frozen band, `fails=0`, PASS. Its `errors=801` include 558 import errors of the stock Triton reference arm (a broken reference checkout on that node; the Triton column for c9 therefore comes from the supplementary pass below); the remaining 243 are the CuTe shape constraints. The candidate and previous-release arms have 0 errors.
- c9 disclosure pass (original row order, same tree): geomean 1.1049; 5 of 93 rows fall below the same-run band (short_varlen_1 0.9731, short_varlen_64_60 0.9846, nem_v4x128_float32 0.9850, perf_batched_1x16 0.9883, nem_v1x128_float32 0.9899), so this pass alone records `verdict_same_run=FAIL`. These rows are whole-call times of 11.9–32.0 µs; four are cpi=1 two-kernel rows and perf_batched_1x16 is a cpi=16 chunk-parallel look-back row. The preprocess cubins are byte-identical between the start and final arms, so the preprocess-ratio deviations are placement and launch-order effects; the same 5 rows sit inside the band in the verdict pass on the same tree (1.0056 / 1.0000 / 0.9990 / 0.9976 / 1.0021). The verdict pass governs; the disclosure pass is reported for completeness.
- F1b verdict pass: 93 rows, geomean 1.1245, 0 rows below the same-run band, 0 below the frozen band, `fails=0`, PASS. `errors=255` are reference-arm shape constraints (CuTe 243, Triton 12), not candidate failures.
- F1b 7-row A/B: geomean 1.2589, 0 rows below either band, `fails=0`, PASS. `errors=9` are the CuTe arm's chunk-size constraint on short_varlen_64_60, as on GB300.

**Reference-arm ratios on the same gate, B200** (reference time / candidate time). The c9 column comes from a supplementary verdict pass that adds the stock Triton arm (same 93 rows; geomean 1.1052, 0 rows below either band, PASS); the F1b column is the F1b verdict pass itself. Rows where an arm does not run are excluded.

| Arm | c9 (rows; min / median / max) | F1b verdict pass (rows; min / median / max) |
|---|---|---|
| CuTe | 66; 2.103 / 3.141 / 12.855 | 66; 2.100 / 3.253 / 12.835 |
| stock Triton | 91; 2.869 / 9.897 / 49.439 | 91; 2.876 / 9.954 / 49.082 |

### Eager one-wave launch gap

The target is an eager one-wave launch gap of p50 <= 2 µs on the one-wave rows. Fused rows launch once, so they read 0.00 µs.

- **GB300, c9 tree, shared node:** the fused k=1 rows read 0.00 µs (5/5), and 7/10 rows are <= 2 µs. The two-launch rows read 2.2–2.9 µs. The previous-release arm reads 1/10 on the same clause, so we treat this gap as platform-level.
- **GB300, F1b, exclusive node:** 8/10 rows meet the target, and perf_varlen_1x1 reads 0.00 µs. Two rows miss it: short_varlen_1 (2.69 µs) and short_varlen_127 (2.54 µs). Both are derived-triple two-kernel rows, not on the F1b path.
- **GB300, F1b, graph replay:** replay is bitwise 21/21. Four rows show a replay-span increase of +0.26…+0.42 µs. All four are derived-triple two-kernel rows.
- **B200, c9 tree, shared node:** 10/10 rows are <= 2 µs (0.00–0.86), and the two-launch rows read 0.29–0.86 µs. Graph replay is bitwise 21/21.

## Sanitizer

The tool is compute-sanitizer 2026.2.1.0. synccheck and racecheck run as separate bounded commands. The matrices ran on the c9 tree; they were not repeated on this PR's head, which changes no kernel source (`csrc/` is byte-identical between the c9 loader commit and this head; only the loader and the two test files differ). The Cake sanitizer wrapper now synchronizes the device before the worker exits. It also requires a `SANITIZE_DEVICE_SYNC` record, so racecheck records are no longer lost at exit.

**synccheck: STRICT_PASS.** This holds on both archs, for both the previous release and this release's Cake head. It covers every executed form:

- registered CLI `exact_scan` / `chunk_parallel` on 4 shapes
- worker subprocess
- single shape
- custom driver on 4 ring + 4 `_noring` shapes, including the preprocess kernel
- three-phase entry

**racecheck: INCONCLUSIVE (tool limitation).** INCONCLUSIVE is not a pass.

- Every call that reuses an aux-ring stage reports WAR records. Counts on this release's Cake head:
  - GB300: `exactpre_*` 5, look-back 9, three-phase 9, and 2 per shape for the fused program on large shapes.
  - B200: `exactpre_*` 5, look-back 9, three-phase 9, and 2/5/2/2 per shape in the custom driver.
- The fused program on the 3 small registered shapes (<= 2 chunks) reports 0 records. That is STRICT_PASS on both archs.
- Each record pairs two accesses to the same aux-ring stage (`smem_delta_all` / `smem_cumsum_all`). One is a loader-warp `STS`. The other is an `LDS` by pre_inter / pre_intra / epilogue.

Four pieces of evidence point to a tool limitation:

1. Source: the release chain is complete. Reads -> `bar.sync` -> one elected `mbarrier.arrive.release` -> writer `try_wait.acquire`.
2. Minimal reproducer under the same sanitizer: a race-free ring with an elected arrive (`elected`) reports 2 WAR. The same ring with per-thread arrives (`allarrive_both`) reports 0.
3. SASS: every write site is an aux-ring `STS/STS.128`.
4. Addresses: across 40 runs, 30.36 M displayed hazards fall 100 % inside each program's 2 KiB aux ring, on both archs.

`bar.sync` orders other threads' accesses before the elected arrive. racecheck 2026.2.1.0 does not count that arrive as releasing them. compute-sanitizer 2026.3.0.0 gives the same classification on both archs: the race-free elected-arrive control still reports 2 WAR and the per-thread-arrive control 0, and the production kernels report the same record sites (B200: one more record of the same site family on the three-phase kernel; the B200 `exactpre_*` single-shape run timed out at 1800 s under 2026.3.0.0).

This PR makes no kernel change for this finding. A follow-up evaluates per-thread `mbarrier.arrive` on the aux-ring empty side. That means init_count 2/1 -> 256/128, or 384 once pre_intra joins. The change would touch every program, including the 13 retained files. Its performance cost is untested.

The sanitizer statements in the PR #6330 description are corrected in a separate comment.

## End-to-end

We ran Nemotron-H-8B-Reasoning-128K BF16, TP1, through sglang on GB200. The run used the c9 loader and was not repeated on this PR's loader. The engine passes `cu_seqlens` only, and the loader change does not touch that path: with `cu_seqlens` the new fused condition reduces to the c9 condition, and the generated kernels are byte-identical between the two loaders. A 0-GPU host-route probe confirms it: over 88160 engine call shapes (128 and 16 heads, 1–64 sequences, 30 fixed packed-token totals plus 14 per-sequence tiers (30–44 distinct totals per sequence count, including empty sequences), bf16 and f32 state, with and without z, 4 SM-count / capability settings) both loaders select the same program in every case. The triple form with a caller cumsum differs in 1680 of 4416 probed shapes (two-kernel -> fused), which is the intended change.

| Arm | GSM8K-200 |
|---|---|
| Baseline | 0.895 |
| Previous release (start) | 0.905 |
| This release (c9) | 0.890 |

- This release − baseline = −0.005 (1 question).
- The previous release saw a band of 0.885–0.890. The baseline and previous-release arms read 1–3 questions above it.
- We attribute this excursion to batch-composition nondeterminism under `--parallel 64`. With identical software, stock-vs-stock drifted 0.885 -> 0.895. Single-request probes were byte-identical to an earlier run.
- All arms are NaN-free.
- sglang CPU route tests (`test/registered/unit/kernels/test_cake_mamba_sp_routes.py`) pass 47/47 on both the unpatched and the patched tree.
- sglang GPU route tests ran at sglang `328e862122a0f9133620ec7a3ca8b2867ffcbfcd` (`test/registered/kernels/ops/mamba/test_cake_ssd_combined.py`, 42 tests). The previous-release tree passes 42. The c9 tree gives 38 passed, 4 failed on both archs.
- The 4 failures are the two-form bitwise assertion `torch.equal(final_cu, final_tr)` in `test_route_call_cu_seqlens_at_engine_chunk_size_matches_triple_and_stock`. Routing is unchanged: the two forms run different programs for one-chunk items under the host route, so they are not bitwise there. The sglang pin bump carries the test fix (cross-form sanity at the state-dtype tolerance, each form against the fixed fp64 tolerance, and the bitwise clause with both forms pinned to the two-kernel family). With that fix the file passes 42/42 on both GB300 and B200 against this PR's loader code.

## Cake side

- The Cake-side export tool `tools/export_cake_mamba_ssd_combined.py --check` (Cake repository, not part of this PR) gives byte-identical output in the B200 and GB300 environments. It reports 13/13 retained files, 49 device / 5 host sources and table 12/12/12/6/6.
- Cake GPU tests (the Mamba SSD end-to-end slice of the kernel generator's GPU test suite): 78 passed on both archs.

## Bot commands and review plan

- At least 1 min after every push, post:
  - `@flashinfer-bot run tests/mamba/test_cake_ssd_combined.py tests/mamba/test_cake_ssd_combined_capture.py`
  - `/bot run`
- Every CodeRabbit thread gets an individual reply, including outside-diff comments.
- The branch contains only `csrc/cake_mamba_ssd_combined/**`, `flashinfer/mamba/cake_ssd_combined.py` and `tests/mamba/**`.

title: perf(cake_ssd_combined): capability-routed one-launch and tail-wave exact-scan programs for Blackwell
body:
Title: perf(cake_ssd_combined): capability-routed one-launch and tail-wave exact-scan programs for Blackwell

## Summary

This PR updates the cake backend of the Mamba2 SSD combined chunk-scan prefill (`SSDCombined(backend="cake")`) on Blackwell sm_100a (B200) and sm_103a (GB300). On sm_103a, the seq_idx triple form now runs as one launch, using exactone programs that build the sequence table in-kernel. On GB300 this measured A/B geomeans of 1.2906 and 1.2652 over two 17-row runs. Rows of 512 items, which left 13.5 % / 15.8 % of the SMs idle, now use 2-CTA pair programs that split one item across the pair (geomean 1.0124 on B200 and 1.0196 on GB300, 6-row set). Every consumer thread now releases the aux-ring "empty" mbarrier, so compute-sanitizer racecheck reports 0 records on the exact-scan, look-back and three-phase kernels (geomean 0.9977–1.0003).

## Changes

### 1. Per-reader aux-ring release (device sources only)
- Why: racecheck credits an `mbarrier.arrive.release` → `try_wait.acquire` chain only with the arriving thread's own earlier accesses. If `bar.sync` orders the accesses before a single elected arrive, racecheck does not credit them. As a result, each stage reuse was reported as a WAR record (aux-ring STS vs consumer LDS).
- The aux_empty init count changes from 2 to 384, so every consumer thread releases it.
- pre_inter: the elected arrive becomes a per-thread arrive.
- pre_intra: one extra arrive before `barrier.sync 2`.
- Epilogue: the aux_empty arrive moves out of the warp-12 elect block.
- This applies to the exact-scan, look-back and three-phase programs. There is no loader change.
- Micro-benchmark on GB300: −36.15 ns per release. The per-thread arrive is not slower.

### 2. Tail-wave pair programs (`79fbfcf37`, `3ec7ae76c`)
- Why: 512-item rows (perf_batched_64x4, perf_batched_64x16, perf_varlen_64x8, perf_varlen_64x32) ran 128 CTAs × 4 items on 148 (B200) / 152 (GB300) SMs.
- A whole-item 148-CTA grid was measured 1.003–1.072x slower (bandwidth sharing, same critical path).
- 2-CTA cluster pair: `cluster_dims (2,1,1)`, cta_group 1. tcgen05 and TMA stay CTA-local. The cluster only co-schedules the pair and gives DSM addressing of the peer's mbarrier.
- If a pair owns an odd number of items, rank 0 runs HEAD chunks [0,h) of the odd item. Rank 1 runs its whole items, then TAIL chunks [h,n). The split is taken only when it is worthwhile.
- The loader's `tail_selected` route is exactpre-only and sends these rows to six new exactpre `*_precomputed_tail` programs.
- The six `exactfused_*_tail` programs and the loader's `_FUSED_TAIL_*` entries are removed. `prepare()` takes the tail route only when `not fused`.
- Removing the fused tail programs left the other 55 exported programs unchanged (ident, render sha, status, smem, launch facts).

### 3. seq_idx triple form routed by compute capability (`7b898548b`)
- Varlen shapes that pass `seq_idx` in the triple form without a caller-provided cumsum (the loader has to derive the sequence table) are now routed by compute capability: on SM100 the new `exactmeta` programs (a light packed-varlen metadata kernel publishes the sequence tables, then the fused exact-scan main kernel runs: two launches, replacing the full preprocess kernel + two-kernel main kernel); on SM103 the one-launch `exactone` programs of section 4.
- Screening reading on B200 vs the previous programs: 17 rows (4 controls), geomean 1.0221, 10 rows faster by 1.3–7.7 %, 0 below band. `exactmeta` was measured on GB300 as well and rejected there (0.9704, 12 rows below band).

### 4. One-launch exactone on SM103 (`863b6c2b9`)
- On sm_103a, the fused varlen programs build the per-CTA sequence table in-kernel from the seq_idx triple (`TABLE_IN_KERNEL_*` forms).
- The two-kernel exactpre route (preprocess kernel + main kernel) becomes one launch, through 6 new exactone programs.
- `test_cake_ssd_combined_updates_caller_buffers` now asserts per capability. On SM103, the publish call runs the two-kernel program and writes the table into the caller buffers.

### Exported sources
- Diff vs `main` `5c5c44c3`: 54 files, +35723/−2709 (14 added, 3 modified, 37 device sources renamed with changes).
- Export gates: 185 checks, 0 failing.
- Programs (68): 37 changed, 12 carried, 6 alias, 12 new, 1 identical.
- Loader program table: exactfused 12, exactmeta 6, exactone 6, exactpre 18 entries. No fused `*_varlen_tail` program ships.

### Commits
- `79fbfcf37` perf(cake_ssd_combined): tail-wave pair programs for the two-kernel exact-scan family
- `7b898548b` perf(cake_ssd_combined): route the seq_idx triple form by compute capability
- `863b6c2b9` perf(cake_ssd_combined): one-launch seq_idx triple form on SM103 (exactone programs)
- `3ec7ae76c` test(cake_ssd_combined): the tail pair program against the other route rules
- `bfb505d86` perf(cake_ssd_combined): ship the capability-routed, one-launch and tail-wave exact-scan sources
- `202d416ef` test(cake_ssd_combined): pin the exact-scan persistent grid rule in a source test

## Testing / gates (done)

Each change was measured on its own against the previous shipped sources (`main` `5c5c44c3`), on sm_100a (B200) and sm_103a (GB300).

racecheck, compute-sanitizer 2026.3.0.0. Shapes: cp_b1h32c16, ck_b2x1000_z_bf16, dn95_b1x4096_z_bf16 and nem_v1024_bfloat16; look-back and three-phase add cp_b4h8c16.

| Kernel family | B200 records before → after | GB300 records before → after |
|---|---|---|
| exact-scan | 56 → 0 | 60 → 0 |
| look-back | 108 → 0 | 108 → 0 |
| three-phase | 127 → 0 | 126 → 0 |

- synccheck (strict): pass on both trees and both archs.
- Cross-tree determinism hashes (same GPU, 20 launches), both archs:
  - exact-scan: 22 equal / 0 different.
  - With look-back and three-phase: 31 equal / 0 different.
- exactone on GB300:
  - Determinism: 21 rows, 20 equal, 0 different, 1 skipped.
  - exactone hashes equal the exactpre hashes on the re-routed varlen shapes vpacked_z_bf16 and vpacked_noz_f32.
  - synccheck (strict): pass.
- `pytest tests/mamba/test_cake_ssd_combined.py` (module + capture) on the tree with changes 3 and 4:

| Arch | Passed | Skipped | Failed |
|---|---|---|---|
| GB300 | 516 | 2 | 0 |
| B200 | 513 | 5 | 0 |

- Source-level tests on this branch (CPU): 345 passed / 12 skipped / 0 failed, with the 32 GPU-only tests excluded on the CPU host.
  - The GPU-only tests are covered by the GPU module + capture run on this branch, listed below.

A/B vs the previous shipped sources:

| Change | Rows | B200 geomean | GB300 geomean | Rows below band (B200 / GB300) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Per-reader release, exact-scan | 19 | 1.0001 | 0.9983 | 0 / 0 |
| Per-reader release, + look-back / three-phase | 14 | 1.0003 | 0.9977 | 0 / 1 |

## Still running / filled before merge

These gates run on this branch (`main` `5c5c44c3` + the six commits above).

The 93-row A/B acceptance gate runs against the previous shipped sources on an exclusive machine per arch:
- 3 rounds, with an A/A control process.
- A row passes if its ratio is >= 1.00 − band. The band is the larger of the run's measured noise bands and 0.005.

- 93-row A/B acceptance gate, GB300: PASS on the verdict reading (same-run A/A band) after the pre-registered focused re-run. First pass (93 rows x 3 rounds): geomean 1.046, 3 rows below the same-run band (nem_v1000_bfloat16 0.986, nem_v2048_bfloat16 0.993, nem_v8x64_bfloat16 0.9945; all cu_seqlens two-launch rows, per-launch kernel ratios >= 0.993, the remainder is inter-launch gap), 5 below the frozen round-6 band. ## 📌 Description

The split RANK_MAJOR/HT bridge maps non-local routes to the first local expert with zero weight. Those routes still enter expert compute. Pass the global expert count into the bridge and map masked routes to a valid remote expert, so the existing runner filter excludes them before the GEMMs.
