title: [Feature]: sm120 Cake MegaMoE for PCIe hosts: MXFP4-activation (W4A4) variant, int8/FP8 return codec, switch-level dedupe
body:
### Before submitting

- [x] I have searched existing issues and this request has not been filed yet.

### Problem

On PCIe-only sm_120 hosts (8 GPUs behind two PCIe Gen5 switches, no NVLink; ~49-55 GB/s per direction on the x16 links and on the inter-switch fabric) `sm120_mxfp4_mxfp8_bf16_cake` is slower per MoE layer than an unfused DeepEP-style all-to-all + DeepGEMM grouped-GEMM path, because its wire format carries roughly twice the bytes:

- dispatch records carry FP8 activations: 5120 + 160 (+224 header) B per row at H=5120, where an MXFP4 dispatch carries 2560 + 160 B;
- expert results return through the lossless BF16 codec, ~7.8 KB per route, where an int8 combine (per-128 fp32 scale) carries 5.3 KB;
- records are deduplicated per destination rank only; on a two-switch host, one copy per destination switch with the partial sums reduced inside the switch before crossing sends 2.2x fewer cross-switch bytes at EP8.

Measured at the DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash routed geometry (E=384, H=5120, I=2304, top-k 6; EP8, 2048 tokens/rank, 6-layer CUDA graph, slowest rank, us/layer; the local-memory guard was raised to 16 B so the kernel loads at this geometry, see #6755):

| path | uniform | hot (one rank 2.5x) | recorded routing |
|---|---|---|---|
| unfused: all-to-all (one copy per destination switch, in-switch partial-sum reduction) + DeepGEMM grouped GEMM, **MXFP4 activations, int8 combine** | 3850 | 6243 | 4390 |
| same unfused path with **FP8 activations** (per-128 fp32 scales), int8 combine | 5623 | 9449 | 6447 |
| cake, `transport_table` = LSA inside each switch / GIN across (explicit table) | 4745-4936 (two runs) | 7478 | 5677 |
| cake `all_gin` / `all_lsa` | 6067 / 6050 | 7718 / 7615 | 7632 / 6247 |

Against the same-precision unfused path the fused kernel is 14-26% faster, so the overlap works; against the MXFP4-activation path it is 20-28% slower. Switching only the unfused path's activations from MXFP4 to FP8 moves its dispatch from 692 to 1328 us/layer (per-card egress 23.9 -> 46.4 MB/layer), so on these links bytes are time. Numerics for reference (rel L2 vs an fp32 reference with unquantized activations, 512 rows/rank): cake 4.7%, FP8-activation unfused path 4.8%, MXFP4-activation path 22%; cake vs the kernel-boundary oracle of `tests/moe_ep/test_moe_ep_sm120_w4a8_cake_mega.py` 1.6e-4 .. 3.2e-4.

### Requested outcome

A configuration of the sm120 Cake MegaMoE whose bytes on the wire match the unfused W4A4 path on PCIe hosts:

1. an MXFP4-activation variant (e2m1 + UE8M0 per-32 scales, `mma.sync kind::mxf4nvf4`): dispatch rows become 2560 + 160 B and both GEMMs run at the FP4 rate instead of the FP8 rate;
2. an int8 (per-128 fp32 scale) or FP8 return option in place of the lossless BF16 codec, selectable per deployment, with the combine summing the dequantized partials;
3. optionally, topology-aware dedupe in the transport table: one copy per destination LSA group (PCIe switch or host) with in-group fan-out on dispatch and in-group partial-sum reduction on return.

(1) + (2) alone remove the byte handicap, which is the whole 20-28% gap in the table above; what remains after that is the overlap efficiency of the protocol on PCIe (in these runs the kernel hides about a third of the communication time). The kernel's numerics already match the unfused FP8 path, so the request is about the transport format, not a new precision recipe.

### Target hardware

SM120 (RTX PRO 6000, RTX 50-series)

### Inference engine

vLLM

### Affected model or model family

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (MXFP4 routed experts: E=384, H=5120, I=2304, top-k 6, 1 shared expert)

### Workload and configuration

- Data type and quantization: MXFP4 expert weights (e2m1 + UE8M0 per-32) from the checkpoint; activations MXFP4 in our production path, FP8 (per-128 fp32 scale) in the same-precision control and FP8 (UE8M0 per-32) inside Cake; int8 combine (per-128 fp32 scale) on the unfused path, lossless BF16 codec in Cake
- Batch size or request concurrency: prefill, 2048 tokens per rank per step (also 384 and 1024 for the M64 schedule)
- Sequence lengths or token counts: 2048 tokens per rank per layer; routings: uniform, one rank 2.5x hot, and a recorded production routing
- Parallelism: DP8 / EP8 on one host (TP1, PP1); EP16/EP32 across hosts is the next step (GIN) and was not measured
- Relevant shapes: hidden 5120, intermediate 2304, 384 experts (48 per rank at EP8), top-k 6, swiglu_limit 10, max_tokens_per_rank 2048; 8x sm_120 72 GB GPUs, 110 SMs, two PCIe Gen5 switches x 4 GPUs, 2x 400G RDMA NICs per switch
- Environment: output of `python -m flashinfer.collect_env` is attached as a comment on #6755 (flashinfer 399b6c1d source tree, torch 2.13 + NCCL 2.30.7, CUDA 13.3)

### Current workaround

We run the unfused path: DeepEP-style all-to-all with MXFP4 activations on dispatch, DeepGEMM `m_grouped_fp8_fp4_gemm_nt_contiguous` (FP4 x FP4) for both GEMMs, int8 combine, one copy per destination PCIe switch with in-switch partial-sum reduction. Its limitation is that communication and expert GEMMs are serial (about 1.97 ms + 1.93 ms per layer at this shape); a fused kernel could hide most of the smaller term, which is exactly what Cake does, but only if it does not double the bytes first.

### Impact

Throughput, Latency

### Acceptance criteria

- At E=384 / H=5120 / I=2304 / top-k 6, EP8, 2048 tokens per rank on an 8-GPU PCIe sm_120 host, the fused layer is not slower than the unfused MXFP4-activation path (3850 us/layer uniform, 4390 us/layer on recorded routing in our runs) and keeps the overlap gain measured against the same-precision unfused path (>= 10%).
- Per-card dispatch bytes at that shape ~24 MB/layer (MXFP4 rows) instead of ~46 MB; return bytes per route <= 5.3 KB.
- Correctness: passes `tests/moe_ep/test_moe_ep_sm120_w4a8_cake_mega.py`-style oracle checks (rel L2 <= 2%) for the new activation/return formats, protocol_error stays 0, CUDA-graph replay bit-identical to eager, across EP4/8/16 and both row schedules.

### Related work, dependencies, or suggested scope

- #6755: at this geometry the shipped build spills one register (STACK 16 B) and the backend refuses to load the workspace; the measurements above used `LOCAL_BYTES_LIMIT=16` in the test rig. That needs to be resolved first for any sm120 Cake variant to be usable on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash.
- #6346 (the kernel), `kernel_src/sm120/cake_mxfp4_megamoe/README.md` (return codec, transport table, MOE_LSA_COPIERS).
- The SM100/SM107 `nvfp4_nvfp4` cutedsl families are the only W4A4 moe_ep kernels today; they use the NVFP4 recipe (e4m3 per-16 + per-tensor scale) rather than the MXFP4 checkpoint recipe (UE8M0 per-32) that the sm120 Cake weights already consume, so a W4A4 sm120 variant would ideally keep the MXFP4 recipe end to end.
- The dedupe/reduction scheme in (3) is what DeepEP's hybrid (two-hop) kernels do for NVLink+RDMA and what our PCIe variant does per switch; the per-pair transport table already carries the LSA/GIN topology needed to derive the groups.

### Timing or release need

_No response_

title: [Bugfix][DeepEP] Close GIN barrier data-visibility race in vendored DeepEP (per-context signals + NVLink fence)
body:
## Summary

DeepEP `d4f41e4e` (the commit we pin in `docker/Dockerfile` / `tools/ep_kernels/install_python_libraries.sh`) has a data-visibility race in `gin_barrier_wo_local_sync`, the completion barrier of low-latency dispatch/combine over NCCL GIN (GDAKI):

- The barrier publishes completion with a **single context-0 signal**, while dispatch/combine data rides **contexts 1..N as RDMA puts** and, for same-node peers, **NVLink TMA stores** to LSA symmetric memory.
- Signals and puts on different QPs are not ordered at the receiving NIC (confirmed by NVIDIA in nccl#2302; NCCL's own `ncclGinBarrier` with `ncclGinAllContexts` exists for exactly this failure mode), and GIN signals are not ordered with NVLink stores from other threads (fixed upstream in deepseek-ai/DeepEP#715, not in `d4f41e4e`).
- The receiver's copy epilogue (PDL-launched) can therefore read **stale raw-buffer rows from the previous dispatch**: phantom/missing expert routes, double-assigned slots, unwritten `recv_x` rows, occasionally OOB slots — the latter surfacing as the `combine_impl` illegal-memory-access crashes seen in DP=8 direct-mode nightlies.

Root-cause evidence (pristine DeepEP, host-side audit, zero kernel instrumentation): internal repro `repros/pr57991-waldorf-20260928/.../count-discrepancy-audit-20261002/REPORT.md`.

## The patch

`tools/ep_kernels/patches/deepep-gin-barrier-data-visibility.patch` — one file (`deep_ep/include/deep_ep/common/comm.cuh`), two changes mirroring shipped upstream fixes:

1. **Per-context signals**: after the existing flush + grid sync, signal every peer on every GIN context (`ginContextCount × kNumRanks` signals) and wait on the per-(context, signal id) slots. A signal posted on context `c` is SQ-FIFO-ordered behind all WQEs previously reserved on context `c`, covering the RDMA data puts. Mirrors NCCL's `ncclGinBarrierSession` with `ncclGinAllContexts` (`nccl_device/impl/gin_barrier__funcs.h`).
2. **`fence.acq_rel.sys` for world-team barriers** before the barrier signal, so same-node peers' NVLink TMA stores are visible before the GIN signal is published. Mirrors upstream DeepEP #715 (11d1cab), which postdates our pinned commit.

Applied in `install_python_libraries.sh` after the DeepEP clone, guarded to the pinned commit `d4f41e4e` (skips on any other ref) and idempotent (grep guard). `docker/Dockerfile` copies the new `tools/ep_kernels/patches` dir into the extensions-build stage.

## Why this is not duplicating an existing PR

No vLLM PR touches the DeepEP barrier. Upstream DeepEP has neither an issue nor a PR for this (checked 2026-10-03); v2.5 (93eb6eb) has the #715 fence but still signals on context 0 only, so it closes only one of the two holes.

## Test commands and results

- Cluster validation of this exact patch (wheel built from pristine d4f41e4e + patch, NCCL 2.30.7, 3×H200 4+2+2 DP=8 direct mode, DeepSeek-V4-Flash `--enforce-eager`, host-side audit harness): **in progress** — will update with results.
  - Context: per-context signals alone (without the NVLink fence) did **not** pass validation — faulted with the same stale-row signature at a same-node (NVLink) sender pair within ~25 min, which is what motivated adding the fence. Pristine DeepEP faulted during warmup within ~3.5 min.
- `bash -n` + pre-commit (shellcheck) on the install script change; `patch --dry-run` verified against a fresh d4f41e4e checkout.

## Model evaluation results

None yet — behavior-neutral change intended (ordering only), but will run the audit + a serving smoke before marking ready.

## AI assistance

Prepared with AI assistance (patch authoring, validation harness, PR text); root-cause evidence produced by the cluster runs referenced above.

title: [Bugfix][Engine] Skip stream-interval buffering for pooling requests
body:
## Summary

Pooling/embedding `RequestState`s are built with `detokenizer = None` (streaming detokenization is meaningless for pooling output). With `--stream-interval > 1`, the `assert self.detokenizer is not None` fired on **every** finished pooling request, crashing the engine via "AsyncLLM output_handler failed".

The buffering block is now skipped (not asserted) for pooling requests — stream-interval buffering has no effect on pooling output.

## Repro

Start a pooling server with `--stream-interval 8` and send any `PoolingParams` request → `AssertionError` on every request.

Signed-off-by: simpleqt <89645338+simpleqt@users.noreply.github.com>

title: [Bugfix][MoE] Swizzle mxfp8 activation scales after DP/EP dispatch for FlashInfer CUTLASS
body:
FIX #42118

## Purpose

`FLASHINFER_CUTLASS_MXFP4_MXFP8` returns NaN logits for every request when
`data_parallel_size > 1`. The failure is silent: the server stays healthy and generates
at full speed, but completions decode to empty strings and GSM8K scores 0.000. The
quickest check is a completions request with `"logprobs"`, which fails with HTTP 400
("Out of range float values are not JSON compliant: nan").

The CUTLASS kernel expects mxfp8 activation scales in the swizzled 128x4 layout. The
DP/EP prepare paths quantize with row-major scales so they can ride the a2a next to the
hidden states, then swizzle afterwards, but that step only handled nvfp4. So mxfp8
scales reached the kernel row-major and it read wrong e8m0 block exponents. With dp=1
the scales are quantized directly into the swizzled layout, which is why the existing
tests never caught this.

The same gap exists in `naive_dp_ep.py` and in both `flashinfer_nvlink` prepare/finalize
backends. This PR moves the nvfp4-only restore logic into a shared
`restore_dispatched_scale_layout()` in `fused_moe/utils.py`, routes all three backends
through it, and enables it for mxfp8 using the same fused `block_scale_interleave`
kernel the nvfp4 path already used (bit-identical to quantizing directly into the
swizzled layout, covered by the new test). Backends that take row-major scales
(`FLASHINFER_TRTLLM_MXFP4_MXFP8`) pass through unchanged, and nvfp4 behavior is
unchanged.

Not a duplicate: #42133 addresses the same issue but has been conflicted and inactive
since May, predates the prepare_finalize restructure and the NVLink backends, and uses
a multi-pass torch swizzle where this PR reuses the existing fused kernel. Checked
`gh pr list --state open` for "mxfp8 scale swizzle", "block_scale_interleave", and the
issue number; #42133 is the only overlap. #47733 touches the same nvlink
prepare/finalize files for a different scale bug (per-tensor FP8); happy to rebase
whichever lands second.

AI disclosure: developed with AI assistance (Claude). I reviewed every changed line and
validated the change end-to-end on hardware; test commands and results below.

## Test Plan

New regression test (fails on main, passes with this PR; needs a CUDA GPU with
flashinfer installed):

```bash
pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_mxfp8_dp_scale_swizzle.py
```

End-to-end repro on 2 GPUs with open weights:

```bash
vllm serve openai/gpt-oss-20b \
  --moe-backend flashinfer_cutlass \
  --quantization-config '{"moe":{"activation":"mxfp8"}}' \
  --tensor-parallel-size 1 --data-parallel-size 2 --enable-expert-parallel \
  --max-model-len 4096 --disable-custom-all-reduce

curl localhost:8000/v1/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"openai/gpt-oss-20b","prompt":"17*23=","max_tokens":8,"temperature":0,"logprobs":2}'
```

The `--quantization-config` override is needed because plain `flashinfer_cutlass`
selects the BF16-activation variant for gpt-oss, which does not boot on sm_120.

## Test Result

Verified fail to pass against main `5b3762a7f`, with serve logs gated on
`Using 'FLASHINFER_CUTLASS_MXFP4_MXFP8'`:

| platform | config | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| 8x RTX 5090 (sm_120) | gpt-oss-20b, DP4 and DP2 | HTTP 400 nan | pass |
| 2x B200 (sm_100) | gpt-oss-20b, DP2, `--enforce-eager` | HTTP 400 nan | pass |
| 8x RTX 5090 (sm_120) | gpt-oss-20b, TP4 dp=1 control | pass (bug is DP-only) | pass |

Model eval: GSM8K on DeepSeek-V4-Flash (stock MXFP4, DP4xTP2+EP, the config this was
found in) scores 0.000 with the bug and matches its TP8 baseline within noise with
this PR.

Regression checks: the nvfp4 path (DeepSeek-V4-Flash-NVFP4 under the same DP topology)
behaves identically with and without this PR, and the unit test covers the TRTLLM
row-major passthrough.

The NVLink backends use the same unit-tested helper but were not serve-tested for lack
of hardware access; a check on B200/GB200 with
`--all2all-backend flashinfer_nvlink_{one,two}_sided` would be welcome.

title: [MoE] Refine FlashInfer one-sided All2All integration
body:
## Purpose

Refine the FlashInfer NVLink one-sided All2All integration for DeepSeek Blockwise FP8 MoE and sequence parallelism.

- Describe one-sided activation payloads explicitly in bytes for BF16, NVFP4, MXFP8, and DeepSeek Blockwise FP8.
- Dispatch E4M3 activations with FP32 1x128 scales and feed the received layout directly to the FlashInfer TRT-LLM DeepSeekFp8/BlockMajorK kernel.
- Validate activation and scale shapes before converting scales from `[M, K/128]` to the TRT-LLM `[K/128, M]` layout.
- Enable MoE sequence parallelism for `flashinfer_nvlink_one_sided`, avoiding routing and compute on TP-replicated post-attention tokens.
- Document and exercise DeepSeek Blockwise FP8 support in the existing MoE and MNNVL test matrices.

No kernel-warmup changes are included because current upstream `main` already provides generalized distributed FlashInfer autotuning and persistent-cache synchronization.

### Duplicate-work check

No issue number was supplied, so an issue-specific lookup was not applicable. I checked open PRs with:

```bash
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search 'FlashInfer one-sided All2All'
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search 'DeepSeek Blockwise FP8 FlashInfer'
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search 'sequence parallel FlashInfer one sided'
```

The related open PRs are distinct:

- #47733 handles per-tensor FP8 scaling, invalid expert IDs, and communicator cleanup; it does not add E4M3 activation dispatch with FP32 1x128 scales, TRT-LLM BlockMajorK integration, or sequence parallelism.
- #42034 only changes the one-sided padding sentinel for local expert maps.
- #42133 handles delayed MXFP8 scale swizzling for FlashInfer CUTLASS.

## Test Plan

- Run all pre-commit hooks on the changed files.
- Compile every changed Python file.
- Check the patch for whitespace errors.
- Validate DeepSeek Blockwise FP8 payload sizing and TRT-LLM scale layout with focused assertions.
- Run a reproducible model evaluation on a public checkpoint.

## Test Result

Passed all configured pre-commit hooks on the changed files, including ruff check/format, typos, markdownlint, mypy, SPDX, forbidden-import, configuration, and API checks:

```bash
.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \
  docs/design/moe_kernel_features.md \
  tests/distributed/test_mnnvl_alltoall.py \
  tests/kernels/moe/test_moe_layer.py \
  vllm/config/parallel.py \
  vllm/distributed/device_communicators/all2all.py \
  vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/all2all_utils.py \
  vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/experts/trtllm_fp8_moe.py \
  vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/prepare_finalize/flashinfer_nvlink_one_sided.py
```

Passed:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m py_compile \
  tests/distributed/test_mnnvl_alltoall.py \
  tests/kernels/moe/test_moe_layer.py \
  vllm/config/parallel.py \
  vllm/distributed/device_communicators/all2all.py \
  vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/all2all_utils.py \
  vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/experts/trtllm_fp8_moe.py \
  vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/prepare_finalize/flashinfer_nvlink_one_sided.py

git diff --check origin/main...HEAD
```

A focused Python assertion script covering BF16, NVFP4, MXFP8, and DeepSeek Blockwise FP8 dispatch byte layouts plus the TRT-LLM `[M, K/128]` to `[K/128, M]` scale conversion passed.

The repository-wide collection command below could not run in this CPU development environment because the installed `xgrammar` lacks `normalize_tool_choice` and the CUDA flash-attention extension is unavailable:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q --collect-only \
  tests/distributed/test_mnnvl_alltoall.py \
  tests/kernels/moe/test_moe_layer.py
```

### Model evaluation

Full 1,319-example GSM8K on public `Qwen/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-FP8`, using 8 B300
GPUs with TP2 x DP4 / EP8. The runtime used this PR plus the Qwen3Next SP
correctness fix from #50685; that fix is not part of this PR.

Common settings: `flashinfer_trtllm`, FlashInfer autotune enabled,
`max_num_batched_tokens=4096`, `max_num_seqs=64`, 5-shot greedy decoding,
`max_gen_toks=16384`, and 256 concurrent requests. Only the All2All backend
changed. The task used `"\nQuestion:"` instead of stock lm-eval's broad
`"Question:"` stop to avoid terminating inside model reasoning.

| All-to-all backend | Flexible exact match | Strict exact match |
|---|---:|---:|
| `allgather_reducescatter` | 95.75% (1263/1319) | 92.49% (1220/1319) |
| `flashinfer_nvlink_one_sided` | 95.00% (1253/1319) | 90.98% (1200/1319) |

Both runs completed without retries or engine errors. The flexible-score gap
is 10 samples and is not statistically significant (`p=0.143`). Per-sample
review and a repeated AG/RS run found trajectory and formatting variation, but
no systematic one-sided correctness failure.

## AI assistance

AI assistance was used for code exploration, cherry-pick conflict resolution, compatibility review, validation, and PR drafting. The human submitter must review every changed line, understand the change end-to-end, and be able to defend it before merging.

title: [SM120] Field report: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash in production on 8x RTX PRO 6000 (PCIe, no NVLink) - working config, measured throughput, rejected topologies
body:
## Summary

Field data from running **DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash** as a production SGLang backend on **8× RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Max-Q (SM120, 96 GB, PCIe-only — no NVLink)**, including the *only* topology we could get to start, measured prefill/decode, a speculative-decoding A/B, and the configuration traps that cost us real experiments. Posting because SM120 + V4.1-Flash users currently have to rediscover all of this from scratch.

Full write-up (with methodology and reproduction artifacts): https://github.com/Lei-010/hermes-agent/blob/main/docs/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-SM120-Performance-and-Production-Config.md

Related: vLLM field report https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/56700 (same hardware, vLLM side), vLLM https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/56892 (SM120 bug/perf tracker).

## What works

```bash
docker run --gpus all -d --name dsv41 \
  --shm-size=64g --ipc=host --network host \
  --restart unless-stopped \
  -e TP_SIZE=8 -e DP_SIZE=1 -e EP_SIZE=8 \
  -e SPEC_ALGORITHM=dspark -e DSPARK_BLOCK_SIZE=6 \
  -e CHUNKED_PREFILL_SIZE=2048 \
  -v /ssd/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash:/model \
  <sglang image>
```

Effective `server_args` (verified at runtime via `/get_server_info`):

| Parameter | Value |
|---|---|
| `tp_size` / `ep_size` / `dp_size` | 8 / 8 / 1 |
| `speculative_algorithm` | DSPARK, `speculative_dspark_block_size = 6` |
| `chunked_prefill_size` | 2048 |
| `context_length` | 1,048,576 |
| `kv_cache_dtype` | `fp8_e4m3` |
| `mem_fraction_static` | 0.72 |
| `max_running_requests` | 16 |
| `attention_backend` / `moe_runner_backend` | `dsv4` / `flashinfer_mxfp4` |
| CUDA graph decode / prefill | full (max_bs 16) / **disabled** |

**TP8/EP8 is not a preference — it is the only layout that starts** (see "Topologies SGLang rejects" below).

## Measured throughput (cold, single stream, tokens from `usage`, not SSE chunk counts)

128K cold prefill:

| Config | tok/s |
|---|---|
| `chunked_prefill_size=2048` (production) | **6,853** |
| same config re-run | 6,765 (−1.3%) |
| flashmla prefill backend | 6,845 |
| fused-MoE all-reduce | 6,828 |
| `chunked_prefill_size=4096` | 6,301 |
| `chunked_prefill_size=1024` | 6,012 |

32K prompt: ≈7,196 tok/s. GPU util ≈87% at 220 W of 600 W → **communication-bound on PCIe**, not compute-bound. ~7K tok/s looks like the ceiling for this board without NVLink.

Radix/prefix cache is the only large multiplier: cache-hit prefill **0.34 s for a 112K-token prefix ≈ 325K tok/s (≈39×)**.

Decode (client path over SSH tunnel, production config): prose 93.9 tok/s, structured/JSON 134.1 tok/s, TTFT 143–169 ms.

## DSPARK A/B (block_size=2, clean legs, each verified via `server_info` + acceptance length)

| Prompt class | DSPARK ON | DSPARK OFF |
|---|---|---|
| prose | 76.5–78.9 tok/s | 36.4–36.5 tok/s |
| structured | 120.3–120.5 tok/s | 36.5 tok/s |
| `accept len` | 3.0 tokens/step | 1.0 |

With DSPARK off the model flattens to ~36.5 tok/s regardless of prompt class — speculation is the difference between usable and unusable latency on this hardware. Production ships `block_size=6` (structured ≈237–252 tok/s vs 120 at block 2).

## Traps that cost us experiments (SGLang-specific)

1. **`--enable-expert-parallel` is a vLLM flag** — SGLang takes `ep_size`; the vLLM spelling is rejected outright.
2. **`docker run` must pass `TP_SIZE`/`DP_SIZE`/`EP_SIZE` explicitly.** Without `-e`, the container silently serves TP8 defaults and your "new" config never happens (we recorded a full sweep of false data this way before adding a config gate).
3. **`ep_size ≤ tp_size`** or the MoE rank computation divides by zero: `moe_ep_rank = tp_rank % (tp_size // moe_dp_size) // (tp_size // moe_dp_size // ep_size)`.
4. **DSPARK + DP attention requires `--enable-dp-lm-head`** — but is unreachable on this model anyway (next section).

## Topologies SGLang rejects on this model

| Attempt | Result |
|---|---|
| DP2 × TP4 (any EP) | `ValueError: V4.1 vision currently supports TP/EP without DP, CP, PP or MoE A2A` — both replicas die within ~70 s |
| prefill context-parallel | same class of rejection |
| `--enable-dp-attention` alone | silently no DP group (`dp_size: 1`) — looks fine, isn't |

Other SM120 gaps we hit: MSCCL++ (`_tune` kernel crash), FlashInfer all-reduce fusion, `flashmla_sparse_q8`, and CUDA-graph capture for **prefill** (crashes even with DSPARK off, i.e. unrelated to speculation).

## Operational notes

- A defunct container can survive a single `docker rm -f`; the next `docker run` then fails on the name conflict while an orphaned engine process keeps the port and answers health checks — which silently mislabels the next experiment. Loop `docker rm -f` until the container is gone **and** nothing listens on the port.
- A parse failure must never satisfy an "expected config" assertion, or a server that has not started yet gets recorded as "spec disabled".
- Verify intended config from the server (`/get_server_info`) before timing anything; discard legs that fail the gate rather than recording them.

## Not established

No 24 h soak (numbers come from a working day of production use), block sizes 4/8/12 not re-measured with the fixed sweep tool, and >32K prefill/long-context degradation not characterised.

title: github:sgl-project/sglang:39664 fetched implementation patch
[Feat] [NVIDIA] flashinfer_megamoe: SM120 prefill support with FlashInfer's cake MegaMoE backend (DeepSeek-V4-Flash)
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

<!-- PR title: [Type] scope: title, or [Type] [Hardware] scope: title.
Type: Feat, Fix, Refactor, Perf, Doc, Test, CI, or Chore.
Scope: any module or model name (no fixed list or letter-case restriction), e.g. attention, qwen3, or flash-attn.
Hardware: optional single tag without spaces. Use uppercase hardware tags (AMD, NVIDIA, NPU, MI300X), except for exactly these four spellings: Intel, Apple, Huawei, Ascend.
Title: no letter-case restriction.
Reverts: use GitHub's default title, Revert "original title".
Examples: [Fix] attention: Fix KV cache indexing; [Perf] [AMD] flash-attn: Optimize decode performance. -->

Co-authors: @jychen21 @AichenF
Submitted by: @GnohzZ 

> **Draft / dependency scope:** this is opt-in, experimental SM120 support requiring a FlashInfer source build containing flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6346 (validated at `399b6c1d31a13f38dd827018f89c6a04c8487acb`). The default FlashInfer `0.7.1` pin and Docker/CI dependencies remain unchanged. An older build gives an explicit startup error only when SM120 MegaMoE is selected; the regular SM120 backend remains available. The cookbook includes a fixed-revision source-install recipe. We propose reviewing this guarded integration ahead of a dependency release; out-of-box support and validation against a released dependency will follow a coordinated version bump. The candidate is rebased onto main `2528cd2b91`, including CI maintenance base `ff8d964cf5b6`.

## Motivation

`--moe-a2a-backend flashinfer_megamoe` currently requires SM100. FlashInfer #6346 added `sm120_mxfp4_mxfp8_bf16_cake`, a fused EP all-to-all + MXFP4 x MXFP8 expert-compute kernel for SM120 (RTX PRO Blackwell) that runs through the same `flashinfer.moe_ep.MoEEpMegaLayer` API this backend already uses. This PR wires it into the existing `flashinfer_megamoe` path for FP4-expert checkpoints, starting with DeepSeek-V4-Flash.

The kernel targets **prefill**. On 4x RTX PRO 5000 Blackwell (72 GB, PCIe) it roughly doubles prefill throughput over `--moe-runner-backend flashinfer_mxfp4` at the same TP4 / attention-DP4 layout, while decode with a few requests per rank is slower (numbers below). The recommended use is the prefill server of a PD-disaggregated deployment, with decode on the existing SM120 recipe; the server logs this at startup when it is not a PD prefill server.

The PR also fixes a static-EPLB bug on DeepSeek's `forward_normal` path, which serves `flashinfer_megamoe` (SM100 included) and the plain TP MoE: it only mapped logical to physical expert ids with `--enable-eplb`, so `--init-expert-location` alone (which also selects a dispatch algorithm) left the router's logical ids pointing at the physical layout the weights were loaded in.

## Modifications

1. **[Fix] `models/deepseek_v2.py`**: `DeepseekV2MoE._normal_path_dispatch_info()` always builds `ExpertLocationDispatchInfo` on non-NextN layers, as the DeepEP path already does. `init_new` returns `None` without a dispatch algorithm, so the default path is unchanged.
2. **SM120 branch of `flashinfer_megamoe`** (`layers/moe/flashinfer_megamoe.py`, `arg_groups/moe_hook.py`, `environ.py`):
   - Platform gate: SM120 with compute capability exactly 12.0, FP4 experts, EP >= 2, and a FlashInfer build exporting `Sm120_Mxfp4_Mxfp8_Bf16_Cake_MegaMoeConfig` (clear error otherwise). `--enable-eplb` is rejected (the packed scales are not expert-major); speculative decoding without an explicit `--speculative-moe-runner-backend` is rejected (the default draft runner `flashinfer_trtllm` is SM100-only). Settings the SM120 kernel cannot honor fail at startup instead of after the model loads: an unknown transport table, `NCCL_CUMEM_ENABLE=0`, the SM100-only `SGLANG_FLASHINFER_MEGAMOE_COMBINE_DTYPE` / `..._IN_KERNEL_FC2_REDUCE`, and a per-rank prefill chunk or CUDA-graph batch larger than the workspace (`validate_flashinfer_megamoe_sm120_token_budget`). SM100 behaviour is unchanged.
   - `NCCL_CUMEM_ENABLE=1` by default on this path: the kernel joins the EP group's NCCL communicator through NCCL's Device API, which needs cuMem buffers (SGLang otherwise sets it to 0). Same pattern as the `deepep_v2` branch.
   - Weights: FlashInfer's own preprocessing (`preprocess_sm120_mxfp4_mxfp8_cake_mega_weights`). FC1 is a gate/up row interleave of `w13` and is written back into `w13`; FC1/FC2 alias the layer weights, so the experts stay resident once. The float32 (E8M0-widened) checkpoint scales are converted exactly to UE8M0 bytes and replaced by the packed kernel scales.
   - Forward: one pooled workspace; each call stages `compile_tokens_per_rank = max(get_dp_global_num_tokens())`, identical on every EP rank, so there is no per-layer routing all-gather / host sync, and each decode CUDA-graph batch size captures its own bucket. `MegaMoeTunedForward` is not used on SM120 (it would build one compiled kernel + NCCL window set per profiled capacity). Router ids are widened to int64 for this kernel. The kernel's `protocol_error` flag (BF16 return-codec overflow) is not read on the hot path because that needs a host sync; the default codec reserve is 25 % of a row, real V4-Flash activations need about 0.3 %.
   - `SGLANG_FLASHINFER_MEGAMOE_SM120_TRANSPORT_TABLE` (default `lsa_where_reachable`) selects the peer transport.
3. **Tests** (CPU, `base-a-test-cpu`): `test_flashinfer_megamoe.py` (bucket = max over DP ranks + int64 ids, cake config / no startup tuning, swiglu limit, exact UE8M0 conversion, single resident copy of the experts), `test_server_args.py` (SM120 accept / reject cases, cuMem default, token budget), new `test_deepseek_moe_dispatch_info.py` (both real normal-forward entrypoints exercise physical expert selection without `--enable-eplb`; both fail with the pre-fix bodies, while no-dispatch and NextN controls pass); `test/manual/dsv4/test_sm120_flash.py` runs the cookbook recipe on four SM120 GPUs (sgl-eval GSM8K smoke and AIME25).
4. **Docs**: DeepSeek-V4 cookbook, new "FlashInfer MegaMoE on SM120 for prefill (Experimental)" note.

**Local CPU validation** on the rebased candidate: server-args, FlashInfer MegaMoE, EPLB and normal-forward dispatch suites: 376 passed, 1 skipped; pre-commit passed for all changed files. A cake server smoke also passed on the rebased candidate using FlashInfer source `399b6c1d`; validation against the eventual released dependency remains pending.

**Test environment** (GPU numbers below, collected before the rebase): one host, 8x NVIDIA RTX PRO 5000 Blackwell 72 GB (SM120, PCIe, two CPU sockets), driver 580.95.05; image `lmsysorg/sglang:dev-cu13` built 2026-10-13 (CUDA 13.0, torch 2.14.1+cu130, NCCL 2.30.7, nvidia-cutlass-dsl 4.8.0) with this branch on top of `27b68303d0` and FlashInfer main `399b6c1d` (#6346) from source; model `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731`; sgl-eval 0.1.2. Unless noted: `--tp 4 --attn-dp-size 4` on GPUs 0-3.

**Dependency compatibility (2026-10-16).** With the actual installed FlashInfer `0.7.1` wheel (module loaded from `site-packages`, no source override), server-args, MegaMoE adapter and expert-remapping CPU suites passed: 334 tests and 140 subtests. A separate CPU probe uses real FlashInfer imports and simulated SM120 platform facts: default/`flashinfer_mxfp4` argument processing succeeds, while explicit SM120 MegaMoE selection raises the expected missing-backend error. This probe does not claim GPU execution. The existing unit test also covers a missing cake API.

The fixed source revision was additionally installed as an editable package (`0.7.2+g399b6c1d`) in the pinned CUDA 13 image, without a `PYTHONPATH` overlay or disabled version checks. Runtime and distribution versions match, the recorded Git commit matches, and the same 334 tests / 140 subtests pass. Old cubin/JIT-cache distributions and their orphan namespace directories were removed; the source build validates its kernel manifest. This installation intentionally overrides SGLang's `0.7.1` pin (`pip check` reports that mismatch), and ordinary default-wheel CI does not exercise the new cake kernel.

The actual released-wheel GPU check also passed on 4x RTX PRO 5000 Blackwell 72 GB with DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731, TP4/attention-DP4 and `flashinfer_mxfp4`: four HTTP chat requests completed with nonempty responses, including correct answers to 17 x 23 and 48 + 24. FlashInfer autotune logs identify version `0.7.1`; the container had an empty `PYTHONPATH` and no version-check bypass. This is a functional smoke, not an accuracy benchmark.

The source-installed cake GPU smoke also passed on the same GPUs/model/parallelism, using the separately built image and a fresh JIT workspace: all four requests completed, arithmetic checks returned 391 and 72, and server logs identify `0.7.2+g399b6c1d`. The smoke exercised eager prefill plus decode CUDA Graph capture/replay; generated cake binding/device artifacts are present under that version's cache. This validates the source-install recipe without changing the previously reported accuracy/performance measurements.

## Accuracy Tests

DeepSeek-V4-Flash (0731), 4x RTX PRO 5000 Blackwell 72 GB (PCIe), `--tp 4 --attn-dp-size 4`.

**GSM8K-1319** (`sgl-eval run gsm8k --load-preset-from-model-id deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731`, sgl-eval 0.1.2: the model's preset, thinking on, temperature 1.0, top-p 0.95, max_tokens 200000, reasoning_effort=max):

| config | score | truncated | error |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--moe-runner-backend flashinfer_mxfp4` (baseline) | 96.59 % | 0 % | 0 % |
| `--moe-a2a-backend flashinfer_megamoe` (this PR) | 96.13 % | 0 % | 0 % |

**GPQA-diamond** (`sgl-eval run gpqa --from-dataset <gpqa_diamond.jsonl> --load-preset-from-model-id deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 --n-repeats 4`, sgl-eval 0.1.2, 198 questions x 4 repeats). Both arms used the model preset: temperature 1.0, top-p 0.95, max_tokens 200000, reasoning_effort=max, and `chat_template_kwargs={"thinking": true}`.

| config | pass@1 (avg of 4) | repeat-level SEM | pass@4 | majority@4 | truncated | error |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `flashinfer_mxfp4` | 90.28 % | 0.56 % | 93.94 % | 90.15 % | 0.00 % | 0.00 % |
| `flashinfer_megamoe` | 90.15 % | 0.44 % | 93.94 % | 90.66 % | 0.00 % | 0.00 % |

These results replace the earlier temperature-0 / 32k-cap run. Scores were independently recomputed from all 792 outputs per arm. The SEM is across four repeats of the same 198 questions; it is not a confidence interval over independently sampled questions or a formal equivalence test.

**AIME25** (`test/manual/dsv4/test_sm120_flash.py::TestSM120FlashFlashInferMegaMoE::test_aime25`, the fixture shared with the other DeepSeek-V4 cookbook tests: sgl-eval, 30 x 16 repeats, thinking on, temperature 1.0, top-p 1.0, `--max-tokens 65536`): pass@1 = 98.1 % (SEM 0.5 %), pass@16 = 100 %, no truncation, threshold 0.93. `test_smoke_gsm8k` of the same file passes as well.

**Static EPLB** (a recording of V4-Flash routing, `--init-expert-location <file> --ep-dispatch-algorithm static`, no `--enable-eplb`) on this PR's backend; GSM8K-200 via the deprecated `sglang.test.run_eval` (5-shot), run before upstream moved to sgl-eval:

| config | GSM8K-200 | pf1k input tok/s | ShareGPT input tok/s |
|---|---|---|---|
| this PR, no EPLB | 0.990 | 26109 | 1561 |
| this PR, recorded placement, 0 redundant experts | 0.990 | 25013 | 1507 |
| this PR, recorded placement, 32 redundant experts | 0.990 | 25633 | 1453 |
| recorded placement, 0 redundant, **without the EPLB fix** (commit 1 reverted) | 0.005 (garbled output) | 25152 | 1587 |

(The no-EPLB reference is the median of three c1 rounds; the recorded-placement rows are single c3 rounds. They demonstrate functional correctness, but are not a controlled estimate of remapping overhead.)

The same bug on the plain TP MoE path (`--moe-runner-backend flashinfer_mxfp4`, no a2a backend, `--init-expert-location <file>` only, which selects the `dynamic` dispatch algorithm): GSM8K-200 (sgl-eval preset) = 0.0 % on the base commit, 96.5 % with commit 1.

**PD-disaggregated functional check** (cake prefill server on GPUs 0-3 with `--disaggregation-mode prefill`, `flashinfer_mxfp4` decode server on GPUs 4-7, NIXL/UCX KV transfer over RoCE, `sglang_router --pd-disaggregation`): coherent smoke answers and GSM8K-200 = 0.990 (`run_eval`) in two separate runs. (In the second run one request hit the 300 s disaggregation bootstrap timeout before its prefill started.) PD throughput was not measured.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Same setup; `--chunked-prefill-size 16384 --max-prefill-tokens 4096` (4096 prefill tokens per rank), `--mem-fraction-static 0.8`, decode CUDA graphs on (prefill CUDA graphs are disabled for DeepSeek-V4 by SGLang's own rule), `sglang.benchmark.serving --dataset-name random-ids`. Prefill: a dedicated rerun on 2026-10-15 with radix cache disabled, three rounds per point, all three backends on the same production tree. Decode: the earlier c7 session on the same production tree, one round per point; GSM8K-200 (sgl-eval preset) in that session: 96.5 % / 97.0 % / 97.0 %.

**Prefill** (OSL 1, `--max-concurrency 64`, `--disable-radix-cache`), input tokens/s (TTFT mean / median / P99, ms). Both baselines run W4A8 (MXFP4 weights x MXFP8 activations, FlashInfer CUTLASS fused MoE) with the tokens all-gathered over attention DP and reduce-scattered after the MoE; `--ep-size 4` places whole experts per rank like this PR:

| ISL | flashinfer_mxfp4, TP MoE | flashinfer_mxfp4, EP4 | flashinfer_megamoe | vs TP / vs EP4 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 512 | 12125 (2669 / 2630 / 3670) | 13853 (2334 / 2279 / 3243) | 24174 (1336 / 1291 / 1982) | 1.99x / 1.75x |
| 1024 | 12332 (5126 / 5289 / 6301) | 14165 (4462 / 4603 / 5483) | 25106 (2518 / 2583 / 3121) | 2.04x / 1.77x |
| 2048 | 12101 (9861 / 10774 / 11961) | 13854 (8611 / 9411 / 10469) | 24085 (4950 / 5367 / 6086) | 1.99x / 1.74x |
| 4096 | 11935 (17502 / 21537 / 23239) | 13644 (15287 / 18821 / 20285) | 23400 (8923 / 10887 / 11918) | 1.96x / 1.72x |

In this serving configuration, EP4 improves the baseline by about 1.14-1.15x and the MegaMoE backend is 1.72-1.77x faster than that EP4 baseline (1.96-2.04x over TP MoE). This comparison measures the complete backend, including communication and integration; it does not isolate kernel fusion alone.

Each prefill round has 524288 requested input tokens (`num-prompts = 524288 / ISL`), request rate infinity, concurrency 64, temperature 0, and client seeds 101, 102 and 103; a separate cold run is excluded. The server uses `--disable-radix-cache` and each benchmark passes `--flush-cache`. All 36 measured runs completed every request without errors; all output lengths are one token. The table reports medians of three run-level metrics (including run-level P99s), not pooled request percentiles. The largest per-point throughput range `(max-min)/median` across the three rounds was 0.8% / 0.6% / 3.1% for TP / EP4 / MegaMoE respectively. The runs were sequential on one host, so these are synthetic serving measurements, not a PD throughput or kernel microbenchmark result.

Decode uses seed 42, concurrency 4/16/64/256 and 32/32/128/512 requests respectively; all measured output lengths are 1024 tokens. These earlier decode runs retained radix caching and did not explicitly flush between cases.

**Decode** (ISL 128 / OSL 1024, ignore_eos), median TPOT (ms):

| concurrency (req/rank) | flashinfer_mxfp4, TP MoE | flashinfer_mxfp4, `--ep-size 4` | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4 (1) | 15.4 | 16.0 | 21.6 |
| 16 (4) | 21.0 | 22.0 | 27.1 |
| 64 (16) | 33.4 | 33.4 | 37.0 |
| 256 (64) | 61.7 | 60.9 | 60.2 |

Hence the prefill positioning. Decode CUDA graphs capture one bucket per batch size: with `--disable-cuda-graph` the median TPOT of this PR is 65.1 / 62.6 / 62.9 ms at concurrency 4 / 16 / 64 (mxfp4: 66.3 / 65.4 / 66.6 ms).

**Topology (supplementary, historical cache-enabled runs).** The kernel picks a per-peer transport: NCCL LSA (CUDA peer access over PCIe/NVLink) where peers can reach each other and NCCL GIN (GPU-initiated RDMA over the NIC) elsewhere. `SGLANG_FLASHINFER_MEGAMOE_SM120_TRANSPORT_TABLE` selects the table. Prefill, OSL 1, `--max-concurrency 128`, input tokens/s for ISL 2048 / 4096:

| cake layout | GPUs | flashinfer_mxfp4 (TP MoE, EP=1) | this PR, `lsa_where_reachable` (default) | this PR, `all_gin` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| TP4 / attn-DP4 / EP4 | 0-3, one CPU socket | 12126 / 12130 | 24283 / 23629 (2.00x / 1.95x) | 24563 / 23967 (2.03x / 1.98x) |
| TP8 / attn-DP8 / EP8 | 0-7, two CPU sockets | 13578 / 14855 | 40690 / 42221 (3.00x / 2.84x) | 41629 / 44673 (3.07x / 3.01x) |

At EP8 the two sockets have no CUDA peer path between them, so the default table runs LSA for the 24 directed off-diagonal peer pairs inside the sockets and GIN for the 32 directed pairs across sockets (56 off-diagonal pairs in total); an all-LSA table is not possible on this host. At EP8 this PR needed `--mem-fraction-static 0.70` on these 72 GB GPUs (at 0.80 the first MegaMoE launch ran out of memory); the EP8 rows of both backends use 0.70. GSM8K-200 (`run_eval`) was 0.985-0.990 in every layout.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

title: [Refactor] kernels/diffusion/tests: Prune dead code and fix tests that never ran
body:
## Motivation

Six months of fast kernel and diffusion work left a lot behind in `python/sglang/kernels`, `python/sglang/multimodal_gen` and the kernel/diffusion test trees: kernels nothing calls, registry metadata nothing reads, per-model copies of the same fused-op glue, env knobs that do nothing, and tests that pass without testing anything. This PR removes that, and fixes the real bugs the audit turned up along the way (several were silently shipping).

**408 files, +3,629 / -26,346.** About 1.3K of the additions are test oracles and helpers moved out of production modules into `python/sglang/test/kernels/`.

## Bugs fixed (please review these first)

| Area | Problem | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| SANA (diffusion) | Since #37816 the VAE loader calls `vae.state_dict()` before `load_state_dict`; `AutoencoderDC` builds its inner diffusers model lazily, so that call built it with random init and the later load returned early. **All 375 VAE tensors were random; every SANA T2I image on main is noise.** | `load_state_dict` loads into an already-built inner model. Regression test in `test_vae_loader.py` (fails on main). |
| GLM-Image (diffusion) | #33555 added an unconditional `query[:, t:] = q_img` write-back after an in-place RoPE; torch 2.14 rejects the self-copy, so **every GLM-Image request fails** in the first DiT block. | Copy back only when the rotation returned new memory. Regression test `test_glm_image_attention.py`; `test_ar_models` re-enabled (fails on main, passes here in 175 s on 2xH200). |
| MiniMax-H3 VAE | The default-on `h3_vae_qk_rmsnorm_rope` path ran in `quality=exact` but was not bit-exact (~25% of rotated channels differ). A second, faster, quality-gated fused path for the same op already existed. | Removed the non-bit-exact path. **Behavior change:** the exact tier now runs the native chain (bit-identical to native); lossless is unchanged. |
| Diffusion CI | `STANDALONE_FILES` moved to `server/gpu_cases.py` in #24630 but the CUDA partition planner kept reading the runner, so **no CUDA standalone file has run since June** (12 2-GPU files + the 1-GPU ones). | Planner reads the case config. All 15 newly scheduled files were run on H200 through the CI code path; one rotted test fixed. |
| Env vars | Code read the legacy `SGL_*` names while docs/`environ.py` define `SGLANG_*`, and the rewrite is one-directional, so the documented names did nothing: `SGLANG_USE_DEEPGEMM_BMM` (5 models), `SGLANG_DG_USE_NVRTC`, `SGLANG_CPU_QUANTIZATION`, `SGLANG_DSA_TOPK_ROW_SPLIT`. | Read via `envs`; legacy names still work. |
| `BaseFusedOp` | `KernelBackend.FLYDSL` mapped to a missing `forward_flydsl`, so `SGLANG_FORCE_FUSED_OP_BACKEND=flydsl` raised `AttributeError`. | Stub added + test. |
| Tests that never ran | `test_fp8_kernel` returned early on every CUDA GPU with sm>=90; `test_swapab_attention` was registered on H100 but gated to sm_10x (production SM100 kernel had no CUDA coverage); sm_100 / sm_120 / 2-GPU / 4-GPU diffusion unit tests sat on a 1-GPU H100 lane; `test_qwen_image21` cache tests exercised a test-local re-implementation of the fix. | Each now runs on hardware that satisfies its gate (or was deleted with its dead kernel); the qwen_image21 tests drive the real block and fail when the fix is reverted. |
| SenseNova-U1 | `FlowMatchingHead` called `SimpleMLPAdaLN` with a signature the class doesn't have (crash for `fm_head_layers > 2`). | Restored the timestep-conditioned head; test fails on main. |

## Modifications

### Kernels (`python/sglang/kernels`, -13.8K)
- **Dead / test-only kernels removed** (each re-verified with whole-repo grep incl. string lookups): seg_la kernel, dsv4 `fused_ape_pool_norm_rope`, tilelang `fp8_index`, KDA prefill timing scaffolding, nvlink push/pull all-reduce wrappers, inkling two-shot all-reduce, `cutedsl_gdn_mtp_ring` T=1 entry, non-`f_b` FlyDSL KDA decode, dsa `GetK/GetS`, adler32 whole-tensor entry points, ReplaySSM circular commit, cvt helpers, mxfp8 v-cache update, fp8 ue8m0/hopper/transpose helpers, `w8a8_block_fp8_matmul`, `awq_gemm_triton`, rocm `tkw1`, `moe_fused_gate_jit`, inkling gate v1, `post_reorder_triton_kernel`, `fused_inplace_qknorm_across_heads`, elementwise `silu_and_mul_triton`/autotune path, `rms_normalize_triton`, stale `top_p_renorm_triton` copy, and others.
- **Legacy DSV4 compressor path removed** (`compress_old.py`, `fused_compress_triton.py`, srt `dsv4/compress_hip.py`, the old `CompressorBackendMixin`): every CUDA/HIP backend uses `compressor_v2`; `fused_norm_rope_inplace` (live) moved to `dsv4/elementwise.py`. AOT dsv4 q/k norm+RoPE ops (duplicates of the JIT ones) removed.
- **Registry (option A):** the KernelSpec inventory stays; write-only metadata goes (`FormatSignature`, `KernelSpec.format_signature/description/group/name`, `BaseFusedOp.format_signature/descriptions/dispatch_forward`, unused selector/platform helpers). `spec.CUDA_ONLY` replaces ~44 inline frozensets. Unused `BaseFusedOp`s (4 RMSNorm, Gelu/GeluTanh/ReLU2/QuickGELU) removed; facade wrappers nobody imports removed (this also fixes facade functions shadowed by same-named submodules). `Fp8ScaledMMOp` no longer declares an SM90 heuristic as a capability.
- **#42184 criteria applied** to the four remaining gate sites (route-quant, engram, vision_rope, minimax_m3): gates check eligibility, launchers enforce contracts.
- **Duplicates:** sparse-MLA decode reuses the shared kernels (bit-exact, 720 cases x 2 archs incl. fully masked rows); mxfp8 gfx95 reuses `mxfp8_quant`. Forks that are *not* bit-exact stay, each with a one-line comment (grok RMSNorm, gfx1250 qk-RMSNorm, int8 group quant on ROCm, marlin SiTU, minimax Gemma RMSNorm).
- **Test oracles shipped in op modules moved to `sglang.test.kernels`** (LPLB, dsa transform index, DCP LSE combine, dsv4 K-cache quant refs, extend attention, dspark window, multigpu launcher, mhc, per-token-group quant dispatch).

### Diffusion (`python/sglang/multimodal_gen`, -9.4K)
- **Dead code:** SenseNova-U1 unreachable chat/interleave/it2i paths (~2.6K; T2I output byte-identical), auto-residency estimators and the warmup stage-iteration calibration chain nothing read, SANA-WM parity debug harness (`SANAWM_*` env hooks incl. `torch.load` input injection), `MINIMAX_H3_USE_FUSED_NORM` path, unresolved MiniMax-H3 euler scheduler, registry subprocess-inspect path (pointed at a nonexistent module), delta-gzip realtime encoding (server + web UI), bundled-overlay lookup, `EncodingStage`, bitsandbytes 4-bit swap, `generate_with_lora` (could never run), `convert_hf_to_fp8.py`, unused platform hooks, unread `ServerArgs` fields, etc.
- **Env:** 12 `envs.py` entries nothing read removed (+ the docs rows presenting 5 of them as working knobs); raw reads of `SGLANG_ENABLE_FUSED_QKNORM_ROPE` / `MINIMAX_H3_VAE_*` declared in `envs.py` with identical parsing; unprefixed GDN dev knobs dropped.
- **Refactors (bit-exact):** `BitExactFusionGate.run()` replaces 24 hand-written verify-once/fallback blocks and the `mismatch_msg` boilerplate; one LayerNorm+modulate helper for FLUX.3/GLM/LongCat; `sites/` exports one `QualityGatedFusion` per family instead of four wrappers each (~50 facade entries, 28 imports gone). Sites that are hand-tuned for launch overhead, re-raise, verify inside the try, or differ in reference were left as they are (listed in the commit messages).

### Tests and CI
- Deleted always-skipped tests (env var set nowhere, `skipif(True)`, hard-coded dev paths), tautologies (default/literal echoes, `inspect.getsource` shape tests, log-format echoes, torch-behavior tests), duplicate cases and duplicate helpers; trimmed grids with no extra coverage (`fused_fp8_qkv_kv_cache` 1,344 -> 288 cases, AOT `moe_align` 4,368 -> 144, AOT per-token-group quant 3,632 -> 320). CI-tooling meta-tests are intentionally kept.
- New lane wiring: swapab on B200; Blackwell, SM120 and 4-GPU diffusion unit steps; 2-GPU diffusion unit files as 2-gpu standalone files; `quant-videogen` installed for its tests; comm benches no longer register no-op AMD runs; HPC-Ops tests (always skipped: the package isn't in the CI venv) disabled explicitly.
- **CI cost:** the standalone-file fix adds runners (1-GPU H100: 5 -> 6 partitions; 2-GPU: 3 -> 5 by current estimates). The estimates are 2-15x above the measured H200 times; I'll copy this PR's CI-measured values into `STANDALONE_FILE_EST_TIMES` before merge.

## Accuracy Tests

End-to-end, same GPU, fixed seed, base vs this branch (fused paths confirmed active by a gate tracer on both sides; no gate disabled):

| Model | Paths exercised | Result |
|---|---|---|
| ERNIE-Image, LongCat-Image, FLUX.2-klein-4B, Joy, MOSS-Image, Anima, Qwen-Image, Wan2.1-1.3B, Helios-Distilled | `BitExactFusionGate.run`, LN+modulate helper, QK-norm+RoPE, handler-table sites, gated residual | byte-identical |
| GLM-Image (1024², 30 steps) | LN+modulate helper, QK-LN | identical to main+fix; fused == native |
| SANA 600M (512², 20 steps) | VAE fix | identical to main+fix; reproducible across processes (main is noise) |
| SenseNova-U1.5-8B-MoT T2I | dead-path removal | PNG md5 identical |
| Z-Image-Turbo server warmup | residency/warmup cleanup | PNG identical, same peak memory |
| MiniMax-H3 VAE decoder | lossless in-place path / exact tier | lossless identical; exact == native |

Kernel dedups were checked bit-for-bit on H200 and GB300 (scripts in the commit messages' descriptions).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No perf-path changes intended. `BitExactFusionGate.run` was not applied to the launch-overhead-tuned sites (the closures add ~160-180 ns per call on the host).

## Validation

- **H200 (sm_90):** every file under `test/registered/kernels/ops`, `test/registered/unit` and `multimodal_gen/test/unit` (1,624 files). Failures were re-run on main: identical failing test ids (rust extensions not built in the source tree, NPU-only, multi-GPU tests on one GPU, pre-existing diffusion kernel failures); 2 port collisions from parallel runs pass alone. 
- **GB300 (sm_103):** every file under `test/registered/kernels/ops` (334 files): failing ids identical to main.
- **RTX PRO 6000 (sm_120):** FA4 sm120 + FA4 + dense FA4 + sm120 paged MQA logits + sm120 fp8 linear + mxfp4 sm120 + diffusion fp8 FA sm120 + kernel namespace: all pass, same as main.
- **Multi-GPU:** every CUDA diffusion standalone file run on 2xH200 through the CI runner path (incl. `test_ar_models` and `test_diffusion_bcg_tp2_zimage_turbo` at the final head); Kandinsky 6 4-GPU cases on 4xH200.
- `pytest --collect-only` over the test trees: no new collection errors; import walk over `sglang.kernels`, `sglang.multimodal_gen`, `sglang.srt.{layers,models,...}`: no new import failures.
- **Not validated:** ROCm, NPU, XPU, MUSA (HIP-only deletions are traced through backend selection and import-checked on CUDA), a full AOT wheel link (affected TUs compiled for sm90/sm100), 4-GPU cases on Blackwell.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

title: feat(jit): support native MUSA compilation
body:
## Overview

This PR adds native MUSA compilation to SGLang's Ninja-based JIT build path.
The MUSA branch selects `mcc`, passes `-x musa` and
`--offload-arch=mp_*`, and uses MUSA include paths and runtime libraries.
HIP retains precedence, and CUDA remains the fallback.

MUSA JIT uses C++20, aligned with the LLVM20-based mtcc20x path. CUDA and HIP
retain C++20. Shared JIT headers use the upstream C++20 facilities directly;
SGLang no longer carries a duplicate C++17 compatibility layer. The JIT cache
fingerprints the selected compiler path and version.

Runtime and FP8 aliases are supplied by TorchADA through
`stable_compat_include_dir()`. This path depends on
[yingzhou-bjtu/torchada#4](https://github.com/MooreThreads/torchada/pull/132),
currently a fork Draft. A TorchADA release containing that change is required
before this PR can be merged.

[sgl-project/sglang-omni#2442](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-omni/pull/2442)
is the downstream consumer integration: it exposes the existing joint-RoPE
provider on MUSA. JIT compilation remains in SGLang.

Part of #16565.

## Validation

Recorded real mtcc20x evidence: MTT S5000, LLVM20-based `mcc` (clang 20.1.8),
`--offload-arch=mp_31`; 5.3 GA `mcc3` and M1000 were not verified.

- Static checks pass in the current worktree; the recorded mtcc20x focused cache run passed `67 tests` before this C++20-only cleanup.
- The current source selects `mcc`, `-x musa`, `--offload-arch=mp_31`,
  `-DUSE_MUSA`, and `-std=c++20` for MUSA JIT; the recorded mtcc20x run
  confirmed matching host/device standard flags.
- Recorded mtcc20x evidence: `fused_rope` real MUSA JIT build, module load,
  and numerical smoke passed; `q_max_abs_error=0.0`, `k_max_abs_error=0.0`.
- Recorded mtcc20x evidence: `speculative_tree` and `ngram_embedding` real
  MUSA JIT build and module load passed.
- `speculative_sampling`: dependency-blocked because
  `flashinfer/sampling.cuh` is absent from the validation image.

### C++ standard decision

The recorded LLVM20-based mtcc20x probe passed the public-header closure in
C++20 (`bits.h`, `utils.h`, `tensor.h`, `type.cuh`, and `utils.cuh`). The MUSA
JIT path therefore uses C++20 directly, matching the CUDA/HIP upstream model.
The legacy clang14 path and M1000 remain explicit follow-up evidence items;
this PR does not claim they were freshly verified.

## MUSA JIT Build Overview

The production inventory below is generated from every `load_jit` call site
under `python/sglang/kernels/ops/**/*.py`: 194 call sites and 165 unique source
selections. Build, load, runtime smoke, dependency, and backend-specific
states are kept separate.

### Focused real-module results

| Operator / module | Source | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `fused_rope` | `csrc/elementwise/rope.cuh` | `PASS_BUILD_LOAD_SMOKE`; numerical smoke passed |

title: [Perf] [NPU] deepep: enable MXFP8 low-latency dispatch for Fp8MoEMethod FP4 experts
body:
## Motivation

On NPU, FP4-expert models routed through Fp8MoEMethod ( is_fp4_expert=True , e.g. MiMo-V2.5-Pro with modelopt_fp4) delegate execution to NPUW4A8MXFP4MoEMethod kernels via the ASCEND MoE runner. However, process_weights_after_loading only runs Fp8MoEMethod 's own body, so the DeepEP dispatcher quant config was never set — dispatch fell back to BF16 and a separate DynamicMxQuant kernel ran before every grouped matmul (~15ms/layer at 16K-token prefill).

The native FP4 path ( NPUW4A8MXFP4FusedMoEMethod , DSV4) already sets the same dispatcher config; the Fp8MoEMethod path was simply missing it.

## Modifications

- Declare the dispatch wire format as a DISPATCHER_QUANT_CONFIG class attribute on NPUW4A8MXFP4MoEMethod ( low_latency=mxfp8 ; normal stays BF16 since A5 MXFP8 normal dispatch is intranode-only). The kernel that consumes the activations now owns the declaration, instead of each caller hand-writing platform-specific if/else patches.
- In Fp8MoEMethod.process_weights_after_loading , pick the config up from the attached layer.w13_kernel when it declares one; otherwise keep the original checkpoint-dtype config. No _is_npu / is_fp4_expert branching — the attached kernel already encodes both.
- Reuse the same declaration in NPUW4A8MXFP4FusedMoEMethod , replacing its hand-written copy.
With this, A5 low-latency dispatch quantizes activations to MXFP8 in-kernel (with E8M0 block scales) and the GMMs consume them directly; the three previously duplicated config dicts collapse into a single kernel-owned declaration.

## Accuracy Tests

```
echo performance | tee /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu*/cpufreq/scaling_governor
sysctl -w vm.swappiness=0
sysctl -w kernel.numa_balancing=0
sysctl -w kernel.sched_migration_cost_ns=50000
export SGLANG_SET_CPU_AFFINITY=1

source /usr/local/Ascend/ascend-toolkit/set_env.sh
source /usr/local/Ascend/nnal/atb/set_env.sh

export HCCL_BUFFSIZE=300
export HCCL_OP_EXPANSION_MODE=AIV
export PYTORCH_NPU_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True
export STREAMS_PER_DEVICE=32
export SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_BOOTSTRAP_TIMEOUT=600
export SGLANG_ENABLE_SPEC_V2=1
export SGLANG_ENABLE_OVERLAP_PLAN_STREAM=1
export ASCEND_USE_FIA=1
export SGLANG_DEEPEP_NUM_MAX_DISPATCH_TOKENS_PER_RANK=32
export DEEPEP_HCCL_BUFFSIZE=2500
export DEEPEP_NORMAL_LONG_SEQ_ROUND=20
export DEEPEP_NORMAL_LONG_SEQ_PER_ROUND_TOKENS=4096
export HCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME=lo
export GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME=lo
export HCCL_HOST_SOCKET_PORT_RANGE=auto
export SGLANG_ALLOW_OVERWRITE_LONGER_CONTEXT_LEN=1

sglang serve \
        --model-path $MODEL_PATH \
        --served-model-name $MODEL_PATH \
        --trust-remote-code \
        --attention-backend ascend \
        --device npu \
        --mem-fraction-static 0.92 \
        --tp-size 8 --nnodes 1 --node-rank 0 \
        --chunked-prefill-size 8192 --max-total-tokens 600000 \
        --max-running-requests 32 \
        --moe-a2a-backend deepep --deepep-mode auto \
        --cuda-graph-bs-decode 1 2 4 8 16 \
        --speculative-algorithm DFLASH \
        --speculative-draft-model-path $DFLASH_PATH \
        --speculative-num-draft-tokens 8 \
        --dp-size 2 --enable-dp-attention --enable-dp-lm-head \
```

## Speed Tests and Profiling

MiMo-V2.5-Pro-FP4 (DFlash), single-node A5, DeepEP low-latency, prefill with 16K-token random inputs.

Per-layer kernel profile (avg ms, before → after):

| Kernel | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| DynamicMxQuant (post-dispatch) | 15.14 | **eliminated** |
| MoeLowLatencyDispatchV2 | 33.16 | 30.63 |
| GroupedMatmulSwigluQuantV2 | 30.37 | 27.60 |
| Layer total | 238.6 | 222.7 (**-6.7%**) |

|---|---|---|

| P99 TTFT (ms) | 18856 | 16405 |

title: GPU-Initiated Communication: Dissecting Down to the Bone
body:
GPU-initiated communication lets GPU threads post RDMA operations directly to the NIC. It underpins NVSHMEM, NCCL GIN, and DeepEP, which serve the fine-grained, latency-critical communication of Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models, yet its performance characteristics and optimizations remain scarcely documented beyond source code, and library comparisons fail to separate the costs of the hardware mechanism from those of the library around it.
  This paper dissects GPU-initiated communication at the GPU-NIC boundary. We first detail the GPU-side network path: queue placement, work-request construction, doorbell ordering, and completion semantics. We then introduce mini-gda and mini-proxy, minimal transports for the GPU and CPU-proxy submission paths, and measure them alongside NVSHMEM IBGDA, NCCL GIN, DeepEP, UCCL-EP, MSCCL++, and fabric-lib on NVIDIA H100, H200, B200, and GB200 platforms. A minimal GPU path issues an operation in 0.7 μs and completes in 4.0 μs; libraries add up to 4.6 μs of issue time through queue management, memory ordering, and completion scope, and issue time scales with the SM clock. A tuned CPU proxy matches or beats the GPU path at idle, at the cost of a dedicated core whose operating state sets its latency and throughput. On either path, sharing a queue with bulk traffic raises latency by one to three orders of magnitude. Reaching the 260 M msg/s ceiling of our InfiniBand platform requires doorbell batching and queue parallelism, and both have resource costs: communication code can reduce GPU block residency even when unused, and all-to-all traffic loses 59% of its NIC message rate at about 3,000 active connections. The submission path alone therefore does not predict communication performance. Our experiment code and results are available at https://github.com/ParCoreLab/Dissecting-GPU-Communication-Experiments.

title:
FastSwitch: Optimizing Context Switching Efficiency in Fairness-aware
  Large Language Model Serving
body:
Serving numerous users and requests concurrently requires good fairness in
Large Language Models (LLMs) serving system. This ensures that, at the same
cost, the system can meet the Service Level Objectives (SLOs) of more users ,
such as time to first token (TTFT) and time between tokens (TBT), rather than
allowing a few users to experience performance far exceeding the SLOs. To
achieve better fairness, the preemption-based scheduling policy dynamically
adjusts the priority of each request to maintain balance during runtime.
However, existing systems tend to overly prioritize throughput, overlooking the
overhead caused by preemption-induced context switching, which is crucial for
maintaining fairness through priority adjustments. In this work, we identify
three main challenges that result in this overhead. 1) Inadequate I/O
utilization. 2) GPU idleness. 3) Unnecessary I/O transmission during multi-turn
conversations. Our key insight is that the block-based KV cache memory policy
in existing systems, while achieving near-zero memory waste, leads to
discontinuity and insufficient granularity in the KV cache memory. To respond,
we introduce FastSwitch, a fairness-aware serving system that not only aligns
with existing KV cache memory allocation policy but also mitigates context
switching overhead. Our evaluation shows that FastSwitch outperforms the
state-of-the-art LLM serving system vLLM with speedups of 1.4-11.2x across
different tail TTFT and TBT.

title: The Serialized Bridge: Understanding and Recovering LLM Serving Performance under Blackwell GPU Confidential Computing
body:
GPU Confidential Computing (GPU-CC) now preserves GPU-local performance: on NVIDIA B300, BF16 matmul runs at 0.998x of non-confidential performance. Yet LLM serving under Intel TDX plus GPU-CC still loses 13-27% of throughput, and KV-cache restore latency can more than double. This paper studies that gap on two Blackwell platforms, RTX Pro 6000 and B300 HGX, and identifies its dominant cause: the confidential VM-GPU bridge, not GPU compute.
  We find that GPU-CC turns host/device movement into a serialized, high-setup-cost channel. Secure copies do not gain CUDA-stream concurrency within a context, asynchronous transfers block at the runtime boundary, and small crossings pay a fixed toll. This violates the assumptions of modern inference runtimes, where DMA is expected to be cheap, concurrent, and asynchronous. In vLLM dense decode, the gap closes around 44x-slower small alloc-and-copy operations; targeted patches reject alternative explanations. A scheduling flag recovers 57% of the gap, while a worker-thread drain recovers up to 92% in qualified high-concurrency runs. The same bridge model explains a +131% KV-restore penalty and a 34x model-load slowdown.
  Blackwell also changes the confidential tenancy unit. We qualify confidential multi-GPU NVSwitch tenants on B300, including 510 GB/s NVLink P2P inside a CVM and concurrent isolated tenants, and identify the remaining fabric-attestation gap for production confidential AI platforms.
